chapters.title: Chapter 1460: The Tenth Floor - The Planet Devourer (2)
paragraphs: The deeper Zareth and his team head into the planet, the more dangerous it gets, prompting them to understand just how important this mission is.
Everything is unstable to the point that just a slight distortion can cause the space around them to crack.
Thankfully, Ingrid and Elyndra are experts at using the Void and space magic. So slowly, they made their way toward the core of the planet, which happened to be located at the very center.
After 2 hours of flying, they came to a stop in front of a vast sea of water so dark and mysterious that none of them could see an inch beneath the outer layer, no matter how hard they tried.
"This doesn’t inspire confidence," Elyndra said, gazing at the dark water that stood still, almost as if it were being held in place by something.
"I can sense Necrotic Qi emanating from deep within this water," Zareth also said, and Elyndra nodded. As the only undead in the team, only they could sense the Necrotic Qi.
But that didn’t put a smile on their faces. If anything, sensing that the water had the same energy that all undead use made them frown.
"This is not going to be an easy mission," he muttered before taking flight again. The mission remains the same.
"Why did you say that?" Ingrid asked, flying after him.
"Probably nothing. But the fact that the core of the planet is located here and that this water contains a large amount of Necrotic Qi makes me wonder if our opponent is also undead.
If that is the case, we can forget about beating it. There is just no way we can kill it if it can harness or, more accurately, devour the Necrotic Qi.
But as I said, it is probably nothing."
"Maybe you are right," Enkay, one of Uncle Drew’s Night Agents, said, flying alongside everyone. "Maybe this Necrotic Qi came about due to the planet’s core dying."

They decided to go with Enkay’s suggestion. That makes more sense. From the description of the mission, they know the core is dying, so maybe the water is being affected by the death Qi coming from it.

But even if they are going after an undead, the mere fact that Vexthra added Enkay to the mix meant that, regardless of how dangerous their opponent is, with the hell flame at his disposal, the mission will be completed with just a single death.
The hell flame has a property that makes it lethal even to undead beings.
It took a couple of hours, but they finally reached the core.

The moment they came within viewing distance of the core, they all stopped. That was because right at that moment, their opponent came into sight, and just a single glance made them all get goosebumps.
"What is that?" Ingrid couldn’t help but ask.
The monster they had to defeat is an abomination on a scale beyond imagination.
It is a very large, round monster with jagged, rotting skin filled with countless eyes. On one side of it, a large maw lined with teeth could be seen, menacing in every way.
But that isn’t even the scariest part. Extending from its body are dozens of tendrils, each ending with deadly razor-sharp spikes.
It is scary beyond measure, and that can be seen from their expressions. They are terrified, and that is perfectly normal. Anyone would be terrified.
"We have no choice but to battle and kill it. So, how about we come up with a battle strategy before it notices us?"
"Well, I think it did," Elyndra said, pointing at the abomination. Turning around, they all saw it had long seen them and was looking at them with hundreds of tiny eyes.
"I feel like calling it Vorath kind of humanizes it," Ingrid said before spinning her spear around. The battle will happen no matter how scared they are.

"Let’s focus more on killing it rather than wondering why it has a name," Zareth said before turning toward Enkay. "You and I will face it head-on and try not to get stabbed through by those pointy things.

Elyndra will use her affinity for space to help with movement, while Ingrid uses the void to create openings for us. As for Veydris, your job is to create a blind spot for us. So blind as many eyes as you can in one section of its body."
They nodded, while Veydris merely vanished into the void. He can’t speak, but he understood the assignment, so he got right on it.
Also, with him having a metallic body, there is no way he would be affected by the void, which was growing increasingly unstable by the second.
Elyndra retrieved a staff, and Enkay pulled out a scythe. Since things had gotten to this point, using his daggers wouldn’t help him or anyone.
"All right, let’s move out," Zareth said, taking to the sky. Since he is the only one with devourer abilities, he unleashed his strongest move from the start.
A large serpent appeared, and he jumped on its head, speeding toward Vorath, who sensed them long before they moved.
The massive serpent roared as it tore through the unstable space, its colossal body coiling and uncoiling with terrifying speed.
The black scales of the snake shimmered with a faint violet glow, and fragments of distorted space shattered in its wake. To win, he needed the first advantage, so every second counted.
Zareth stood firmly on its head, his curved spear absorbing so much devouring Qi while his eyes locked onto the abomination before him.
Vorath did not remain idle.
The countless eyes covering its bloated body snapped open all at once.
Then a low, guttural vibration spread across the sea of dark water, and the tendrils extending from its body twitched violently before shooting outward like harpoons.
They were directed at Enkay and Zareth.
"Incoming!" Elyndra shouted, alerting everyone before she waved her staff.
Space folded instantly.
The area around Zareth and Enkay twisted, and several of the incoming tendrils pierced nothing but warped air.
Still, not all were avoided. One spike grazed the serpent’s body, tearing away scales and releasing a burst of dark energy.
Zareth’s expression hardened in that instant, a very bad feeling creeping in.
He sensed right away that the abomination was not an easy target. Just a single attack gave the creeps.
He knew something had to happen, and thankfully, he had the perfect person for it.
"Ingrid," he called out, knowing Ingrid had what it takes to change the scene.
The void responded.
A surge of pure void energy erupted beneath Vorath, swallowing several tendrils and snapping them off entirely.
The severed ends wriggled violently before dissolving into black mist. Ingrid shot forward and vanished into the void immediately.
At the same time, Enkay used a movement technique to close the gap between him and Vorath. Its many eyes glared at him, releasing waves of pressure that slammed into his head.
The attack made him lose his sight for a moment.
The momentary loss of sight gave Vorath the opening to attack. A tendril moved forward, aiming for his chest. However, it reached nowhere since Elyndra used space magic to move Enkay farther back.
Zareth seized the moment to attack. The serpent opened its mouth, and from within, a dark beam shot forward, slamming into Vorath’s darkened skin.
The force pushed it back, but before it could stabilize itself, the void opened, and Veydris appeared, his metallic body and long, jagged sword humming with energy.
He struck his sword forward once, but hundreds of arcs appeared, the majority of them cutting into the many eyes on its body.
But things didn’t end there. Ingrid, who vanished into the void, appeared, her spear thrusting toward a cluster of eyes Veydris had just blinded.
Since Veydris created the opening, taking advantage of it seems like the most logical thing to do.
However, she was forced to come to a halt when two tendrils coming from two different directions closed in on her, their deadly spikes aiming for her head and stomach.
"Watch out..."

sentences.text: The deeper Zareth and his team head into the planet, the more dangerous it gets, prompting them to understand just how important this mission is.
Everything is unstable to the point that just a slight distortion can cause the space around them to crack.
Thankfully, Ingrid and Elyndra are experts at using the Void and space magic.
So slowly, they made their way toward the core of the planet, which happened to be located at the very center.
After 2 hours of flying, they came to a stop in front of a vast sea of water so dark and mysterious that none of them could see an inch beneath the outer layer, no matter how hard they tried.
"This doesn’t inspire confidence," Elyndra said, gazing at the dark water that stood still, almost as if it were being held in place by something.
"I can sense Necrotic Qi emanating from deep within this water," Zareth also said, and Elyndra nodded.
As the only undead in the team, only they could sense the Necrotic Qi.
But that didn’t put a smile on their faces.
If anything, sensing that the water had the same energy that all undead use made them frown.
"This is not going to be an easy mission," he muttered before taking flight again.
The mission remains the same.
"Why did you say that?" Ingrid asked, flying after him.
"Probably nothing.
But the fact that the core of the planet is located here and that this water contains a large amount of Necrotic Qi makes me wonder if our opponent is also undead.
If that is the case, we can forget about beating it.
There is just no way we can kill it if it can harness or, more accurately, devour the Necrotic Qi.
But as I said, it is probably nothing."
"Maybe you are right," Enkay, one of Uncle Drew’s Night Agents, said, flying alongside everyone.
"Maybe this Necrotic Qi came about due to the planet’s core dying."
They decided to go with Enkay’s suggestion.
That makes more sense.
From the description of the mission, they know the core is dying, so maybe the water is being affected by the death Qi coming from it.

But even if they are going after an undead, the mere fact that Vexthra added Enkay to the mix meant that, regardless of how dangerous their opponent is, with the hell flame at his disposal, the mission will be completed with just a single death.
The hell flame has a property that makes it lethal even to undead beings.
It took a couple of hours, but they finally reached the core.
The moment they came within viewing distance of the core, they all stopped.
That was because right at that moment, their opponent came into sight, and just a single glance made them all get goosebumps.
"What is that?" Ingrid couldn’t help but ask.
The monster they had to defeat is an abomination on a scale beyond imagination.
It is a very large, round monster with jagged, rotting skin filled with countless eyes.
On one side of it, a large maw lined with teeth could be seen, menacing in every way.
But that isn’t even the scariest part.
Extending from its body are dozens of tendrils, each ending with deadly razor-sharp spikes.
It is scary beyond measure, and that can be seen from their expressions.
They are terrified, and that is perfectly normal.
Anyone would be terrified.
"We have no choice but to battle and kill it.
So, how about we come up with a battle strategy before it notices us?"
"Well, I think it did," Elyndra said, pointing at the abomination.
Turning around, they all saw it had long seen them and was looking at them with hundreds of tiny eyes.
"I feel like calling it Vorath kind of humanizes it," Ingrid said before spinning her spear around.
The battle will happen no matter how scared they are.
"Let’s focus more on killing it rather than wondering why it has a name," Zareth said before turning toward Enkay.
"You and I will face it head-on and try not to get stabbed through by those pointy things.
Elyndra will use her affinity for space to help with movement, while Ingrid uses the void to create openings for us.
As for Veydris, your job is to create a blind spot for us.
So blind as many eyes as you can in one section of its body."
They nodded, while Veydris merely vanished into the void.
He can’t speak, but he understood the assignment, so he got right on it.
Also, with him having a metallic body, there is no way he would be affected by the void, which was growing increasingly unstable by the second.
Elyndra retrieved a staff, and Enkay pulled out a scythe.
Since things had gotten to this point, using his daggers wouldn’t help him or anyone.
"All right, let’s move out," Zareth said, taking to the sky.
Since he is the only one with devourer abilities, he unleashed his strongest move from the start.
A large serpent appeared, and he jumped on its head, speeding toward Vorath, who sensed them long before they moved.
The massive serpent roared as it tore through the unstable space, its colossal body coiling and uncoiling with terrifying speed.
The black scales of the snake shimmered with a faint violet glow, and fragments of distorted space shattered in its wake.
To win, he needed the first advantage, so every second counted.
Zareth stood firmly on its head, his curved spear absorbing so much devouring Qi while his eyes locked onto the abomination before him.
Vorath did not remain idle.
The countless eyes covering its bloated body snapped open all at once.
Then a low, guttural vibration spread across the sea of dark water, and the tendrils extending from its body twitched violently before shooting outward like harpoons.
They were directed at Enkay and Zareth.
"Incoming!" Elyndra shouted, alerting everyone before she waved her staff.
Space folded instantly.
The area around Zareth and Enkay twisted, and several of the incoming tendrils pierced nothing but warped air.
Still, not all were avoided.
One spike grazed the serpent’s body, tearing away scales and releasing a burst of dark energy.
Zareth’s expression hardened in that instant, a very bad feeling creeping in.

But things didn’t end there.
Ingrid, who vanished into the void, appeared, her spear thrusting toward a cluster of eyes Veydris had just blinded.

chapters.title: Chapter 1461: The Tenth Floor - The Planet Devourer (3)
paragraphs: Ingrid came this close to being turned into a skewer; however, before the tendrils could pierce through her, space fractured.
Elyndra’s staff pulsed with a silver glow, and the area around Ingrid twisted violently. She was rather quick with her attacks, almost as if she saw it coming long before it happened.
Thanks to her, the two spikes that were meant to skewer Ingrid’s head and stomach phased past her by mere inches, tearing through warped space instead of flesh.
Ingrid used that split second to spin her spear, slicing one tendril clean in half.
She came close to death, but even in that gray moment, she found an opening and went for it. It appears Kent isn’t the only risk taker in the family.
Black ichor sprayed outward, hissing as it touched the unstable void. With how fierce the battle had become, the void was basically leaking.
The second tendril recoiled, but Ingrid did not retreat. She stepped forward instead, her void energy expanding even further.
With the kind of energy now leaking on the battlefield, she felt like a fish in water.
Her spear thrust forward with terrifying precision, piercing directly into the cluster of blinded eyes that Veydris had carved open.
A shrill, mind-piercing screech erupted from Vorath’s massive body, spreading out like a shockwave.
As the sound spread out, Zareth and his team felt a sense of dizziness, almost as if the mere sound contained some form of mental attack.
Zareth had already felt it once, so the second time made him frown deeply. However, before he could deduce anything, something else started to happen.
The sea of dark water below began to churn violently.
Zareth and everyone felt it immediately.
The creature was about to unleash a powerful attack, one that made their backs break into a cold sweat.
The countless remaining eyes shifted, each focusing strategically on the five bugs attacking it. The pressure in the void thickened, and cracks spiderwebbed outward from Vorath’s bloated form.
"Move back," Zareth roared, directing his command to Ingrid.
At the moment, only Ingrid was within range where Vorath’s attack would prove fatal. Also, the eyes on its colossal body seem to focus more on her.
Zareth knew he had to act since she wouldn’t be able to escape easily this time.

A pulse of devouring Qi erupted from his serpent, swallowing the corrosive energy gathering around Ingrid. At the same time, Enkay, who also sensed the danger, raised his scythe high, dark flames igniting along its curved blade.
Unlike how Uncle Drew harnesses green hellflame, Enkay’s was crimson and black.
"Hellfire Bloom."
The crimson-black flames twisted unnaturally, burning like fuel had been added to them. He swung downward, and a crescent of hellfire shot forward, carving across Vorath’s rotting skin.
Where the flames touched, the flesh did not regenerate—it charred and withered.
It was a bit strange, but it worked.
Vorath convulsed.
Several tendrils lashed wildly in retaliation, smashing into the sea beneath and sending massive waves of necrotic water into the air.
However, as the water shot up into the air, the droplets did not fall like normal liquid should. Instead, they floated, each drop containing dense, concentrated Necrotic Qi.
As they condensed, Elyndra sensed the danger immediately. It took her a moment to make sense of what was happening.
Her eyes widened as the realization finally clicked. "Don’t let that touch you."
She slammed her staff down, creating layered space barriers that redirected the floating droplets away from the team.
Still, as if my design, one drop slipped through and struck the serpent’s tail. The scales blackened instantly, decay spreading like a disease.
Zareth gritted his teeth and pressed his palm forward. Although his serpent is merely a construct, if it were to be corrupted, he would also be affected, even worse, injured deep in the soul.
So he had to prevent that from happening.
Devouring Qi surged, consuming the corruption before it could spread further.
But in that moment of distraction, Vorath changed tactics.

Under normal circumstances, once one gets the upper hand to deal some dire damage, just like how Zareth was affected by the necrotic water, the most logical move is to attack and deal more heavy damage.
However, Vorath didn’t do that. Instead, it adopted an unconventional method, one that Zareth and his team never expected.
Vorath’s bloated body suddenly stilled.
For a brief second, the battlefield fell into an eerie silence.
The floating droplets of necrotic water froze midair, the fractured void stopped trembling, and even the sea beneath ceased its violent churning.
That unnatural stillness made Zareth’s heart sink.
"Something bad is about to happen."
From the start of the battle, he could sense this bone-chilling danger that, regardless of how he looked at it, he just couldn’t place his finger on where it was coming from.
Now, he seemed to have finally sensed exactly where the danger was coming from. But before he could make a move to mitigate it, something changed.
Every remaining eye that Veydris hadn’t blinded rotated at once.
They did not look at Ingrid. They did not look at Enkay. They locked onto him.
At the same time, a deep, resonant hum spread outward, vibrating through bone and soul alike.
The tendrils that had been flailing wildly retracted toward Vorath’s body, coiling tightly around it like a grotesque shield.

Then, in an eerie manner, the countless eyes began glowing with a sickly green-black light. Right when they started to glow, the unstable void around Zareth thickened, as if gravity itself had multiplied.
"Heads up," Elyndra shouted, slamming her staff down again, harnessing her space abilities.
Space bent around Zareth, but this time the distortion resisted her. Just when her space magic took effect, the space around her attack became corrupted, canceling out her space distortion ability.
"Oh no," she panicked.
Ingrid, who could come to Zareth’s aid, was also locked in a formation created by the corrupted necrotic water.
Even if she could break the formation, it would be too late to do anything for him.
On the other hand, Enkay, who could do something, was also blocked by a tendril that looked darker than the others. His scythe bounced off it when he tried severing it.
That was a clear indication that he could not aid his pal.
As for Veydris, nobody knew what he would do since his mission was to make sure the bastard was blinded and, if possible, killed.
His mission details are clear as crystal.
From where he stood, the moment Zareth found himself surrounded and with nowhere to go, Vorath would also become vulnerable, creating the perfect opening for him to go for the kill.
Of course, a normal person would prioritize Zareth’s safety.
However, Veydris is a battle doll. In his perfect analysis, he sees Zareth as an undead who just could not die even if he wanted to.
So, since that was the case, he would go for the kill, sacrificing Zareth’s undead life for the greater good. He would be revived later, just like the last time.
And so, with nobody coming to his aid, Zareth could only watch as Elyndra tried her best to save him, yet Vorath’s attack kept blocking the way.
A second later, Vorath unleashed its attack.
A concentrated beam of condensed necrotic essence shot from dozens of eyes simultaneously, converging into a single torrent aimed directly at Zareth and the serpent beneath him.
The beam came with such corruption that, as it traveled, the very space around it started to decay. It was as if reality itself was being corrupted by it.
Zareth saw it. His death was in that beam coming toward him, and no matter how much energy he harnessed, he knew there was no surviving it.
He could only watch as the beam sped toward him.
"NOOOOO!" Ingrid’s scream filled the space.
However, she was just too far to make any difference.
Suddenly, just when the beam was a few meters away, golden lightning churned from the cloud, followed by a voice that spread across the space.
"Here I come."

chapters.title: Chapter 1462: The Tenth Floor - The Planet Devourer (4)
paragraphs: Kaizo descended from the clouds like a lightning bolt.
His fist, covered in an elegant golden and silver gauntlet, was clenched tightly, and just when the dark beam was half a meter from striking Zareth, Kaizo appeared before him and punched forward.
His fist met the beam, creating a powerful explosion.
BOOM
Zareth was pushed back, his body flying toward the dark sea.
Luckily, Elyndra was available, so she used space magic to move him toward herself.
"Are you okay?" she asked in a worried tone.
Zareth nodded, but his focus was on Kaizo, whose body was surrounded on all sides by black goo.
He was covered from head to toe, his body hidden within what Zareth knew would devour just about anyone, even an Immortal Lord if applied well.
So Kaizo being covered in it meant danger. However, his worry was dispelled when, suddenly, lightning bolts started crawling around the black goo.
That only lasted for a seconds before a thunderous explosion rocked the goo and Kaizo burst out, his body covered in golden armor.
At the same time, the void cracked in two different places.
From the first crack, Veydris stepped out, his sword glowing red and raised high. In one powerful slash, a terrifying sword arc flashed out, landing on Vorath’s side.
Then, from the second crack, a 3-meter-long arrow appeared, stabbing into Vorath’s side.
These two attacks forced out a painful, shrill cry, one that caused the space to quake. Its tendrils shot out, half going to Veydris, while the other half moved toward the new arrival, Kol.
Vexthra said this mission could only be handled by those with an understanding of the void and the ability to use Devouring Qi. Naturally, Zareth fell right into the Devouring Qi category.
Ingrid, Veydris, and Enkay were aligned with the void, while Elyndra played the counter to the void. She cannot control the void, but she has control over space, the perfect counter for the void.
However, aside from them, there were two others who fit right into the team.
Kaizo has divine lightning, a perfect counter for Devouring Qi and all forms of corruption, while Kol is a deadly void beast whose true power comes from wielding the void.
He is also a True Immortal with 7 strands of Immortal Qi under his control.

With the kind of power he has, if he were sent alone, he would be able to finish this mission with ease. But Vexthra wanted the first five to have a taste of what it feels like fighting a True Immortal.
Kol and Kaizo followed them. However, they were instructed to join only when the battle reached its climax or when something unexpected was to happen.
Zareth’s death was the opening Veydris had been waiting for to launch the attack that would have ended the abomination.
Though it was a bit cold on Veydris’ part, it wasn’t like anyone could blame him. An undead under Kent’s command cannot die, so he made the right move.
And now, watching as Vorath is trying to push for one last desperate move, one could tell Veydris made the right call. His attack contained a divine power that is immune to corruption.
So, although he and Kol were now under a deadly assault, he knew it was only a matter of time before the abomination was dealt with.

Kaizo, however, had no time to wait, so he channeled 7% of his bloodline to end the battle. In an instant, the entire space exploded into a golden lightning domain, covering a vast stretch of the battlefield.
"Move back, everyone."
With that simple command, he leaped into the air, and when he descended, his fist went right through the gaping maw Veydris had left.
Golden lightning detonated from Kaizo’s fist the moment it plunged into the gaping maw.
The impact did not simply strike flesh—it invaded its interior like a poison.

The divine lightning coursed inward like a living thing, racing through Vorath’s rotting interior, illuminating its grotesque body from within. It was as if a bulb had been lit inside its horrible body.
For a brief second, the bloated abomination became translucent, its countless veins and corrupted channels exposed in flashing gold.
The lightning was evading its interior, and from how it was twitching, there is just no way it could survive much longer.
However, it wasn’t going down without a fight.
Suddenly, the sea exploded.
A pillar of necrotic water shot upward as Vorath convulsed violently, its tendrils thrashing in chaotic desperation.
Ingrid, who had managed to free herself from its hold, was struck back, flying toward the black sea. Thankfully, Veydris knew who to save and who to let die.
Ingrid is more important than Zareth, so he moved through the unstable void and caught her before she could slam into the water, which then would have been too late for her.
The necrotic water is a poison that cannot be taken lightly. Zareth even plan on taking a sample for Kent.

Kaizo poured more essence into his domain, causing it to crackle and expand, each bolt acting like a cleansing blade, burning away the floating droplets of Necrotic Qi before they could condense again.
He did not retreat. He knew this was the winning attack, so he pressed forward.
In one desperate move, he roared, channeling more divine lightning into his gauntlet as his fist drove deeper.

Vorath also pushed forward forcing more necrotic essense to fill the air. However, his lightning armor around him flared brighter, resisting the devouring corruption that tried to crawl back into his arm.
At the same time, Kol moved.
The void around him did not crack like when Ingrid and the others used it. To him, given how deep his understanding went, there was just no way he would find it difficult to use the void.
With a single step, he phased through the incoming tendrils and reappeared directly above Vorath’s swollen body.

Three strands of Immortal Qi moved along his arm as his bow was aimed right at the wound his first arrow left. A thick arrow formed, and the Immortal Qi augmented it, causing the void to crack at its tip.
"The end."
He fired the arrow, and it went right through Vorath and came out from the other side.

Without any delay, he moved and grabbed Kaizo by the hand, and they both vanished into the void. Elyndra didn’t know why Kol did that, but she also used space magic to move Enkay, who happened to be the closest to Vorath.
Just as she did, Vorath’s colossal body expanded, and boom, it exploded.

The shockwave from the explosion blasted everyone back. However, before some of them could lose their balance and fall into the harrowing, black, corrupted water, Kol appeared from the void and created channels for them.
In an instant, aside from him, all six teammates vanished into the void, appearing on the other side of the river where Axiom and the others were waiting for them.
Kol only attacked becaure he saw what Kaizo did when he channeled his lightning into the beast’s body.
That gave him the idea of how to kill Vorath. When Kaizo’s lightning illuminated the creature, it reacted violently.
It was clear that no matter how many injuries they left on its body, it would always heal. So killing it from the inside was the only way.
The arrow was used to carry the Immortal Qi into its body. The rest was merely him exploding his own Immortal Qi.

While it would take a couple of days to recover, exploding it was the only way they could kill the abomination. It worked as expected, and with the synergy between him and Axiom, he managed to save his teammates from being pushed into the corrupted water.
He scanned the area, and with a wave, a basketball-sized core flew from the water and landed on his palm. Then, with a step forward, he vanished into the void, appearing on the shore.

sentences.text: Kaizo descended from the clouds like a lightning bolt.
His fist, covered in an elegant golden and silver gauntlet, was clenched tightly, and just when the dark beam was half a meter from striking Zareth, Kaizo appeared before him and punched forward.
His fist met the beam, creating a powerful explosion.
BOOM
Zareth was pushed back, his body flying toward the dark sea.
Luckily, Elyndra was available, so she used space magic to move him toward herself.
"Are you okay?" she asked in a worried tone.
Zareth nodded, but his focus was on Kaizo, whose body was surrounded on all sides by black goo.
He was covered from head to toe, his body hidden within what Zareth knew would devour just about anyone, even an Immortal Lord if applied well.
So Kaizo being covered in it meant danger.
However, his worry was dispelled when, suddenly, lightning bolts started crawling around the black goo.
That only lasted for a seconds before a thunderous explosion rocked the goo and Kaizo burst out, his body covered in golden armor.
At the same time, the void cracked in two different places.
From the first crack, Veydris stepped out, his sword glowing red and raised high.
In one powerful slash, a terrifying sword arc flashed out, landing on Vorath’s side.
Then, from the second crack, a 3-meter-long arrow appeared, stabbing into Vorath’s side.
These two attacks forced out a painful, shrill cry, one that caused the space to quake.
Its tendrils shot out, half going to Veydris, while the other half moved toward the new arrival, Kol.
Vexthra said this mission could only be handled by those with an understanding of the void and the ability to use Devouring Qi.
Naturally, Zareth fell right into the Devouring Qi category.
Ingrid, Veydris, and Enkay were aligned with the void, while Elyndra played the counter to the void.
She cannot control the void, but she has control over space, the perfect counter for the void.
However, aside from them, there were two others who fit right into the team.
Kaizo has divine lightning, a perfect counter for Devouring Qi and all forms of corruption, while Kol is a deadly void beast whose true power comes from wielding the void.
He is also a True Immortal with 7 strands of Immortal Qi under his control.
With the kind of power he has, if he were sent alone, he would be able to finish this mission with ease.
But Vexthra wanted the first five to have a taste of what it feels like fighting a True Immortal.
Kol and Kaizo followed them.
However, they were instructed to join only when the battle reached its climax or when something unexpected was to happen.
Zareth’s death was the opening Veydris had been waiting for to launch the attack that would have ended the abomination.
Though it was a bit cold on Veydris’ part, it wasn’t like anyone could blame him.
An undead under Kent’s command cannot die, so he made the right move.
And now, watching as Vorath is trying to push for one last desperate move, one could tell Veydris made the right call.
His attack contained a divine power that is immune to corruption.
So, although he and Kol were now under a deadly assault, he knew it was only a matter of time before the abomination was dealt with.
Kaizo, however, had no time to wait, so he channeled 7% of his bloodline to end the battle.
In an instant, the entire space exploded into a golden lightning domain, covering a vast stretch of the battlefield.
"Move back, everyone."
With that simple command, he leaped into the air, and when he descended, his fist went right through the gaping maw Veydris had left.
Golden lightning detonated from Kaizo’s fist the moment it plunged into the gaping maw.
The impact did not simply strike flesh—it invaded its interior like a poison.
The divine lightning coursed inward like a living thing, racing through Vorath’s rotting interior, illuminating its grotesque body from within.
It was as if a bulb had been lit inside its horrible body.
For a brief second, the bloated abomination became translucent, its countless veins and corrupted channels exposed in flashing gold.
The lightning was evading its interior, and from how it was twitching, there is just no way it could survive much longer.
However, it wasn’t going down without a fight.
Suddenly, the sea exploded.
A pillar of necrotic water shot upward as Vorath convulsed violently, its tendrils thrashing in chaotic desperation.
Ingrid, who had managed to free herself from its hold, was struck back, flying toward the black sea.
Thankfully, Veydris knew who to save and who to let die.
Ingrid is more important than Zareth, so he moved through the unstable void and caught her before she could slam into the water, which then would have been too late for her.
The necrotic water is a poison that cannot be taken lightly.
Zareth even plan on taking a sample for Kent.

Kaizo poured more essence into his domain, causing it to crackle and expand, each bolt acting like a cleansing blade, burning away the floating droplets of Necrotic Qi before they could condense again.
He did not retreat.
He knew this was the winning attack, so he pressed forward.
In one desperate move, he roared, channeling more divine lightning into his gauntlet as his fist drove deeper.
Vorath also pushed forward forcing more necrotic essense to fill the air.
However, his lightning armor around him flared brighter, resisting the devouring corruption that tried to crawl back into his arm.
At the same time, Kol moved.
The void around him did not crack like when Ingrid and the others used it.
To him, given how deep his understanding went, there was just no way he would find it difficult to use the void.
With a single step, he phased through the incoming tendrils and reappeared directly above Vorath’s swollen body.
Three strands of Immortal Qi moved along his arm as his bow was aimed right at the wound his first arrow left.
A thick arrow formed, and the Immortal Qi augmented it, causing the void to crack at its tip.
"The end."
He fired the arrow, and it went right through Vorath and came out from the other side.
Without any delay, he moved and grabbed Kaizo by the hand, and they both vanished into the void.
Elyndra didn’t know why Kol did that, but she also used space magic to move Enkay, who happened to be the closest to Vorath.
Just as she did, Vorath’s colossal body expanded, and boom, it exploded.
The shockwave from the explosion blasted everyone back.
However, before some of them could lose their balance and fall into the harrowing, black, corrupted water, Kol appeared from the void and created channels for them.
In an instant, aside from him, all six teammates vanished into the void, appearing on the other side of the river where Axiom and the others were waiting for them.
Kol only attacked becaure he saw what Kaizo did when he channeled his lightning into the beast’s body.
That gave him the idea of how to kill Vorath.
When Kaizo’s lightning illuminated the creature, it reacted violently.
It was clear that no matter how many injuries they left on its body, it would always heal.
So killing it from the inside was the only way.

Then, with a step forward, he vanished into the void, appearing on the shore.

chapters.title: Chapter 1463: Void Mark
paragraphs: [Congratulations, you have cleared the 10th floor of the Planet Killer Dungeon.]
A new message appeared before everyone, announcing that the harrowing mission on the 10th floor had been completed thanks to the brilliant efforts of Zareth and his team.
Although the win nearly came at a cost, they all finally understood how hard it is to fight immortals, especially True Immortals and above.
Initially, even with Enkay, who is also a True Immortal, they came close to losing Zareth. That shows there is just no way a warrior should underestimate their opponent before battle.

If Vexthra had looked down on Vorath and hadn’t prepared Kaizo and Kol as a backup plan, the main team, while Veydris would have prepared a good chance for Enkay or Ingrid to go for the kill, Zareth would have died.
So they learned, and next time, they would know what to do to have the upper hand.
"That was an eye-opener," Zareth said, taking a deep breath. Then he turned to Veydris. "I can’t believe you actually chose to let me die."
While he was not angry, the mere fact that Veydris didn’t do anything when he was in danger but went to Ingrid’s rescue when she found herself in a pickle made him smile.
The bias was plain as day.
When it comes to Kent’s wives or just any lady at all, Veydris would not hesitate to save them.
"Don’t blame Veydris. He is a logical being, and so he knew you wouldn’t have died even if you had died." Irina, of course, came to her boyfriend’s rescue.
While Veydris had never spoken a single word nor even made any advances toward her, Irina always hung around him, bothering him with long talks.
In her defence, she claims Veydris is a good listener.
Quite ironic, if one thinks about it critically.
But then again, their happiness is what Vexthra is after, so if she thinks Veydris is the right one for her, then why not?

Already, the men in the legion had started approaching the ladies in the various tower cities. Zareth already had a Sky Fox girlfriend, so there is no harm in letting Irina infatuate herself with a metallic robot.
It isn’t like this was the first time it had ever happened.
"It was indeed an eye-opener, one that had shown just what all of you would perform under pressure," Vexthra said.
She then turned to Elyndra. "I saw how you controlled the battlefield and how brilliant you were in coming to the aid of your teammates.
That was impressive, and so I will teach you an aspect of space law that, if mastered, will take your control of space to a whole new level."
Elyndra nodded.

She was impeccable in all the moves she made during the battle. She made sure their movements more fluid and easy. However, when Zareth found himself in danger, she saw how limited her control over space truly was.
So since Vexthra wanted to aid her, she wasn’t one to reject that.
Vexthra turned to Ingrid next.

"It seems you still need some training on how best to use the void, Ingrid. I saw how you could have taken advantage of certain moments to deal a terrifying attack, but you let them pass. While you came close to injuring it a few times, you could have done better."
"I will work on that, big sister. This happened to be my first big battle, so I was overwhelmed for a moment."

"Then be sure to fix that before the next big battle. If you want, you can go back to the tower and use the time difference to enter seclusion. I am sure you have identified your limitations and would work toward improving them."

"I will be fine, big sister. I have the knowledge. I just need the experience." Ingrid paused for a moment before an idea popped into her mind. She turned toward Axiom. "You are a Void Architect, right?"
Axiom nodded.

"Take me as your disciple. I want to improve my control of the Void. I have the knowledge, and, like you, I am a Voidling with half my bloodline awakened. If you can help me improve my control over the Void, I will be eternally grateful."
Axiom stood there for a few minutes before a sigh escaped his lips.
"To tell you the truth, you already have all you need to master the Void even more than me." He pointed at Ingrid’s left hand, where a lotus flower tattoo could be seen.
"That is not a tattoo; it is a weapon mostly known as the Void Mark." Kailan and Kol nodded. On the other hand, Ingrid and her sisters started paying close attention, Vexthra included.
"Back in the Void Universe, there were rumours of people possessing these tattoos. They called them Void Marks, and what they can do is very simple.
They can be used for attacks, defence, and, to some extent, healing."
Axiom waved his hand, and a large book appeared before him.
When Kol and Kailan saw this, their eyes widened.
"No way," Kol exclaimed.
"You were the one who stole the Void Codex from the 13th Void Supreme."
Axiom grinned. "That bastard had the guts to violate my sister until she died. He is lucky I only stole his life’s work. The next time we meet, I will be sure to smash his face in."
"We will help you. I also have beef with that bastard. He had better prepare himself for the kind of torture I have prepared for him," Kol also said, the three of them flashing an evil smile.
This sight scared the ladies and even a few of the men.
"Maybe we should go back to the Void Mark."
"Oh yes." Axiom flipped the pages till he reached one showing the same lotus tattoo on Ingrid’s arm.
"It is called the Seven Bloom Lotus Flower, one of the ten Void Flowers. This one uses a special flame called the Underworld Void Flame to harness its power.
Every petal has a unique power.
From what has been recorded here, the first petal can summon a Void Dragon two realms above the summoner. The best part is that the dragon won’t rely on her command or Void Essence to fight.
The second will grant an ability called ’Void Annihilation,’ where, thanks to the Void Mark, every attack has three times the original effect.
And the third petal, when it is harnessed, will also summon a Void Being known as a Void Knight. These knights are like judgment gods that the Void created as a defence mechanism for the Void Race.
If she can harness just one, then perhaps among all of us, she will be the most powerful. So you don’t need my help; you are just lacking one important aspect of your power."
"The Underworld Void Flame," Ingrid muttered, and Axiom nodded.

"I believe that is the last flavour you need to harness your power. It may even be the last ingredient you needed to complete your bloodline" He flipped to close the book; however, before the page could close, an image appeared for a moment.
"What is that?" Ingrid asked, pointing at the image of a wolf.

"Oh, this is one of the Void Monarchs. They are Void Beings created and blessed by the Void Dao. Every last one of them can harness the true power of the Void and bestow it on their master." Axiom paused and let out a smile.
"There has never been anyone who managed to tame a Void Monarch. Of course, it is just a rumour, but some claim somebody has done it before.
However, from what I read in this book and know, nobody ever recorded in the Void Codex succeeded in taming a Void Monarch."
Vexthra and her sisters gave Ingrid a sidelong glance.

chapters.title: Chapter 1464: Making a Lavish Purchase
paragraphs: [Alchemy Tower]
"Damn it. Another wasted effort," Kent cursed, frustration bubbling in his heart, eyes, and face.
He slammed the side of the cauldron, sending the lid flying.
Then, from within, a 98% pure Tier 14 Bone Hardening Pill appeared. He grabbed it, and after a few observations, he threw it into his space ring and walked out of the Pill Room.
There was no need to put it in a pill bottle, since it would be wasted.
He stretched for a few minutes, then he vanished into the Harem Tower to take his bath before heading out again.
It had already been eight days since he entered the Alchemy Tower, which is just 8 hours on the outside.
The past 8 days have been him working hard to make a pure Tier 14 pill. However, even after over 24 different sets of concoctions, he had yet to concoct a pure Tier 14 Pill.
He had progressed much more easily with Tier 13.
However, Tier 14 was dragging him to the point where he started to wonder if he could even handle it.
While he understood that Tier 14 Pills are basically the peak of pill making in a High World, the mere fact that he had been struggling with it baffled him.

It felt like he had not made much progress, despite gaining recognition from the Pill Dao. Naturally, it was because of the insight he had gotten from the Pill Dao that enabled him to even score 98% purity.
Even so, he still had a long way to go, and the constant failure was not helping at all.

However, since his days were over, he had to return to Planet Brymrr to continue his mission. His next agenda was to find the Green Ice Restaurant and finally meet the Bimk guy that Randel said could help him.
For now, he had to know more about the world before he made any rash decisions.
After freshening up, he harnesses the power of the marker he left in the hotel room. The moment he appeared, a knock landed on the door.
He first used the soul map to confirm who knocked before opening it. He was in a world populated by beings far beyond his level, so he had to be extra careful.
Luckily, it turned out the one who knocked was merely a worker who came to clean the room. Since he would be checking out, he let the cleaner in and left to check out at the reception.
"Come back again, Mr. Jaqen," the lady at the gate said when he stepped out.
Kent nodded and soon walked away, heading deeper into the city.
Aside from looking for the Green Ice Restaurant, he also knew he had to find information as he moved, so he kept the soul map active, listening to every small thing said within an 80,000 km radius.
Unfortunately, even after one hour, nothing of interest was said, so he decided to ask someone for directions.
He approached a jewelry store that sold earrings, bracelets, and similar items. It isn’t that grand, so he figured he would ask the seller.

"Welcome to the Everyday Jewelry Shop," a young lady said, approaching Kent the moment he stepped into the store. Looking at the polite smile on her face, Kent knew he had to purchase something before asking his question.

There was no way she would maintain the same smile if she found out he had only entered the store to ask for directions. Thankfully, he had more than enough spirit stones to use and wives to buy gifts for.
Even if he was out of cash, he could just cash out his earnings after becoming a partner of the Brown Maple Auction Empire.
Three hundred thousand years ago, he bought a 2% share in the auction house, then known as the Brown Maple Auction House.
Now, it had become the Brown Maple Auction Empire, and after 300,000 years, who knew how much he had made?
"Hi, I want to buy necklaces for my sweetheart waiting for me back home," Kent said with a smile, making sure the lady knew he wasn’t the kind who liked to waste time.
As expected, she lit up with joy when she heard him. She was smart enough to know Kent wanted to buy more than one, merely from what he said.
"Please enter."
Kent entered the store, following her.
It was after he entered that he saw the kind of space he was in. While on the outside it appeared like a small store, the inside is rather vast and extremely lavish.
It appeared to be a pocket dimension of some kind.
There are other sellers and quite a lot of buyers. This made Kent aware of where all the smiles came from when he was approached by the lady.
She is a seller, so when she makes a sale, she gets a commission.
"Can I get you anything to drink?" she further offered, to which Kent shook his head. He understood she merely wanted to make sales, so she was being extra hospitable.
This made him remember Veth, whom he had met 300,000 years ago while roaming the Pill World.
"What is your name?" Kent asked.
"Lia."
"Well, Lia, my name is Jaqen. This is my first time in Snow City and my first time in any store, so if possible, help me purchase some necklaces for some people who would very much appreciate them."

Lia smiled and nodded. "Sure. We have all kinds of jewelry, ranging from 100,000 to the millions. Of course, if your pocket is deep enough and can fork out a billion plus, we have some classic ones that would most certainly bring smiles to the faces of whoever you will be buying them for."
"Sounds like a good plan. Why don’t we head to the billion section instead?"
Lia narrowed her eyes for a moment, then nodded and started leading Kent toward a VIP section where only one person could be seen looking through the display.

As they headed there, the other sellers and buyers couldn’t help but shake their heads in contempt. In their heads, a Heavenly Ascension Stage cultivator—especially one with no guard—had no business looking at a billion jewelry displays.
Even walking behind Lia, Kent could tell she was of the same mindset. However, he said nothing and followed her there.
When they reached the VIP section, fewer than 40 necklaces were on display, each with a beautiful design that would undoubtedly make any lady happy.
Kent wanted to buy necklaces as gifts for his wives, so buying high-quality ones made the most sense.
After spending a few minutes looking through the display, he pointed at 26 necklaces. "Package them for me, would you?"
For a moment, everyone inside the store froze.
"Are you sure?" Lia asked, a bit skeptical.

"I am dead serious, dear." Kent took a few steps back and sat in a chair. He lifted his right leg and placed it on his left. "Of course, if you want one, I don’t mind making it 27. You can pick anyone you want.
Afterward, go to the bracelets section and pick 20 bracelets for children."

Lia remained standing for a few minutes before nodding and starting to package the goods. Seeing this, Kent smiled, retrieved a spirit fruit, and began eating, oblivious to the stunned expressions on everyone’s faces.
Before entering the store, he had no plan to spend more than a billion. However, meeting Lia made him remember the kind of backing he has.
While at the moment he is no different from a mortal, he is affiliated with the Brown Maple Auction Empire and Dream Pill Emporium.
These are some of the most powerful businesses in the universe now. If he wants, he can reveal he is from there, and not many will bother him.
This will eliminate all unnecessary trouble, at least while in Snow City.
So he made a big purchase, and when his total came, he let out a smile and retrieved the bank card Lady Wu gave him.

Luckily, it turned out the one who knocked was merely a worker who came to clean the room.
Since he would be checking out, he let the cleaner in and left to check out at the reception.
"Come back again, Mr.
Jaqen," the lady at the gate said when he stepped out.
Kent nodded and soon walked away, heading deeper into the city.
Aside from looking for the Green Ice Restaurant, he also knew he had to find information as he moved, so he kept the soul map active, listening to every small thing said within an 80,000 km radius.
Unfortunately, even after one hour, nothing of interest was said, so he decided to ask someone for directions.
He approached a jewelry store that sold earrings, bracelets, and similar items.
It isn’t that grand, so he figured he would ask the seller.
"Welcome to the Everyday Jewelry Shop," a young lady said, approaching Kent the moment he stepped into the store.
Looking at the polite smile on her face, Kent knew he had to purchase something before asking his question.
There was no way she would maintain the same smile if she found out he had only entered the store to ask for directions.
Thankfully, he had more than enough spirit stones to use and wives to buy gifts for.
Even if he was out of cash, he could just cash out his earnings after becoming a partner of the Brown Maple Auction Empire.
Three hundred thousand years ago, he bought a 2% share in the auction house, then known as the Brown Maple Auction House.
Now, it had become the Brown Maple Auction Empire, and after 300,000 years, who knew how much he had made?
"Hi, I want to buy necklaces for my sweetheart waiting for me back home," Kent said with a smile, making sure the lady knew he wasn’t the kind who liked to waste time.
As expected, she lit up with joy when she heard him.
She was smart enough to know Kent wanted to buy more than one, merely from what he said.
"Please enter."
Kent entered the store, following her.
It was after he entered that he saw the kind of space he was in.
While on the outside it appeared like a small store, the inside is rather vast and extremely lavish.
It appeared to be a pocket dimension of some kind.
There are other sellers and quite a lot of buyers.
This made Kent aware of where all the smiles came from when he was approached by the lady.
She is a seller, so when she makes a sale, she gets a commission.
"Can I get you anything to drink?" she further offered, to which Kent shook his head.
He understood she merely wanted to make sales, so she was being extra hospitable.
This made him remember Veth, whom he had met 300,000 years ago while roaming the Pill World.
"What is your name?" Kent asked.
"Lia."
"Well, Lia, my name is Jaqen.
This is my first time in Snow City and my first time in any store, so if possible, help me purchase some necklaces for some people who would very much appreciate them."
Lia smiled and nodded.
"Sure.
We have all kinds of jewelry, ranging from 100,000 to the millions.
Of course, if your pocket is deep enough and can fork out a billion plus, we have some classic ones that would most certainly bring smiles to the faces of whoever you will be buying them for."
"Sounds like a good plan.
Why don’t we head to the billion section instead?"
Lia narrowed her eyes for a moment, then nodded and started leading Kent toward a VIP section where only one person could be seen looking through the display.
As they headed there, the other sellers and buyers couldn’t help but shake their heads in contempt.
In their heads, a Heavenly Ascension Stage cultivator—especially one with no guard—had no business looking at a billion jewelry displays.
Even walking behind Lia, Kent could tell she was of the same mindset.
However, he said nothing and followed her there.
When they reached the VIP section, fewer than 40 necklaces were on display, each with a beautiful design that would undoubtedly make any lady happy.
Kent wanted to buy necklaces as gifts for his wives, so buying high-quality ones made the most sense.
After spending a few minutes looking through the display, he pointed at 26 necklaces.
"Package them for me, would you?"
For a moment, everyone inside the store froze.
"Are you sure?" Lia asked, a bit skeptical.
"I am dead serious, dear." Kent took a few steps back and sat in a chair.
He lifted his right leg and placed it on his left.
"Of course, if you want one, I don’t mind making it 27.
You can pick anyone you want.
Afterward, go to the bracelets section and pick 20 bracelets for children."
Lia remained standing for a few minutes before nodding and starting to package the goods.
Seeing this, Kent smiled, retrieved a spirit fruit, and began eating, oblivious to the stunned expressions on everyone’s faces.
Before entering the store, he had no plan to spend more than a billion.
However, meeting Lia made him remember the kind of backing he has.
While at the moment he is no different from a mortal, he is affiliated with the Brown Maple Auction Empire and Dream Pill Emporium.
These are some of the most powerful businesses in the universe now.
If he wants, he can reveal he is from there, and not many will bother him.
This will eliminate all unnecessary trouble, at least while in Snow City.
So he made a big purchase, and when his total came, he let out a smile and retrieved the bank card Lady Wu gave him.

chapters.title: Chapter 1465: Green Ice Restaurant
paragraphs: "Everything sums up to 123 billion high-grade spirit stones."
"Here you go." Kent handed the card to Lia and leaned back in his chair.
The Tower had already informed him that the first 100 years’ benefits from his 2% shares had been deposited into his account. After that, everything started to accumulate onto his VIP auction card.
But the one on his bank card was already enough to pay for this item. He also had physical spirit stones that he could use. However, to take his eye off his wealth, he decided to use the card.
This was also his way of letting Lady Wu know he was back. Kent was sure she should be monitoring his wealth, so he used it.
Lia, who couldn’t believe her eyes, took the card and pressed it against the payment crystal. Everyone inside the store held their breath, watching as the crystal hummed softly before turning green.
When the payment is confirmed, they all turned to look at Kent, who bit into his fruit as if he hadn’t just made the biggest purchase in the store’s history.

Lia couldn’t believe she had made such a sale. The biggest sale she had ever made in her life was 2 billion. However, to make 123 billion in a single sale was just beyond anything she had prepared for.
She returned with the card and a space ring holding the items he bought. Kent wasted no time and stored them away before asking the question that had brought him into the store in the first place.
"I was told the Green Ice Restaurant serves some of the best dishes in Snow City. If you don’t mind, kindly show me the direction to get there."
Lia nodded promptly and led Kent out of the store. The other sellers and buyers could only stand there and watch them leave. It was after they left that many started wondering who Kent was.
After many assumptions, they concluded that, since Kent didn’t mind showing off his wealth in front of dozens of others, he might come from a very powerful background.
Once that conclusion was reached, none of them dared follow him or even plot behind closed doors. They didn’t want to anger him.
On the other hand, Lia led Kent out of the store and started walking due east. "You can just show me where to go, and that would do. No need to take me there."
"I insist. Your purchase just now has changed my life in ways you can’t start to imagine, so the least I can do is take you where you want to go."
"If you insist, then I will be in your care."
Lia nodded, and soon, they put quite a distance between them and the store. Half an hour later, they arrived at a grand restaurant.
"Wow, I guess the hype wasn’t for nothing. This place is grand."

"Indeed. It is one of the best restaurants in Snow City. The last I checked, reserving a table here requires you to be of a certain social standing. Only powerful immortals, demigods, and gods eat here."
Kent nodded but said nothing. He wasn’t here to eat, so there was just no way he would bother with reserving a table.
"By the way, thanks for bringing me here. If you need anything, feel free to tell me, and I will do my best to help you."
Lia smiled and shook her head. "You have done enough. Just enjoy your meal. If destiny wills it, we will meet again."
Kent nodded, and they parted ways. He stood there for a few minutes before approaching the restaurant.
’Immortal Emperors as guards, huh?’ Kent said inwardly as he approached the guards with a polite smile.
"Good day, seniors. I am here to meet Lord Bimk."
"Is he aware you are coming?" one of them asked.

Even without them saying a word, Kent could see the disdain on their faces. They looked down on him, which in reality wasn’t their fault. He had no powerful guard with him, so there was no need to respect him, even if he was some powerful heir.
"If the one who sent me informed him, then yes. But just in case she hasn’t, then let him know Queen Randel sent me."
At the mention of Randel’s name, the two of them straightened up.
"Can we see some proof?" This time, their tone wasn’t arrogant in any way. If anything, he now sounded more respectful.
Kent nodded, retrieved the jade token Randel had given him, and handed it to them. Seeing the familiar token, they bowed, and one of them gestured for him to follow.
Kent said nothing and started to follow him inside.
The interior was lavish, as one would expect. Of course, he paid little to no attention to that since the last thing he wanted was meeting the gaze of anyone he shouldn’t have.
If this were a place where the strongest was an Immortal Lord, he wouldn’t have minded. However, he could already sense people more powerful than Immortal Lords, so he was being respectful.
They moved up the stairs. A few minutes later, they arrived in a VIP room where only a jade table and marble chairs could be seen.
On the table rested a jug filled with wine and two wine glasses on the side.
"Please wait here. I will inform Lord Bimk of your arrival."
The guard left, leaving Kent alone in the room. He stayed there for a few minutes before pouring some wine for himself.
Taking a sip, he felt a refreshing sensation pass through his body. "Good wine," he began, taking tiny sips and savoring the taste.
Meanwhile, the guard quickly made his way toward another VIP room, where a fat man with a belly so big that fitting him in a Cybertruck would be an impossible task.
With him was a lady dressed like a man. She is extremely beautiful, but with he low-cut hair and cloak, she appeared more handsome.
Both of them were Peak Immortal Lords; however, at a glance, one could tell the fatty would easily end her existence with a snap of his finger.
Suddenly, a knock landed on the door, causing them to pause their discussion. They turned to the door, both letting out dangerous glares.
Before they even asked, the guard knelt and spoke. "My lord, the person Lady Randel spoke about is here. I took him to VIP room 342."
The lady dressed as a man sighed. "My apologies, Lord Bigson. I will be right back."
The fatty growled but nodded.
He extended his senses to the VIP room where Kent was resting. When he saw the person who dared to end his meeting with Lord Bimk, a frown appeared on his face.
However, he made no action that would suggest he was pissed.
Instead, he took a large chunk of meat and started devouring it.
Lord Bimk, who preferred to be called that way despite being a lady, left the VIP room where she was meeting the fatty and headed toward VIP room 342.
Queen Randel had called and informed her that Kent would be coming. She made sure she was aware that Kent was a very important person, so he should be treated with respect.
Since she was instructed by a VIP member of her restaurant, she took Kent’s arrival seriously, so now that he was here, she decided to go see him first.
A few minutes later, she stood before the door leading to the VIP room.
’Here we go.’ She swung the door open, and when her eyes landed on Kent’s face, a stunned expression filled her eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 1466: Lord Bimk
paragraphs: "You know, when Queen Randel called, saying someone would be coming with her referral token, I expected you to be some terrifying beast. Who would have thought you were just a human mortal?"
Lord Bimk said, her eyes narrowing a bit as she walked into the VIP room and sat in the chair opposite Kent.
"Though now that I have met you, mind telling me what business a human mortal like you had inside that place? Even better, how did you survive meeting her?"
Kent let a smile appear on his face. To be honest, he himself couldn’t make sense of what Lord Bimk had asked, despite actually meeting and surviving the Unknown Forest.
Considering his status and rank, there is just no way he should have survived that place. So, going as far as getting the referral of such a terrifying beast shocked her.
"What can I say? I happen to have a good impression on people," he laughed in the end, and Lord Bimk also couldn’t help but chuckle.
There is no way Kent would tell her all he had to do just to secure a safe passage from the Unknown Forest. If he were to get into it, then he would be forced to reveal his true identity.

There is just no way anyone would believe he had killed a Peak Immortal Lord and a pseudo-demigod. So changing the topic was the best move. Thankfully, Lord Bimk had little time, so she got right to the point.
"I owe Queen Randel a favour, so since she said you can cash in her favour, you have 10 minutes to ask me anything you need, and I will do my best to help you."

’A favour, huh?’ Kent felt touched that Queen Randel was using a favour she could have used for something better to aid him instead. ’Then again, I have given her more than she asked for, so there is that.’
The treasures he left her are worth more than her favour.
"First thing I want to know is the name, location, and cultivation rank of the current ruler of this planet."

Lord Bimk blinked a few times when she heard the question Kent asked. For a moment, she just couldn’t help but wonder if Kent was messing with her. However, when she saw the look of seriousness on his face, she narrowed her eyes.
"Wait, you actually want to ask that? Aren’t you a bit ahead of yourself, asking such big questions?"

"I know. However, I really want to know, so if possible, kindly answer my question." There is no beating around the bush here. After all, there is just no way he would come all this way if he didn’t want to know that.
"A very weird question, but I will answer." She sighed and started to answer, "From what I know, the ruler of this universe is the legendary Ten Emotions Sword Supreme.
Of course, this knowledge came from billions of years ago, just when the planet became a Unique World, so there is a chance it is outdated.
After all, it had been billions of years already, and considering the many Supremes that had appeared, anything is possible.
There are some even claiming that a Celestial lives here, so there is a strong chance she has long been dethroned. As to whether that is indeed the case, you would have to find out yourself.

However, unless there is another ruler, if you ask anyone, they would say she is the only known ruler. As to where you can find her, you can go to the two strongest continents in the world, the Elven Continent or the Dwarven Continent.
Most of the Supremes and Gods reside on those continents."
"I see," Kent nodded, feeling a bit happy now that he had made some progress. "It is going to be a road trip then."
Lord Bimk turned her head sideways and looked at Kent with both a stunned and amused expression.

"First of all, there is nothing like a road trip here. Second, what are you even happy about? From where I stand, with your current standing, moving from one city to another would be a headache, much less continental travel."
Kent blinked a few times before asking, "Care to elaborate more on that?"
"There is nothing more to say. From what I know, long before the planet ascended and became a Unique World, travelling from one continent to another was simple.

You just had to use teleportation gates, and if the distance is vast, using Teleportation Channels would do. However, now continental travel requires either using the Continental Teleportation Channel or crossing the Domain Sea.

The Continental Teleportation Channel is the safest but also the hardest to use since only the most powerful people can afford the tickets, or even better, only they have the qualifications to book a ticket.
The Domain Sea is very dangerous, but also the cheapest and easiest to get to. However, looking at your frail body, taking that route is suicide."
Kent sat there frozen for a few seconds, unsure of what to even say. Here, he had hoped to find out more about Inaya, only to learn that she could be in two places, but with no easy way to reach her.
He never expected this journey to be full of perils and obstacles. The least he expected was maybe finding it hard to know more about Inaya; he never looked forward to what Lord Bimk had just said.
And as if to make matters even worse, Kent immediately knew his chances of securing a Continental Teleportation Channel ticket were next to none.
This means he must take the Domain Sea.
But from Lord Bimk’s tone, it appears the Domain Sea isn’t a good place to traverse.
"Domain Sea, what can you tell me about it?"
"Think pirates, Sea Demons, the Underwater Cult, and all kinds of horrors you can imagine coming out to get you." She smiled, seeing the dark expression appear on Kent’s brow.
"Not to discourage you, depending on how deep your pockets are, you can secure a ticket to a ship where the guards would be strong enough to protect your dear life. But I wouldn’t count on it.
When the danger is chilling enough, all those guards will save their skins, so it would be best if you enjoy Snow City and leave when you have had enough."
"That is not something I can do. I am here on a mission, and so I must cross to the continents you mentioned.

If by chance I manage to get a Continental Teleportation Channel ticket, then fine, but now that I know there is a way to at least have some semblance of safe travel through the Domain Sea, I have to keep pushing forward."
There are many reasons why considering his current path sounds like a bad idea. However, he had to go, and so he would at least try his luck first.
"Whatever you think is best, kid. All I know is, staying here is the best decision you will ever make. But if you insist, then I will recommend trying your luck with the Seven Flag Sea Shanti.
They will head to the Dwarven Continent in three months’ time. Although they will take the Domain Sea, they are known for possessing some of the finest guards.

Their last voyage was a success, so choosing them is the best advice I can give you. Of course, if you want to try the Continental Teleportation Channel, the Falcon Crew is known to have much softer requirements.
Regardless, the Dwarven Continent is the closest to us, so going there first is the safest option."

They will head to the Dwarven Continent in three months’ time.
Although they will take the Domain Sea, they are known for possessing some of the finest guards.
Their last voyage was a success, so choosing them is the best advice I can give you.
Of course, if you want to try the Continental Teleportation Channel, the Falcon Crew is known to have much softer requirements.
Regardless, the Dwarven Continent is the closest to us, so going there first is the safest option."

chapters.title: Chapter 1467: Talent Search
paragraphs: Kent had to be honest that he never expected the next stages of his journey to be impossible ones.
Nothing that Lord Bimk had said inspired his confidence to keep moving forward. If anything, he considered calling Vexthra or Miryssa to help him cross to the next continent.
Lord Bimk made it sound like he had nowhere else to go but to stay in Snow City.
Using the Continental Teleportation Channel sounded safe but hard to get. Kent knew if he wanted, he could just call Vexthra over, who he knew would be able to get a ticket or two for both of them.
However, doing so would defeat the purpose of his mission. The next time he can’t call for her help, what then would he do?
For now, he wants to be able to solve his problems without relying on others.
This is but a prelude to the main mission he would be embarking on in about a year’s time. So he wants to solve his own problems.
This means his focus should go to the Domain Sea, where he had to prepare for just about anything. Lord Bimk recommended Seven Flag Sea Shanti as the best cruise ship he could go for.
Kent was grateful for that because at least he would have a chance. The next thing would be to secure a ticket, meaning he must head over to where they are located.
"This Seven Flag Sea Shanti, where can I find them, and how prepared should I be?"

"They are in Crystal City. You can pick a teleportation gate from here and get there directly in less than five minutes. As for what you need to qualify for a ticket, just become popular. They are known for transporting celebrities.
I doubt you have fighting power that will impress a demigod, so if you have other talents, now would be the time for you to show them. Maybe it would earn you some social standing.
I will also give you a recommendation letter, so that would butter up your chances. That is the least I can do for you."
Kent nodded.
He is grateful for that.
Lord Bimk went ahead to scribble a few words on a scroll. Then she placed her seal on it to authenticate it. After that, she handed it to Kent before she stood up.
They are done with their discussion. All Kent wanted to know had been answered, so the next thing was to leave.
Lord Bimk is also meeting with someone important, so staying too long would infuriate that person.
"By the way, what is your name?" she asked.
"Jaqen."
"Well then, Jaqen. Good luck, and I hope with every fibre of my being you succeed." Kent nodded and exchanged a handshake with her before leaving the room.
They parted ways, and Kent quickly left the restaurant.
He had a lot to think about before making any decision after hearing what kind of journey lies ahead of him.
From what Lord Bimk said, the ship will be leaving in three months. This means he has three months, or maybe less, to get a ticket.
But to do that, he had to go to Crystal City, where he had been before. It is just like Snow City, but unlike how there is snow raining here, it is filled with only crystallized ice.

In the past, one of his adventures brought him there. He spent close to a year there before leaving. Now, he had to go there again, but first, he needed to understand just what he had to do to become popular.
"Are all Unique Worlds this complicated?" he muttered as he moved deeper into the city.
He never expected Planet Brymrr to be this challenging.
He is a mortal, so aside from his good looks, there is basically nothing else he can do that will impress anyone that high up the ladder.
His swordsmanship is good, but he isn’t about to reveal that here. Who knows what kind of danger he would be putting himself in if he were to display his moves?
This is a planet that gave birth to Lord Genesis, the greatest swordsman to ever live. It means there are always swordsmen around, each looking to be the next Lord Genesis.
So until he is certain his swordsmanship won’t put him in danger, he wouldn’t dare try that.

This means he must use his Pill Monarch status to his advantage. Thankfully, Lord Bimk had given him a recommendation. Adding that to his Pill Monarch status would allow him to get a ticket or at least improve his chances.

A plan set in his mind, one that he had absolute trust in. However, to be on the safe side, he decided to look for something else he could do that would give him a name in Snow City before heading to Crystal City.
His thought was, ’If I can dominate the scene in Snow City, there is a chance I can make it to the Continental Teleportation Channel.’

Although he is also here to train, if he could avoid the domain sea, he would love that. In the past, the domain sea wasn’t that big of a deal. But after billions of years, it seems things had changed.
So using the teleport channel sounds like a good idea.
Though that would probably never happen, he couldn’t help but entertain the thought. Of course, it would be great if he could make a name for himself, not as a swordsman or an alchemist.
The problem is, he had no other way. His memories are there, but aside from swordsmanship, Alchemy and assassination, he is blank.
Chaos had no other talents aside from fighting. As a brute, he had no elegance that would give Kent a chance to become someone else.
If he had even a single elegant side, Elina wouldn’t have suffered that much trying to turn him into a human.
Jest was also all about the sword. He never had time to pick up on anything aside from pursuing more knowledge about the sword.
When it came to Faceless, he was also all about assassination. Maybe due to that limitation he had, he made sure the Faceless Agent created a second persona.
As for the Ruthless Bandit, his earlier years were fun, but nothing mind-blowing that could aid him today. Perhaps if he hadn’t come home to the death of his family, he would have helped someone.
Right now, Kent knew the rest of the book contained bitterness, and so he chose to ignore it.

This means the only path now is to become a con artist because, aside from the above-mentioned professions, the only skill he has that isn’t widely recognized is con artistry, and he has that thanks to Kevin Sage, whose memories he recently started to recall.
That bastard’s father turned him into one of the finest con artists in the universe before he died. So aside from swordsmanship, alchemy, and assassination, he is also a con artist.
Unfortunately, there is no way he can use that talent to make a good name for himself.
Just thinking about it made him grin from ear to ear.
He really is fucked, and that can be understood from how useless his past lives were.
Because of his thoughts, he had no idea when he walked to a section of the city where thousands of calligraphies and paintings were displayed.
When Kent saw this, he was brought to a halt, his fingers tingling as he looked at the beautiful paintings and calligraphy on display.
This isn’t the first time he felt this. Whenever he sees Unity’s Primordial Spirit Paint, he feels some form of attraction to it.
He had no idea where that feeling was coming from. However, one thing is certain: as he stood there staring at the paintings and calligraphies, he felt like he could do it.
