chapters.title: Chapter 1468: Aysel
paragraphs: Kent clearly didn’t know where the sudden interest in painting and calligraphy came from. He was only thinking about how to become famous when he lost track of time and found himself in this part of the city.
However, as he stood there, watching the thousands of paintings lined up on display, the same feeling he got when he held the sword for the first time seemed to crawl its way back into his heart.
Immediately, he could tell he had, at one point in time, fancied calligraphy and painting.
This means that one of his past incarnations had been a painter.
He, of course, ruled out Chaos, Jest, Faceless, the Ruthless Bandit, and even Kevin Sage. They aren’t the kind of people with an eye for painting or calligraphy.

This could only mean that out of the eight lives he had yet to know something of, one of them was a painter, and judging by the feeling he was getting as he stood there staring at the paintings, he knew without a shred of doubt that he was a very good painter.
He could see it clearly—most of the paintings on display are flawed. Some characters aren’t cleanly written, and most shocking of all was how there is no soul in anything he had seen so far.

Very shocking even was the feeling of intrigue and a bit of bias toward some of the paintings he was seeing. To him, some looked ugly, not because of their appearance but because of how he understood them.
Kent stood there for half an hour, admiring the arts with an open mind. This was also his way of making sure he actually had a good episode or a bad one.
For all he knew, this was merely a feeling of him liking something in a fleeting moment. He saw how Chaos fell in love with masquerade festivals after Elina forced him to attend a few.
What if this were one of those episodes?
Thankfully, even after an hour, he still could feel his understanding sharpening.
"Excuse me, big brother." Suddenly, a young lady with a rather large set of cute brown eyes tugged on Kent’s trousers, prompting him to look down.
When their gazes met, Kent felt an immediate attraction to the young lady. Seeing how short and petite she looked, he became interested in what she had to say.
Gaia and her band of troublemakers came to mind.
This young lady is a loli, as evidenced by her cute little appearance. Although she isn’t in any fancy clothing, her eyes and cute brown hair make her attractive.
Maybe it is just Kent’s bias toward lolis. He finds them cute and fun.
"Hi there, little lady, what is your name?"
"Aysel is Aysel."
Kent furrowed his brow, a smile appearing on his face. ’Just like Gaia and the others, she also speaks in the third person.’
His smile blossomed when this thought came to mind. He just doesn’t understand why, but after meeting Gaia, Akira, and Dori, his life was filled with people like them.
There is Li Hua, whom he saved back on Planet Sonox when he had just arrived in the cultivation world after his death on Earth.

There was also Yuna and Purity. Now, Aala and Vexthra’s sister, Risana, had joined them. He has eight lolis in his life, and when Nana is done merging back with her other parts, it will be nine lolis.
Looking at Aysel’s cute eyes, the urge to kidnap her flashed through his mind, but he smiled it off.
"I am Jaqen, nice meeting you." Kent extended his hand for a handshake, which Aysel accepted.
"Aysel saw that big brother was admiring the paintings. Aysel happens to sell paintings, so if big brother wants to buy some, he can follow me."
She started walking away, dragging Kent with her. Although she said he could follow her, she made it so he had no choice but to follow her.
As they moved forward, Kent could see the other sellers sighing in his direction. It appeared this little girl is quite popular, and perhaps this isn’t her first rodeo.
The mere fact that she came to him and even insisted that he follow her made him realize she wanted him to buy from her. Being a lolita lover, he said nothing and followed her.

A few minutes later, they arrived in front of a rundown store where two paintings of a mountain range and sunset clouds, and three calligraphies that read, "Mountain, Tomorrow, and Hope," hung at the entrance.
Kent didn’t know why he was brought there, but when his eyes landed on the mountain painting, a feeling of attraction formed in his heart.
A couple of minutes ago, he had looked at over 300 paintings, but this was the first one to catch his attention. It is ugly, but he sensed a genuine attraction to it.
It felt strange, but he didn’t hate the feeling.
Aysel pulled him closer, and that was when his eyes landed on a young lady painting inside the store. When she saw Aysel pull Kent into the store, a sigh escaped her lips.
"Aysel, didn’t I warn you against dragging strangers to our store against their wishes?"

"But big sister, big brother here loves painting, so Aysel brought him to buy one or else we can’t eat di—" Before she could end her sentence, the lady moved and covered her lips with her paint-stained hand, flashing an awkward smile at Kent.
"Sorry about that." She pulled Aysel away, leaving Kent standing there alone. Inwardly, a smile filled his heart. Aysel made him recall when he first met Li Hua.

The little human forced him to buy her cupcakes, citing that she needed the money to take care of her grandma. Although the lady covered Aysel’s mouth before she could end her sentence, Kent knew what she wanted to say.
She needed the money so they could eat dinner.
"Sorry about that. Aysel is always dragging people here to buy my paintings," the lady said, hiding Aysel behind her.
She poked her head out and spoke, "But big sister’s paintings are beautiful. Aysel just wants people to see and buy them."
"That doesn’t mean you should drag them here. How many times have I warned you against that behaviour?"
Aysel sighed and bent her head down. "Sorry, big brother. Aysel shouldn’t have dragged you here by force."
"No need to apologize, Aysel. If you hadn’t brought me here, I wouldn’t have seen this beautiful painting," Kent said and moved toward the painting of the mountain.
Aysel jumped from her sister’s back and rushed to Kent’s side. "Really? Does Big Brother want to buy it? It is just 1000 spirit stones."
Kent chuckled, turning to look at the beautiful, big-browed eyes on Aysel. "Why not? I have 1000 spirit stones to spare."
Aysel beamed with joy. She ran back to her sister, who earlier opposed her stance on Aysel’s behaviour, but now smiled when she heard Kent say he wanted to buy the painting.
Kent turned and faced her. "However, if you can tell me the story behind this painting, I will add another 1000 spirit stones."
"Really?" This time, it was Aysel’s sister’s turn to exclaim in a stunned tone.
"Yeah. I happen to have recently found a liking for painting and calligraphy, so telling me the inspiration behind it will make me super happy."

Kent didn’t know whether his offer would be accepted. However, he really wants to understand what the feeling he felt in his chest was. The only way to do that is to understand where the inspiration came from.
Thankfully, Aysel and her sister wanted the money, so she accepted his offer.

chapters.title: Chapter 1469: Memories of the Divine Beast Tamer
paragraphs: Kent had no reason to buy the painting on a normal day.
If he wanted a painting, Blossom would have painted a beautiful one for him.

However, in his bid to find other talents aside from his three professions, he found himself in this rundown store buying a painting that wouldn’t add any value to his collection if he were a collector.

His question was purely from an artist’s point of view. Of course, most collectors who love to display their collections feel they need to know the inspiration behind what they buy, so they can better sell their value to others.
The Mona Lisa had an inspiration behind it, as did other famous paintings.
Kent just wanted to satiate his curiosity, so he asked, and Aysel’s sister started to speak.
"This is the Dream Mountain. It is located in a village near Fractured City. Aysel and I came from there, and this mountain happens to be right beside our house.
It was where we grew up playing, and also the haven that most of us flee to whenever there are beast tides. I only painted it because it reminds us of home."
"I see," Kent muttered, feeling slightly better hearing the origin of the inspiration behind the painting. He wasn’t fully satiated, but he seemed satisfied enough to ask a second question.
"Why is one side of it broken off?" The painting in itself was mediocre. However, the meaning behind it seemed more intriguing if one put their soul into understanding it.
The painting showed that one side was broken off, with debris falling from it. From his perspective, that detail could have been ignored without changing the painting.
However, adding it seemed to hold some meaning, so he asked.
This time, it was Aysel who answered, "Big sister pushed the bad man off that section of the mountain, and it fell with him. Very bad man."
Kent turned to the young lady and smiled. He sensed her sister’s hesitation to answer, so, hearing from Aysel that something personal had happened that triggered her when he asked, he understood.
Because of that, he chose not to ask any further questions.

He gently touched the painting, brushing his hand across the canvas to mimic the brushstrokes. He closed his eyes and moved his finger a few times as if trying to force out where the feeling was coming from.
Seeing this, Aysel’s big sister furrowed her brow.
"Do you paint?" she asked, paying close attention to how Kent was moving his hand across the painting. She was a painter, so seeing his hands move made her wonder whether Kent was one too.

"Not that I can recall," Kent replied, getting absorbed in his gesture. A few seconds later, he pulled his hand back and turned to Aysel’s sister. "I only recently discovered my love for painting, so you can say I am at the budding stage, trying to find my groove."
"Why don’t you give it a try? I have a fresh canvas here and a few paints."
"I wouldn’t want to intrude," Kent tried to decline the offer, but Aysel reached for his hand, grabbed it, and pulled him toward the canvas.
"Big brother can try it, and if it is nice, big brother can buy it."
Kent chuckled.
How come he had to buy his own painting when he was the one who painted it? He turned and looked at Aysel’s sister, but she smiled and turned away.
Looking at the two of them, it was clear she was the brain behind the painting, while the little human was the brain behind the money-making.
Kent smiled and turned to face the canvas. He didn’t know if this was merely a fool’s errand. However, until he managed to make sense of his newest feelings, he would not be satisfied.
He reached for the palette and the brush. This was his first time holding these two things, but just as he touched them, a feeling of familiarity washed over him.
He lifted the brush to eye level and, just as he was about to pass it through the paint on the palette, he blacked out.
On the outside, he appeared fine. His hand began moving, picking up the paint, and he started painting. However, his senses were far gone...
In his mind, memories of a life he had lived several billion years ago were being replayed.
In that life, he was the son of a merchant and an Elven painter. Growing up, his mother doted on him so much that he spent most of his time by her side.
As a result, he fell in love with painting at a very young age. Whenever his mom started painting, he set up shop beside her and mimicked her painting.

At first, he was terrible at it. However, as a loving mother, whatever her son painted looked beautiful in her eyes. And since he was but a kid, every praise from his mother fueled his determination to do more.
Eventually, he started to improve. By the time he turned 10, his paintings started to sell, earning him fame and fortune.
His mother, whose main profession was painting, quit and began mentoring him, making sure his talent was put to good use.

They travelled a lot just so little Aurelion could see more and be inspired to paint beautiful things. By the time he turned 16 and was ready to start cultivating, his name had reached thousands of worlds.
He was called a young prodigy, one who only appeared every generation.
Thanks to him, their family became powerful and wealthy, so when he started cultivating, his parents hired the most powerful immortals as his teachers.
Initially, he hated the idea of cultivating; however, when his parents told him a story about a once-legendary painter who dominated the world through his paintings, his interest was piqued.
So he started cultivating, and in no time, his genius started to shine. He picked up everything very fast, and he never forgot anything he saw.
A few years later, when he finally reached the Core Formation stage, people from a sect called Spirit Ascension came to take him away under the direction of a god.
His parents wanted to stop them, but after hearing he would be safe and could return once he became an immortal, they let him go.
When he arrived at the sect, the first thing he did was look for a way to incorporate his art into his cultivation.
It took some time, but through his search, he found Talisman Arts, and that was when his brilliance began to shine.
Aurelion’s imagination was vivid, and his painting was on another level. So, with this discovery, he began to create art and calligraphy that held more than just beauty.
His paintings became more than just vivid imagination. A river painting could be manifested into a dangerous ocean using spiritual Qi.
Calligraphy of the word spear could be manifested into a deadly spear that could threaten even immortals. His cultivation surged from there, and for hundreds of years, he continued to improve.
Kent remained seated for 30 minutes, completely blacked out. However, his hands were moving as if he were conscious.
Standing behind him, Aysel’s sister kept her eyes wide, her jaw hanging loose as she gazed at the painting coming to life before her.
On the canvas, a beautiful lady with a star-shattering smile was slowly coming to life.
Aysel, who mostly had no interest in the painting process, even stood quietly, watching as Kent’s hand moved across the canvas, adding more layers to the paint.
The beauty of it all had gotten to her.

sentences.text: Kent had no reason to buy the painting on a normal day.
If he wanted a painting, Blossom would have painted a beautiful one for him.

However, in his bid to find other talents aside from his three professions, he found himself in this rundown store buying a painting that wouldn’t add any value to his collection if he were a collector.
His question was purely from an artist’s point of view.
Of course, most collectors who love to display their collections feel they need to know the inspiration behind what they buy, so they can better sell their value to others.
The Mona Lisa had an inspiration behind it, as did other famous paintings.

"This is the Dream Mountain.
It is located in a village near Fractured City.
Aysel and I came from there, and this mountain happens to be right beside our house.
It was where we grew up playing, and also the haven that most of us flee to whenever there are beast tides.
I only painted it because it reminds us of home."
"I see," Kent muttered, feeling slightly better hearing the origin of the inspiration behind the painting.
He wasn’t fully satiated, but he seemed satisfied enough to ask a second question.
"Why is one side of it broken off?" The painting in itself was mediocre.
However, the meaning behind it seemed more intriguing if one put their soul into understanding it.
The painting showed that one side was broken off, with debris falling from it.
From his perspective, that detail could have been ignored without changing the painting.
However, adding it seemed to hold some meaning, so he asked.
This time, it was Aysel who answered, "Big sister pushed the bad man off that section of the mountain, and it fell with him.
Very bad man."
Kent turned to the young lady and smiled.
He sensed her sister’s hesitation to answer, so, hearing from Aysel that something personal had happened that triggered her when he asked, he understood.
Because of that, he chose not to ask any further questions.
He gently touched the painting, brushing his hand across the canvas to mimic the brushstrokes.
He closed his eyes and moved his finger a few times as if trying to force out where the feeling was coming from.
Seeing this, Aysel’s big sister furrowed her brow.
"Do you paint?" she asked, paying close attention to how Kent was moving his hand across the painting.
She was a painter, so seeing his hands move made her wonder whether Kent was one too.

chapters.title: Chapter 1470: Longing
paragraphs: As more memories flowed into Kent’s mind, his hand continued to move, adding more details to the painting, making sure every brushstroke gave the image he was trying to bring out meaning.
Aysel and her sister remained rooted in the same spot, their focus fixed on the canvas.
The image was only half done, but even that seemed to have captured their undivided attention, and as more detail was added, that attention only grew.
The details were being poured onto the canvas, and neither Aysel nor her sister could make head or tail of them. To them, the more details being added to the painting, the more beautiful it became.
It got to the point where they even wondered whether there was any need to add more details to the already beautiful painting.
Two hours later, Kent snapped awake, and right then, the last brushstroke was added, bringing the entire process to an end.
He stood up and walked back, making sure his back was facing the painting as he took in deep breaths. This ritual was something Aurelion had always done whenever he was done painting.
He walks back for five minutes, making sure not even his peripheral vision sees what he has painted. This, of course, was only done for paintings. Calligraphy had its own ritual.
Aysel and her sister remained standing, staring at his back throughout the ritual. After five minutes, he turned slowly and looked at the painting.
It was then that Aysel and her sister saw the tears falling down his face.
He walked closer to the painting and brushed his fingers tenderly across the beautiful face of the lady in the painting.
It had been billions of years, but thanks to the memories he had recovered, his longing for his mother persisted, which is evident in his first-ever painting in this life.
The woman in the painting was a beautiful elf who, many years ago, gave birth to the sweet kid who later ruled the universe as the legendary Divine Beast Tamer.
Kent remembered up to the point when Aurelion wrote the first piece of calligraphy that changed the world of Beast Taming.
He once witnessed how inhuman a beast was being treated by a Beast tamer. That ordeal left a scar on his heart, so he swore to do something about it.
It was also that incident that made him switch from painting for others to painting for himself.

Over the years, he had improved upon his painting, creating both good and bad scenes using brushes and paints. He painted many beautiful scenes, which, thanks to his unique talent, could be manifested in real life.
He was what the universe called a Spirit Painter. There were others like him; however, he was one of a kind. His imagination was vivid and all-encompassing.
All his creations were deemed perfect, and so for who knows how long, he had created many masterpieces. However, his big break came when he drew the Beast Tamer calligraphy.
He had tried many times to create a spirited word, one that could bend the will of nature and imprint on divine beasts, but he failed many times.
However, he never stopped, and thanks to the occasional letters his mom kept sending, he always had the inspiration to keep going.
Thanks to her, he had achieved a big goal. A goal that would later shape the universe that nobody saw coming.
So while he had no idea what he had painted, now that he looked at it, and with memories of his past life still fresh in his mind, the emotions of it all were getting to him.
Aysel moved forward and took his hand, hugging it close to her tiny chest. Kent turned and looked at her, allowing a small smile to appear on his face.
Then, to his shock, her sister moved to hug him from the side as well.
Aysel, he understood.
But to think her sister, who happened to be bountiful on the chest, would hug him, giving him all the emotional support there was, he was a bit stunned.
What Kent didn’t know was that while the lady in the picture wore a beaming smile, the brushstrokes added a layer of emotion that even Aysel and her sister felt.

The emotion of longing ran deep in the painting. His gratitude, love, and sadness had been poured into it. He made sure to capture how he felt, and now it seemed others had felt his longing for his mother, too.
Surprisingly, too, in that life, his mom and dad didn’t die like in the previous ones. His memories ended when he became an Immortal King, and through it all, he maintained contact with his parents.
This meant that everything went all right in the end. His parents were still alive, and he couldn’t help but wish that would prove true once all the memories had been recovered.
He might have a mother in this life, or a partial one, all things considered, but that didn’t mean he didn’t wish for his parents from his past lives to still live.
Chaos was born from an egg created by the universe, so he had no parents. Jest didn’t know who his father was, but he knew his mom died the day she gave birth to him as a slave.

He wanted to find his lineage now that he was back to where it all began. But until then, there was also Faceless, who also didn’t know who his father was but was aware his mother allegedly died protecting him from assassins.
As to whether she truly died, since he had never seen a body, he couldn’t confirm it.

Then came the Ruthless Bandit, who lost everything at the hands of those he and his family trusted. He would never forget that, and he would most certainly pay back everyone if there was even a strand of that lineage still alive.
Lastly, Kevin Sage. He knew his mother had abandoned him, so he grew up knowing only his father, who, from the few memories he had of that life, was his inspiration, even if he was a con artist.
He didn’t know if his mother still lived. Of course, even if she did, it wasn’t like Kent would be happy to seek her out. After all, she abandoned him, so in his heart, they were not a family.

So far, all his other lives had lost those closest to them. But this new life seemed to have it the other way around. His parents were super supportive, and those who sought to develop his talent were incredible as well.
The sect he was taken to was the best.
So a part of him wished with every fiber of his being that they still lived to this day. He longed for them, especially his mother, who was both his mentor and his inspiration.
The painting conveyed that longing, and now, as two adorable ladies hugged him, the little resistance he had mounted broke, allowing his tears to flow freely.
He chose not to resist it. This was a moment he never expected, so he allowed himself to be moved by the emotion.
Ten minutes later, he pulled them back and wiped the tears from their eyes. He wasn’t the only one who shed tears.
Aysel and her sister also shed their fair share of tears, mainly from the emotion contained in the painting, but partly also from their own hidden trauma.
"Sorry about that, ladies. I didn’t know I had this many emotions bottled up within me." He pulled Aysel’s sister’s head onto his shoulder and kissed her hair.
"Big brother, Aysel wants to know who this beautiful woman is."
Kent smiled and lifted Aysel into his arms, allowing her to wrap her tiny legs around him. "Her name is Rohesia Amynta, my mother."

chapters.title: Chapter 1471: Fallon
paragraphs: "Wow, Big Brother’s mother is beautiful," Aysel said, her smile spreading all over her face. Kent smiled too, seeing how genuinely she believed in what she said.
Not that he doubted that.

His mother is indeed beautiful, like every other Elf. She was the most beautiful person he knew growing up, and now that he looks at her again, even if through a painting, he knows she was right: his mother is indeed beautiful.
"She is indeed cute, like Aysel."
The little human smiled, but then her face turned solemn. "Aysel is not beautiful. Aysel doesn’t have beautiful princess clothes like the little girls."
She sigh and bend her head down.
She indeed had no proper clothes, which suggested she had no money to keep her appearance on point, as many would.
Kent saw that her sister was also the same. The clothes around her aren’t something someone as beautiful as her should be wearing.
However, despite knowing all this, hearing what Aysel said, he merely smiled and shook his head. "Aysel is beautiful regardless of what she is wearing.
Beauty is not defined by what you are wearing or how you look. At the end of the day, if you have a beautiful appearance but are rotten inwardly, you become the ugliest person."
He paused and brushed her head with his right hand before adding, "However, if Aysel wants princess clothing, I will take her shopping later and buy her all the princess clothes she wants."
"Really?" she beamed with joy.
"Yeah. I may not look like it, but I am actually very rich." Not to brag, but he is rich for someone his age.
"Aysel trusts Big Brother. Also, can we stop and eat first? I am starving."
Kent nodded and set her down. He then snapped his fingers, and a bowl of fruit that he had asked the Tower to prepare appeared.

"You can start with fruit salad," Kent said, and Aysel started to eat. Seeing this, her sister shook her head but said nothing. She was still in Kent’s arms, so she merely smiled, feeling a bit embarrassed.
Of course, she had no idea Kent had long discovered Aysel’s secret. While he is not one hundred percent certain at first, the Tower confirmed Aysel is one of the sins.
He had no idea which sin she was. However, when she kept hammering on about food, he decided to find the right time to see if she is the Sin of Gluttony or if she merely likes food.
Now, watching her eat, he knew which sin she was.

But he said nothing. Mostly, people like this are hidden from the universe because of their unique traits. Many gods, Supremes, and Celestials would not hesitate to refine them and extract their talents for themselves.
A devourer getting the sin of Gluttony will become unstoppable, just as a succubus possessing the sin of lust would become the most dangerous woman to ever meet.
Because of this, he decided not to say anything for now and play along.
He turned and looked at Aysel’s sister, pulling her back slightly. "We haven’t been properly introduced. My name is Jaqen, pleasure meeting you."
"Well met." She nodded, a bit embarrassed, holding hands with Kent. "You can call me Fallon."
"Fallon." Kent furrowed his brow. "You wouldn’t happen to be a phoenix, would you?"
"No." Fallon narrowed her eyes slightly, clearly not expecting that question. "But why did you ask?"
"I once knew a Phoenix called Fallon." Kent didn’t add much context since the Phoenix was from his life as Jest.

Back when Jest left the Whispering Wind Sword Sect to pursue his dreams and also to run from those who sought to get their hands on him because his name appeared on the Sword Dao tablet, he met a demigod Phoenix who saved him from some bad people.
She was also called Fallon. It was a short encounter, but he never forgot her generosity.
Fallon nodded at his answer and turned to look at the painting. Kent also did, letting go of her hand finally.
"You can have it if you want."
"I wouldn’t. This is a painting of your mother; gifting it to me holds no purpose."
"I insist. She is also a painter like you, so keep it."
Fallon turned and looked at him for a few heartbeats before a nod came from her. Although the painting is of importance to him, he didn’t feel like keeping it.
He also had no plans to sell it, so the least he could do was gift it to someone. After standing there for a few minutes, Kent pulled her aside so they could sit and talk.
The store is not that big, but he could tell they lived there. This further made him conclude that they are struggling. So, being the gentleman he is, he knew he had to help.
However, he didn’t want to make it seem like he had pity for them, which was why he wanted to help them.
"I want to join you and Aysel to paint and sell."
"Huh?" She was stunned upon hearing what Kent said.
"Well, I can tell you are passionate about art, even if you are terrible at it."
"Hey, no need to be rude," she pouted and threw a playful punch, which Kent deftly caught and pulled her closer, wrapping his left arm around her shoulder.
"I ain’t looking down on you, Fallon. You actually have the heart of an artist, just not good at the painting aspect.
I, on the other hand, seem to have discovered my love for painting, and thanks to you and Aysel helping me, I managed to bring out my hidden talent.
So I want to paint and sell it with you ladies. This way, we both can make money and perhaps even make a name for ourselves."
Fallon nodded, but Kent could tell she wasn’t comfortable with that. She turned and looked at Aysel, who was busy eating her fill.
"Making money is good. However, I am not sure about the making-a-name part."
He raised his brow and smiled, knowing his chance to come clean and win their genuine trust had come. "Is it because Aysel is the Sin of Gluttony?"
Fallon’s body jerked up, and at once, her aura changed from True Immortal to Immortal Monarch. The paintbrush on the table, four feet from them, flew and turned into a short sword.
She pointed it at him and asked, "Who are you?"

Even Aysel stopped eating and stood up, her expression narrowing at Kent. To his shock, she also happened to be a True Immortal despite the Tower confirming she was only a Root Saint and that her age was merely 18.
Clearly, there was something else at play that even the Tower couldn’t see through. However, he wasn’t worried despite being surrounded by an Immortal Monarch and a True Immortal.
Kent stood up and snapped his fingers, sealing the store using the Soul Universe. He then turned to Aysel and smiled before turning back to Fallon.
"My name is not really Jaqen. Of course, at one point in time, I was known for a while by that name. However, now, I go by a different name."
His appearance started to change. His hair changed from black to the usual purple with strands of red and gold. Then his eyes also changed, taking on a reddish-golden hue.
But it didn’t stop there. His horns appeared, and golden scales lined the sides of his neck. His physique shifted, giving him that dragonkin look.
"My name is Kent Madson. Pleasure meeting you two."
Fallon and her sister, Aysel, widened their eyes, their stances faltering for a moment.

She indeed had no proper clothes, which suggested she had no money to keep her appearance on point, as many would.
Kent saw that her sister was also the same.
The clothes around her aren’t something someone as beautiful as her should be wearing.
However, despite knowing all this, hearing what Aysel said, he merely smiled and shook his head.
"Aysel is beautiful regardless of what she is wearing.
Beauty is not defined by what you are wearing or how you look.
At the end of the day, if you have a beautiful appearance but are rotten inwardly, you become the ugliest person."
He paused and brushed her head with his right hand before adding, "However, if Aysel wants princess clothing, I will take her shopping later and buy her all the princess clothes she wants."
"Really?" she beamed with joy.
"Yeah.
I may not look like it, but I am actually very rich." Not to brag, but he is rich for someone his age.
"Aysel trusts Big Brother.
Also, can we stop and eat first?
I am starving."
Kent nodded and set her down.
He then snapped his fingers, and a bowl of fruit that he had asked the Tower to prepare appeared.
"You can start with fruit salad," Kent said, and Aysel started to eat.
Seeing this, her sister shook her head but said nothing.
She was still in Kent’s arms, so she merely smiled, feeling a bit embarrassed.
Of course, she had no idea Kent had long discovered Aysel’s secret.
While he is not one hundred percent certain at first, the Tower confirmed Aysel is one of the sins.
He had no idea which sin she was.
However, when she kept hammering on about food, he decided to find the right time to see if she is the Sin of Gluttony or if she merely likes food.
Now, watching her eat, he knew which sin she was.
But he said nothing.
Mostly, people like this are hidden from the universe because of their unique traits.
Many gods, Supremes, and Celestials would not hesitate to refine them and extract their talents for themselves.
A devourer getting the sin of Gluttony will become unstoppable, just as a succubus possessing the sin of lust would become the most dangerous woman to ever meet.
Because of this, he decided not to say anything for now and play along.
He turned and looked at Aysel’s sister, pulling her back slightly.
"We haven’t been properly introduced.
My name is Jaqen, pleasure meeting you."
"Well met." She nodded, a bit embarrassed, holding hands with Kent.
"You can call me Fallon."
"Fallon." Kent furrowed his brow.
"You wouldn’t happen to be a phoenix, would you?"
"No." Fallon narrowed her eyes slightly, clearly not expecting that question.
"But why did you ask?"
"I once knew a Phoenix called Fallon." Kent didn’t add much context since the Phoenix was from his life as Jest.

Back when Jest left the Whispering Wind Sword Sect to pursue his dreams and also to run from those who sought to get their hands on him because his name appeared on the Sword Dao tablet, he met a demigod Phoenix who saved him from some bad people.
She was also called Fallon.
It was a short encounter, but he never forgot her generosity.
Fallon nodded at his answer and turned to look at the painting.
Kent also did, letting go of her hand finally.
"You can have it if you want."
"I wouldn’t.
This is a painting of your mother; gifting it to me holds no purpose."
"I insist.
She is also a painter like you, so keep it."
Fallon turned and looked at him for a few heartbeats before a nod came from her.
Although the painting is of importance to him, he didn’t feel like keeping it.
He also had no plans to sell it, so the least he could do was gift it to someone.
After standing there for a few minutes, Kent pulled her aside so they could sit and talk.
The store is not that big, but he could tell they lived there.
This further made him conclude that they are struggling.
So, being the gentleman he is, he knew he had to help.
However, he didn’t want to make it seem like he had pity for them, which was why he wanted to help them.
"I want to join you and Aysel to paint and sell."
"Huh?" She was stunned upon hearing what Kent said.
"Well, I can tell you are passionate about art, even if you are terrible at it."
"Hey, no need to be rude," she pouted and threw a playful punch, which Kent deftly caught and pulled her closer, wrapping his left arm around her shoulder.
"I ain’t looking down on you, Fallon.
You actually have the heart of an artist, just not good at the painting aspect.
I, on the other hand, seem to have discovered my love for painting, and thanks to you and Aysel helping me, I managed to bring out my hidden talent.
So I want to paint and sell it with you ladies.
This way, we both can make money and perhaps even make a name for ourselves."
Fallon nodded, but Kent could tell she wasn’t comfortable with that.
She turned and looked at Aysel, who was busy eating her fill.
"Making money is good.
However, I am not sure about the making-a-name part."
He raised his brow and smiled, knowing his chance to come clean and win their genuine trust had come.
"Is it because Aysel is the Sin of Gluttony?"
Fallon’s body jerked up, and at once, her aura changed from True Immortal to Immortal Monarch.
The paintbrush on the table, four feet from them, flew and turned into a short sword.
She pointed it at him and asked, "Who are you?"
Even Aysel stopped eating and stood up, her expression narrowing at Kent.
To his shock, she also happened to be a True Immortal despite the Tower confirming she was only a Root Saint and that her age was merely 18.
Clearly, there was something else at play that even the Tower couldn’t see through.
However, he wasn’t worried despite being surrounded by an Immortal Monarch and a True Immortal.
Kent stood up and snapped his fingers, sealing the store using the Soul Universe.
He then turned to Aysel and smiled before turning back to Fallon.
"My name is not really Jaqen.
Of course, at one point in time, I was known for a while by that name.
However, now, I go by a different name."
His appearance started to change.
His hair changed from black to the usual purple with strands of red and gold.
Then his eyes also changed, taking on a reddish-golden hue.
But it didn’t stop there.
His horns appeared, and golden scales lined the sides of his neck.
His physique shifted, giving him that dragonkin look.
"My name is Kent Madson.
Pleasure meeting you two."
Fallon and her sister, Aysel, widened their eyes, their stances faltering for a moment.

chapters.title: Chapter 1472: Proving His Identity
paragraphs: If there is one world where Kent’s name will be known by all, then it is the world that gave birth to the first person to immortalize their name on the Sword Dao Tablet.
Jest, popularly known as Lord Genesis, was the first person to be recognized by the Sword Dao, and he came from planet Brymrr.
He had left an impact on swordsmen. So after him, every other name that appears on the Sword Dao Tablet is respected.
Kent is the 14th name to appear on the Sword Dao Tablet, and that is something nobody saw coming, especially when the first 13 were all swordsmen widely known before they appeared on the tablet.
Just like every other world, this one too is looking for him, so the fact that he now stood before Fallon and Aysel with a smile on his face said everything there is to know.
"Prove it."
Aysel said, walking toward Kent. She stopped beside her sister and added, "Prove you are Kent Madson, and we will spare you."
Her nature as the sin of gluttony cannot be known by others, else she would be in trouble. However, Kent Madson is a legend, and so they can give him the benefit of the doubt.

Naturally, this was also their own way of saving their skin. Kent had already appeared on the Three Dao Tablets. This means he has a powerful background. So if he is indeed who he said he is, asking for his help would go a long way.
"How do you suppose I should go about proving myself?" he asked, not particularly bothered. If he wants to leave, with the Soul Map opened, he can simply teleport away.
He is certain they wouldn’t chase after him, not when it would create so much chaos and expose them to more eyes.
Aysel looked at her sister, who gave her a slight nod. She nodded back and walked toward Kent. She extended her tiny arm, her palm facing outward.

"Place your palm on mine and say your name." She narrowed her big brown eyes and added, "If you are who you said you are, nothing will happen to you. However, if you lie, your soul will be devoured in less than a second."

Kent smiled a little, a bit taken aback by her ability. While he is not lying about who he is, the mere fact that Aysel has such an ability made him wonder just what goes into being one of the Seven Deadly Sins.
’She is probably a part-cosmic being to possess such a power that even the Tower can’t see through.’
With that thought in mind, he extended his hand and placed it on Aysel’s. He took a deep breath and spoke the magic words.
"My name is Kent Madson. I have appeared on the Sword, Ice, and Pill Dao Tablets. I have no plans on hurting Aysel and Fallon since I consider them friends."
A second passed, but nothing happened to Kent. This caused Aysel and her sister to narrow their eyes at him. To be safe, she remained vigilant for a few more seconds before Aysel pulled back.
She turned and looked at her sister. "Big Brother is telling the truth. Big Brother is indeed Kent Madson that we heard about."

Kent flashed them the told-you smile. "As I said, I have no plans on hurting you. I am here on a mission, but I am currently in a bind. To get out of it, I need to become popular, and that can be achieved through painting.

I can also tell you that the two of you are hiding from something, or perhaps someone. So, how about we help each other? You allow me to join your team, and in return, I will make sure you and Aysel never have to worry about anything ever again.
You will have a safe place to sleep, and Aysel will have all the food in the universe to eat."

The two sisters turned and looked at each other again. Aysel even moved her head toward the almost empty bowl of fruit. Recalling how delicious it was, her insatiable hunger started to cloud her judgment.
"Why even help us? You have the talent to become popular on your own. You can just buy a few canvases, a few paints, and a brush, and the rest will be magic.
So why bother asking for our help?" She sighed and smiled. "As you said, I am mediocre at best. Before this painting ordeal, I was a collector. I collected paintings for rich and powerful people.
However, now, to survive, I had to channel my love for paintings into making a few spirit stones to live by. I am no painter. I cannot help you in any way, and neither can Aysel, so why help us?"
Kent smirked and looked at Aysel. "First of all, even if I had no reason to help you, I cannot turn away from a loli. She is just too cute that I want to squeeze her in my arms all day long.
Honestly, I don’t know why, but I find myself surrounded by cute little humans like her. They are a bit stubborn, but they are good people. Aysel will fit right in.
Second, knowing she is a Sin means she would always be in danger. Luckily, I happen to have a place where she will be safe for as long as she wishes to stay there."

He turned toward Fallon. "Third, I need your expertise as a warrior. I may not look like it, but I can read people, and you, my dear, are not rainbows and sunshine. I see you have killed your fair share of people. This only means you are a warrior.
I need you by my side. Where I may end up if my plans don’t work out will be dangerous. However, with you by my side, I will feel safe."
His eyes moved toward her chest area, causing Fallon to use her hand to cover the glistening surface of her breasts. "Who knows what else would happen?" Kent laughed, and Aysel laughed too.
Fallon ignored them and adjusted her clothes, hoping to cover the glistening surface of her breasts. After failing a few times, she stopped and turned to Kent.

"The people after us are dangerous. We started this journey with our entire family, but only the two of us are left. Aysel is everything to me, so if allying with you will make her safe, then I accept.
However, be warned, even if you were to put her somewhere she will be safe, as a Sin, she is bound to rub off her bad luck on you. So are you sure you want to become allies with us?"
"Of course. I wouldn’t miss a chance to give Gaia and her band of troublemakers one more friend. Also, I want to know you more, so a little trouble here and there won’t hurt."
Fallon gave him a suspicious look but said nothing.

Seeing this, Kent smiled. He knew what had to be done next. However, before he could take action, his sixth sense flared, causing him to push Fallon to the side just as a dagger grazed his left cheek.
He landed on his left foot, then, using the Soul Map, teleported to Aysel and grabbed her hand.
He wished to pull her away, but before he could move, a dark-cloaked Immortal Lord appeared from the shadows, their dagger humming with darkness.

chapters.title: Chapter 1473: Dark Cloak Assassin
paragraphs: Everything happened so fast that before Kent knew it, he was staring face-to-face with an Immortal Lord who also happened to be a Shadow Legend.
He, on the other hand, was just a Heavenly Ascension stage warrior, and assassination-wise, he was only a Shadow King.

The gap was vast, and he knew that from the get-go. However, with the promise he had just made to protect Aysel and her sister, his grip on Aysel was firm, and his attention on the assassin was unwavering.
The danger was in the air, and so he could not summon anyone from the tower or send anyone in. Even so, he did not panic.
He moved Aysel to stand behind him. Fallon also moved and stood beside him, her expression showing fear.

Suddenly, the assassin let out a low hum. "How moving. To think you managed to evade dozens of assassins over the years, even managing to cross two continents somehow, I am impressed, Fallon... Lord Dove will be proud of you."

"S-Shut up, Vika." Fallon glared dangerously at the assassin, who happened to be a lady, and, judging by how she addressed her, she knew Fallon and her had a past, some of which she had yet to reveal to Kent.

He wasn’t mad about that. He himself had several secrets he would not share willingly, so being recognised by an assassin and also replying to them using her first name seemed normal on a Tuesday afternoon.
"No need to be rude, my dear Fallon. Ever since you left, I have not been able to sleep. It was like you took a part of my heart with you."
As if to add to the drama, Vika clenched her chest as if to show how hurt she was. Unfortunately, her gesture caused the large cloak she had on to wrap around the huge melons on her chest.
Kent saw it, but said nothing.
The look on Fallon’s face twisted into anger; however, she did not attack. This made the assassin lady, called Vika, giggle.
She turned and looked at Kent. "And who might you be?"
"Nobody special. But you can call me Chaos..."
"Chaos. That is a peculiar name for a human." Right now, Kent was back in his disguise.
The moment he sensed danger, the soul universe and the tower worked their magic.
"I get that a lot." He smiled and then cleared his throat. "I figured you are here for this little princess."
"I suppose you can say that. However, if I can get my hands on my favourite collector, I would be very happy."

Kent smiled and moved closer to Fallon, shielding half of her body. This gesture made Vika giggle even more. "How touching. A Heavenly Ascension stage warrior shielding an Immortal Monarch from an Immortal Lord."
She spun the dagger in her gloved hand. "What makes you think you are qualified to stand in my way, human?"
Kent smiled. "Everything, I suppose. You see, I find myself wondering why a Shadow Legend such as yourself would stoop so low as to do someone else’s work.
I have not lived long, but I have seen enough to know that in this life, there is nothing better than freedom. So why hurt two sisters who just want to be free and live their lives?"

She chuckled and replied, "Isn’t it obvious? Life is cruel, and the only way to survive it is if you learn to adapt. 45,000 years ago, I was dying in a ditch, blood oozing from my gut. However, a kind-hearted man saved me and gave me a purpose.
Now, my life, my freedom, is to do his will. So when he asks me to get something done, it will be done. Plus, it isn’t like I want them dead.

This little princess will be shipped to the Supreme Realm, while my sweet Fallan will probably be made into a concubine. It pains me that she wouldn’t be mine, but as I said, this is my freedom now, so I must sustain it for as long as it can last."
Kent sighed.
Right now, he had two ways to save the sisters. Hidden inside his shadows now were his three Soul Warriors.
If he played his cards right, he could save the sisters and even severely injure the lady, but he would also sustain some damage.
The second was whether he could use a shadow-type skill he learned from Faceless’s memories. It would give him 0.2 seconds to teleport the sisters away long enough to enter the tower, maybe.
Both plans would probably fail; however, he knew he had to do something. Of course, he might succeed, for which he would have to give his all to be able to escape long enough to call for help.
Life was on the line right now, so he would not hesitate to call for help.

But then again, there was one last aspect of this that kept bugging him. How did Fallon and her sisters cross over two continents? Even better, how did Vika follow them all the way here if crossing continents was a headache?

Clearly, there was something afoot that he needed to know. Even better, now that he had been recognised and also exposed to Vika’s shadow, even if he ran, as an expert assassin himself, he knew she would always follow him.
Based on the danger, he knew he had to run, but from what he had learned so far, running was not an option, especially when the road was not open as it should be.
Vika had to be taken care of right here and right now.
The only question was, how was he going to do that without dying himself?
"I know you are thinking about several ways to escape from me. I applaud that. Not many people at your level can stand against an Immortal Lord, especially someone like me.
However, while you are probably some kind of genius, know that even if you employ the help of the three hidden in your shadow, you wouldn’t even have a 1% chance of success.
That is because from the moment my dagger grazed your cheek, you had become a part of my domain. But even without that, not even my sweet Fallon can escape.
Right now, with a mere thought, I can render you immobile for as long as I want."
As if to prove a point, Kent suddenly lost control of his body. Even his eyelids were taken over, leaving him unable to move them.
"I may be a Shadow Legend, but I have already formed my domain, or at least formed a part of it. However, that small part is all I need to make you watch as I take them away."
She moved closer and used her dagger to wipe the blood off Kent’s cheek. "I don’t want to kill you simply because you look so innocent.
However, I can make you my slave. Such a handsome lad like yourself would fetch some good coins on the gigolo market."
Vika clearly had control over Kent’s body. She made sure that not even his eyelids could be moved. So for all that resistance to be defied when Kent suddenly moved his eyes, Vika sensed danger.
However, instead of killing him, she found it intriguing that Kent could break a part of her domain.
Fallon could not move either, nor could Aysel. However, Kent moving his eyes and even managing to move his facial muscles to convey his frown caught her attention.
"How did you do that?" she asked, freeing his mouth so he could answer.
"Nothing that can be explained with a sentence. If you are willing, I would like to share a short story with you. That would explain everything."

Even better, how did Vika follow them all the way here if crossing continents was a headache?
Clearly, there was something afoot that he needed to know.
Even better, now that he had been recognised and also exposed to Vika’s shadow, even if he ran, as an expert assassin himself, he knew she would always follow him.
Based on the danger, he knew he had to run, but from what he had learned so far, running was not an option, especially when the road was not open as it should be.
Vika had to be taken care of right here and right now.
The only question was, how was he going to do that without dying himself?
"I know you are thinking about several ways to escape from me.
I applaud that.
Not many people at your level can stand against an Immortal Lord, especially someone like me.
However, while you are probably some kind of genius, know that even if you employ the help of the three hidden in your shadow, you wouldn’t even have a 1% chance of success.
That is because from the moment my dagger grazed your cheek, you had become a part of my domain.
But even without that, not even my sweet Fallon can escape.
Right now, with a mere thought, I can render you immobile for as long as I want."
As if to prove a point, Kent suddenly lost control of his body.
Even his eyelids were taken over, leaving him unable to move them.
"I may be a Shadow Legend, but I have already formed my domain, or at least formed a part of it.
However, that small part is all I need to make you watch as I take them away."
She moved closer and used her dagger to wipe the blood off Kent’s cheek.
"I don’t want to kill you simply because you look so innocent.
However, I can make you my slave.
Such a handsome lad like yourself would fetch some good coins on the gigolo market."
Vika clearly had control over Kent’s body.
She made sure that not even his eyelids could be moved.
So for all that resistance to be defied when Kent suddenly moved his eyes, Vika sensed danger.
However, instead of killing him, she found it intriguing that Kent could break a part of her domain.
Fallon could not move either, nor could Aysel.
However, Kent moving his eyes and even managing to move his facial muscles to convey his frown caught her attention.
"How did you do that?" she asked, freeing his mouth so he could answer.
"Nothing that can be explained with a sentence.
If you are willing, I would like to share a short story with you.
That would explain everything."

chapters.title: Chapter 1474: The Immortal One
paragraphs: "A story?" Vika muttered, using her dagger to brush the side of her cheek that was hidden behind a black mask.

"Do you perhaps think this is a joke? If you don’t know, then I will tell you. A whole Supreme being wants her hands on this young lady. So if you think a mere story would save you from me, then think again."
Kent had a frown on his face simply because Vika threatened to make him her slave. Normally, he would be boiling with anger by now, but he suppressed that fury for Aysel and Fallon’s sake.
Their safety is his priority now.
"Trust me, you are going to want to hear what I have to say. Also, it would be best if you let go of my hands. I have already concluded that I am not your match, so worry not, I won’t try to run."

Kent was hoping Bello, Calix, and Kenna, hidden in his shadow, would come into play when he finally made his move. However, the fact that she saw through his scheme so easily made him forgo that thought.
He didn’t expect Vika to form a partial shadow domain when she hadn’t yet become a Shadow Immortal.
As long as she had that much control, there was no way he could escape from her. So he resolved to use his last move.
Kent felt her hold on him weaken. This allowed him to turn to Fallon. "Relax, everything will be alright."
She nodded and held Aysel’s other hand. Tears flowed down her big brown eyes, a sight that made Kent’s heart ache.
However, while he would love nothing more than to sever every limb on Vika, he had no means for now. For the first time ever, he found himself with no easy way out...
So he began his story.
"Before I begin, what can you tell me about the Seven Mysteries of the assassin world?"
Vika narrowed her eyes as if she wanted to bore a hole through Kent’s soul. However, she replied, "They are the unresolved mysteries that have plagued and still are plaguing the world of assassins.
Over the years, mysteries like the Faceless Assassin, the Shadow Lord, and the Immortal One have driven many assassins mad in the pursuit of their treasures.
Some of the mysteries have been resolved, while some still remain at large."

Kent nodded. "That is indeed true. The Faceless Assassin was one of those mysteries. However, Today, I will be telling you a story of the Immortal One, someone who, to this day, nobody has managed to figure out his mystery, at least that is what many believed."
Vika sighed and was about to call Kent’s bullshit when he spoke, shutting her up.
"Those who seek my techniques must walk the path of death itself. The ghost walks unseen. The blade strikes the heart. The shadow returns from death.
Those were the famous last words of the Immortal One, a second before the Dream King severed his head.

Legend has it that when he was alive, he created three legendary techniques that, for the duration of his life, made him nearly unkillable, just like how, to this day, nobody can beat their chest and say they know what the Faceless Assassin looks like."
Kent sighed and let his words sink deep into Vika’s head before he continued.

"Eternal Ghost Step. A movement technique said to rank among the top five in the universe. Legend has it that, when mastered to a certain level, it can allow an assassin to move between worlds and travel millions of light-years in a single step.
They even said that at his peak, the Immortal One was able to step outside of space and time using the Eternal Ghost Step.

Over the years, this technique has been sought by billions of assassins, yet no one has found it. Nobody has even come close to finding it." A smile formed on Kent’s face, causing Vika to further narrow her eyes and frown.
"Don’t tell me you have it and that if I were to free you, you would give it to me," she sneered and added, "Even if you have it, as long as I make you my slave, I can extract it from you."
"You really should stop threatening me with slavery. Trust me, it is for your own good," he sighed and opened his palm, causing a small rune to appear in it.

"I indeed have the Eternal Ghost Step. In fact, I have all three techniques, and yes, I want to trade the Eternal Ghost Step for the lives of these two and a promise to never come after them ever again."
Vika chuckled, then pointed her dagger at Kent. "I don’t believe you, and I think you are bluffing."
"I don’t lie. Also, if you recognise this rune, it would go a long way in making you believe what I am saying."
Vika looked at the rune again, but clearly, she did not recognise it. Fortunately, Fallon recognised it. "This is the mark of the Midnight Shadows."
Hearing what Fallon said, Vika narrowed her eyes and looked at the rune again. This time, thanks to Fallon, she recognised it too. This made her change her stance against Kent.
"How do you have this mark?" she asked, the aura surrounding her shifting with her words.

"Even if I wanted to, I would not tell you. Trust me, it is for your own safety. However, I can give you the Eternal Ghost Step, and, as I requested, the price is that you let us go and promise not to come after us anymore.
Now, I know you are following orders, but a chance to have such a legendary technique should at least make you compromise.
Your freedom is important, but I believe the freedom to make your own decisions should trump any beliefs you have about whoever you serve now.
Unless, of course, you believe the Eternal Ghost Step is not worth more than your dedication to your master."

Kent waved his hand again, and a contract appeared. "This is a contract that will be enforced by the tainted soul of the goddess of hatred and resentment. If you sign it, it will hold for as long as both of us live.

You cannot come after us, nor would you lead others after us. Going against these words will call down the wrath of the goddess" Kent smiled and added, "Of course, since you can’t kill us, if you want to tag along, I wouldn’t mind. Heaven knows you are going to need a genius like me to help decipher the technique for you."

Inasmuch as he would love to sever her head from her body, Kent could not deny that Vika had what it took to protect him on this journey. Recruiting allies is also part of one’s strength, so if he could kill two birds with one stone, he would not miss the opportunity.
Of course, he also wanted to know more about the organisation she was from and who truly wanted Aysel. To better protect her, it would be good to know more about her pursuers.
The only question was: would Vika accept his offer and sign the contract with him, or stick to her beliefs and attack him?
He used the mark of the Faceless Agents to make her wonder just who Kent really was. This was also his way of telling her that his background was not simple.
She seemed to grasp that, and so she started to wonder about many things. Ten minutes later, a sigh escaped her lips. Then she lifted the hood off her head, removed the mask and smiled.
"Nice story, Chaos... But why should I trust you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1475: Are you hitting on me
paragraphs: "I have to applaud your bravery, Chaos. You have proven to me that even a mortal can face an immortal and not cower like a bug. For that, I, Vika Bin Masha, am impressed.
However, being impressed and trusting you are completely different things. To tell you the truth, I am happy with the life I have now.

I have enough power to roam this world and many worlds out there. I have friends who would come to my aid when I find myself in a bind, and most importantly, I have a backer before whom even gods bow. So why should I even trust you?

If I take Fallon and her sister away like I planned to, my position in my master’s heart will skyrocket, and I know without a shred of doubt that I would gain more than I have now. So basically, I have nothing to lose and more to gain."
Kent sighed, and then he smiled before raising two fingers. "I am now going to threaten you. After that, I will also give you a peaceful reason why you should trust me."
Fallon shifted her head and looked strangely at Kent. She was scared, which was perfectly normal. She and her sister arrived in Snow City two years ago and have been lying low ever since.

They usually had 10 years before they were forced to move. However, this time around, after just two years, they were found. While it was shocking to see that the one who came after her now is Vika, it made her sigh.
She once trusted Vika with a secret, and now, it seems she has used it against her.
In the past, those who came after them were found out by her first, and she made sure to eliminate them before they moved to a different city.
But today, they had nowhere to go. Their only hope was Kent, who seemed to have somehow captured Vika’s attention, only for him to say he would threaten her.
Vika laughed, which, for some reason, made her seem harmless thanks to her beauty. Maybe that was why she wore the mask. She is too good-looking to be an assassin.
"Go ahead and threaten me."
Kent nodded. "First of all, I have to admit you are one beautiful elf. Not many beauties like you would resolve to killing people for a living."
Vika smirked, and Fallon sighed, knowing they were doomed.

"However, since you want to have a reason to trust me, then here we go. My name is not really Chaos. Of course, it used to be my name. As to what I am called now, I won’t tell you, unless, of course, you want to know over a drink, maybe dinner."
Vika narrowed her eyes. "Are you hitting on me?"
"A wise man once said, even in death, one cannot stop shooting their shot."
"Unbelievable... Just who are you?"

Kent laughed and answered, "Nobody special, just the most beloved only brother of a legendary supreme level assassin many call Crimson Dagger. He also happens to be the First Elder of the Midnight Shadows.
I don’t like being associated with him because he is all about one mission after another instead of living life.

Oh, before I forget, I also happen to have a close relationship with the goddess of hatred and resentment. This contract is linked to her, so even if you were to kill me today or, worse, try to enslave me, she would know, and trust me, she will come for me.
Of course, even if you let me go but take these two away, I will just have to call for help, and she will come. I hate to call my brother because he would kill more than he should.
Also, before I forget, I am friends with the Overlord of Hell. That bastard kidnapped me once, but thanks to my brother’s help, he and I are now friends.
Lastly, I happen to know the ruler of this planet. While she hates my guts, if she senses my life is in danger, she would come to my rescue no matter the distance between us.
But then again, knowing her temper, I may end up dead alongside you.
If you don’t believe me, take away your aura, and I will show you that a mere snap of my finger is all it will take to summon gods and demigods."
The smile on Kent’s face grew while the frown on Vika’s deepened.

"Now, to make peace, if you were to help me today by freeing the two sisters, I will use every connection I have to ensure that in less than 1,000 years, you will become a demigod, and in 10,000 years’ time, becoming a god won’t be impossible.
We can sign a blood contract, which I believe will cement my words. In the end, we all want to live and one day reach the peak, so make the best decision that will benefit you the most.

In addition, I will offer my painting services for any request you have. Personally, I want to give you a full-body portrait that will capture every aspect of your being, with no clothes on, obviously."
"Bluffs," Vika said.
"Drop your aura and let’s find out. Of course, I promise you will not die today, even if I summon a god, which I can do, provided you take away your aura."
"What if I do not want to?"
"Then kill me and take them away. Of course, with that, I doubt you will live long enough to deliver them to whoever sent you."
Vika moved close to Kent and took hold of his chin. Their faces were only inches apart. "Who really are you, and why aren’t you scared of me?"

"As I said, I won’t tell you, at least until we get to know each other better." Kent pointed at the contract. "Sign, and we will go our separate ways, or drop your aura and let’s see if I was telling the truth."
Vika took a step back, then she sighed. Afterwards, she turned and looked at Fallon before shifting her attention to Aysel.
"Prove it." She lowered her aura, which instantly made Kent sigh. He then turned to Fallon and Aysel and gave them a simple nod.
"Very well. Everyone, meet Vexthra, the goddess of hatred and resentment." Kent snapped his fingers, a smile playing on his lips.
Vika, Fallon, and Aysel tensed, hoping to meet the goddess Kent was calling. However, even after 10 seconds, nobody appeared. The sisters lost their last strand of hope while Vika grinned.
Kent, on the other hand, frowned. He snapped his fingers again, calling for Miryssa, but, to his shock, even after calling for Avotha, Vargus, and Lene, none of them appeared.
This soured his mood very much. Seeing this, Vika spun her dagger and took a step forward, pressing it against his neck.

"Looks like you are all talk and no action. Fear not, I won’t kill you. After I deliver these two, I will take you to a slave master who would make you mine and perhaps help me extract whatever secret you have."
Kent’s killing intent filled his eyes when he heard Vika threaten for the third time that she would make him her slave.
He wanted to attack; however, before he could will his body to move, a sweet voice came from nowhere and entered everyone’s ears.
"He really hates it when you threaten him with slavery, especially when he was being nice."
Space warped, and from thin air, Vexthra appeared, a smile playing on her lips. "Looks like you have finally met your match, dear."

chapters.title: Chapter 1476: Harmless Prank
paragraphs: The moment Vika laid eyes on Vexthra, she tensed. She could sense with every fibre of her being that the lady who appeared from thin air wasn’t someone she could offend.
She tried to sense her cultivation, but not even a strand of her energy could be felt. She felt like she was a mere ant before her.
But her shock didn’t end there.
Just like how Vexthra appeared, space warped, and Miryssa also walked out, holding a smile on her face. After her, Lene appeared as well, the same smile playing on her face.
The smile was, of course, directed at Kent, whom they decided to prank after he called out to them for help.
Even so, Vika had become pale, her legs losing all energy. She lost her balance, but before she could fall to the ground, Lene appeared behind her, supporting her with one hand.

Vexthra walked toward Kent, and while the latter wasn’t smiling, the goddess who had learned to play pranks smiled and, under the shocked gazes of Fallon, Aysel, and Vika, planted a kiss on Kent’s lips.
After savouring the taste of his lips, she pulled back and made way for Miryssa to have a go at it. Only when both of them had had enough did Vexthra speak.
"Sorry about that, dear, we just wanted to see this look on your face."
Kent smirked. "Wicked vixens. What if my life was really in danger?"
"Good thing your life wasn’t in danger." Miryssa giggled and covered her mouth. Seeing this, Kent made a mental note to punish her when he returned from his mission.

paragraphs: It’s been a while since Kent saw Li Hua.
He had been too busy to be there when she was available. In the past, she emerged from seclusion now and then to spend time with him; however, Kent was either in seclusion or away on a mission.

This was why, after a few times, she decided to become strong enough to spend more time with him. In her eyes, she could only spend more time with her big brother if she was strong enough to protect him.

"Is that right?"
"Yes. This means I will go wherever Big Brother goes next."
Kent smiled weakly, already aware that letting her follow him would not only expose her to all kinds of danger, but her nature as an Atomic Body would be exposed too.
Of course, he could protect her and keep her close. However, who knew the kind of danger that would find him next and how unlucky he would become this time?
"I will take you out for sure. However, for now, why don’t I introduce you to some new friends?" He turned toward Fallon and Aysel. "This is Fallon and her sister Aysel. The other lady is Vika."

"Okay." He set her down. Aysel was already dying to know more about Li Hua, so seeing her chance come, she jumped on the offer and ran off with the tiny human child who seemed to have become one with the shadows.

"That is a bit shocking, considering she started cultivating only a year ago. However, I guess someone with the Atomic Divine Body is already a naturally born assassin. I can’t wait for the day she becomes a Shadow Immortal or even a Shadow God."
"So she is an Atomic Divine Body... No wonder I sensed divine energy from her," Miryssa said with a smile.
Although she is no longer a wielder of a Pure Yin Body, she still has access to Pure Yin Ice, and so she could sense when someone has a specialised physique or constitution.
"People like her aren’t just born, though. They have a mission to fulfil, a mission that mostly concerns the Daos," she added, causing Kent and Vexthra to focus their attention on her.
"What do you mean?" Kent asked.
Instead of answering, Miryssa asked, "When you met her, was she on the run?"
He nodded.
Li Hua was indeed on the run with her grandma when they met.

"From what I know, people born with the Atomic Divine Body are destined to walk the path of the shadows just like every other assassin. However, since she has a divine physique, it means she was born to represent something.
When the day comes, she will embark on a life-or-death trial that will make or break her. I read somewhere a very long time ago that this trial usually comes when they are ascending to godhood.
But thanks to their nature connection to the Dao, fortunes find them. So people try to get their hands on them just so they can use them for their own good"
