It worked perfectly for Kent’s plans, since he would now have nothing to worry about while away.
After leaving them at his mom’s place, he returned to the Mountain Garden to meet the ladies.
Vexthra and Miryssa had already put things in place by the time he returned, so he wasn’t so surprised when he found out Vika had accepted to be his guard.
He knew that with Vexthra taking the helm, there was no way Vika would reject such an offer.
She signed the contract, and Kent transferred the technique as he promised.
"Remember, whenever you face any problem you cannot handle, don’t hesitate to call for help.
Whatever you are training for will take care of itself when the time comes."
Kent nodded to Miryssa’s words, and he got ready to head back with the ladies.
Fallon agreed to go with him, and so did Vika.

Vexthra didn’t reveal what she offered Vika before she accepted to become his guard, but judging from how happy she was smiling with Vexthra and the others when he arrived, he knew Vexthra had gone out of her way.
Lene, on the other hand, was more than happy to go with him.
She had already shown her desire to go with him when he first revealed he would be going to a unique world.
So this was her chance, and she took it with both hands.
"Ladies, be sure to keep him safe.
He may be a monster, but even he needs help.
Also, make sure he doesn’t go chasing every woman he sees.
You three are more than enough to keep him busy..."
They blushed, which was normal considering Vexthra had her hands all over Kent, even in their presence.
But her words spoiled everything, so they could only blush.
"Alright, time to head out.
We will be in touch." Kent nodded and kissed his two goddesses before vanishing away.
After they were gone, Vexthra turned and looked at Miryssa, who smiled and nodded at her.
The two of them vanished and appeared somewhere on Planet Brymrr.
Vexthra used her superior senses to scan the whole of Snow City as if she were looking for something.
A few seconds later, a smile appeared on her face.
"Let’s go." Miryssa nodded and vanished from sight.
Unknown to Kent, his two goddesses had followed him on a mission they had told him nothing about.
He and the three ladies returned to Fallon’s store, where the painting of his mom remained where he had left it seven hours ago.
Lene walked over and looked at it.
"Master, is this your mother?" she asked politely.
While underneath that calm and docile nature lay a beast ready to be unleashed, she always appeared quiet when around people.
"Yes, and you can call me Kent when we are alone.
No need to keep calling me master."
She nodded, but Kent knew she would never do that.
"She is beautiful."
"That she is." While he had no idea whether she was still alive or not, in his heart, she was still alive, so he wouldn’t address her in the past tense.
Vika, already aware of Kent’s real identity, was still struggling to make sense of it.
But for now, she knew the brat before her was the Kent Madson everyone kept searching for.
As for Fallon, she was grateful that Kent finally managed to give them a home where they wouldn’t have to worry about running from their enemies ever again.
They now have literal goddesses protecting them.
"Where do we go next?" Lene asked after having had enough of Kent’s painting.
Kent turned to Vika and asked, "You are an elf, meaning you came from the Elven Continent.
Mind telling me how you managed to cross over?
The last time I checked, you had to be of a certain standing to be able to use the Continental Teleportation Channel.
The other method is a death sentence if not lucky enough."
Even from what Vika said during their standoff, it was clear Fallon and Aysel also crossed two continents to get here.
It seems there is another way that isn’t being discussed.
"Using the channel is indeed difficult to come by, and travelling by sea is dangerous.
The last I heard, a god-level whale had surfaced, and so far, three ships had fallen prey to it.
This has left many worried.
While using the channel is hard to come by, there is a third method available only to key members of society.
These aren’t channels like the Continental Teleportation Channel, but instant teleportation gates that work by activating them using Spirit Crystals.
I came from the Red Diary Assassin Guild, so I have an access token that activates the Teleportation Gate belonging to my guild." She turned and looked at Fallon.
"My dear Fallon here used the token of a merchant she acquired a painting for to travel..."
Fallon nodded.
"Indeed.
When she and those bastards murdered my family and chased after us, I asked for a favour from an old client of mine.
Because she was so pleased with the service I provided, she granted me temporary access.
I can’t use it anymore.
However, as she said, there is a third way, and that is a Teleportation Gate belonging to some prominent powerhouses."
Vika smiled, focusing on the former part of Fallon’s words.
"For your information, sweet Fallon, I never killed any member of your family.
In fact, for what they had done, I have already killed over a dozen who had a hand in the demise of your family.
While I may be the most evil person in your eyes, I see you as my friend, and so I can never bring myself to hurt you or your family."
"How noble," Fallon sneered.
"Aren’t you the same person willing to take my sister from me, knowing full well she would be killed and refined into whatever twisted thing your employers had in mind?"
She took a step forward and appeared before Vika.
"I don’t care about whether or not you have avenged my family.
In my eyes, you people killed my family, and one day, I will get my revenge."
Vika sighed and said nothing.
Lene pulled Fallon away to calm her down while Kent shook his head and smiled. ’Looks like I will have so much drama on this journey.’
Fallon hates Vika, and that is plain from the look in her eyes.
However, while in a way that should have compelled Kent to separate them, he chose not to.
Instead, he listened to what they both said and started coming up with plans to ensure they don’t rip each other’s clothes off.
Not that he would hate to see what is hidden beneath their clothes.
Talk about clothes.
"Why don’t we go have dinner?
Then we can head to the clothing store for a makeover.
We can pick a few canvases, paint, and brushes afterwards."
They nodded and soon left the rundown store, heading to a restaurant Vika had recommended at Kent’s request.

chapters.title: Chapter 1481: Reason why they hate each other
paragraphs: With Vika leading the way, they reached the restaurant she recommended in less than an hour. It was nothing compared to Lord Bimk’s Restaurant. However, it was good enough for them.
Kent’s main aim in bringing them was to learn more about them and also find out more about Fallon’s former profession.

Since she and Vika also seemed to be at each other’s throats, he wanted to address that too before they moved to the clothes store. There are other perverted plans in mind, but for now, he just wants to hear them talk.
Kent had no problem with the clothes he had on. After all, he can change them any way he wants. However, Vexthra said the ladies could use some clothes, so he would take them out to get some.
The food was served, with most of it going to Kent. He didn’t mind eating his fill despite having the means to live for thousands of years without food, and he wouldn’t lose weight.
At the table, he saw how Fallon was eyeing Vika. If she could, she would kill her where she sat.
Kent smiled and asked, "Fallon, why don’t you tell me how you two met? And don’t hesitate to reveal every last thing. Aysel is now safe, so tell me everything."
She sat there for a few minutes, playing with her noodles. In the end, she sighed and started to speak.
"I came from a merchant family. Both my parents are merchants, so you can say it rubbed off on me from a young age.
When I came of age, I started escorting my parents on business trips to many cities and sometimes even to other continents. Along the way, I started to pick up things about procuring goods.

Later, I joined a sect to cultivate and become stronger. In this vast universe, nothing is easy, so I needed strength to back up my ambitions. While there, I met a woman who claimed to be a collector. We became friends, and after 500 years, she taught me all she knew.
So when I left the sect, I decided to become a collector. However, since I had no money to back up my dreams, I pivoted to collecting for people.
In no time, my reputation started to spread. I have an eye for valuable things, and those I collected for were impressed and recommended me to their friends.
That was when I met her master. Initially, I never knew I had gone into bed with monsters."
"Wow, isn’t monster such a harsh word?" Vika feigned hurt; however, Fallon didn’t care.
"If killing people for money doesn’t make you a monster, then I guess I will marry a monster." Her words were rather sharp, something Kent saw struck a chord in Vika’s heart.
She may look calm on the outside, but inwardly, he could tell she was burning with rage, guilty and hurt.

"The first few years I worked for that monster were normal. Along the way, he assigned Vika as my personal guard whenever he sent me to collect on his behalf. We became friends, and over the years, our relationship deepened.

Along the way, I saw her as my best friend." Fallon sighed. "If only I knew the kind of viper she was, I wouldn’t have trusted her with my sister’s secret. But I guess the desperate me wanting a shoulder to lean on resulted in me ending up falling face-first."
Fallon sighed and bent her head down.

She seemed regretful and perhaps guilty about how her relationship with Vika ended. They were indeed best friends back in the day. Now, there is no telling whether that friendship can be fixed, especially after Fallon lost her entire family because of her.
Lene reached for Fallon’s trembling hand while Kent worked on clearing a plate of noodles. Afterward, he turned and looked at Vika.
"Why did you betray your best friend?"
Vika’s expression turned solemn. "I didn’t betray her, at least not on purpose." She tried to look at Fallon, but the latter turned away from her.
"When Fallon told me about her sister, I realized she was the person every last agent in my organization had been looking for.
Ten years before I became aware, a command came from the Supreme Realm. According to the order, the Sin of Gluttony lives in this world, and our job is to find her.
When Fallon told me about Aysel, I did what I do best, making sure all who suspected her were eliminated."

Fallon turned and looked at Vika, who turned and looked back at her. "Yes, your family was under surveillance. It turns out a tiny human had no business eating ten plates of noodles and 15 breadsticks. Some agents received leads that pointed to your sister.

So I killed them. Unfortunately, one of them managed to report to the headquarters before I got to him. When I realised what had happened, I tried to come to you and perhaps help you escape safely. But I was too late.
By the time I reached your home, the deed had already been done. I tried to follow, but my master asked me to help the other agents track you down using the Dream Surveillance cave.
I, over the past years, had done my best to lead them on a wild goose chase. But there is only so much I could do, so don’t blame me too much.
The organisation I work for is indeed responsible for your loss, but I tried my best to help, okay? I am sorry I couldn’t do much."

"As if I will believe any word coming out of your dirty mouth. If you really wanted to keep us safe, why did you then come after us? Or are you telling me, after living thousands of years already, you don’t recognise when you are being used as bait?"
Vika’s eyes widened. "What are you talking about?" she asked, her expression turning ugly.
Lene intervened. "After spending thousands of years leading them to dead ends, they were bound to suspect you, so they sent you instead, knowing you would lead them directly to them.
You care too much about her that you didn’t even notice when you were being used to get to her."
"Impossible. I made sure I covered all my tracks."

"That never stopped them before, did it?" Fallon smirked and turned her head away while Vika bowed in a defeated posture. She clearly didn’t mean to hurt the two sisters, but now that it had been pointed out to her, she seemed to realise her mistake.
"Relax, everyone. The most important thing now is that Aysel is safe. As for those who intend to use you as bait, there is no need to worry about them.

Vexthra had already wiped the tracker they had on you, so you have nothing to worry about. That said, it will be best if you two stop fighting for now." Kent took a sip of his wine and set the glass down.
"After this mission is over, and you still want to rip each other’s clothes off, I wouldn’t mind buying a front-row ticket to watch."
Lene smiled, taking a small chunk of meat and placing it into her mouth. Vika and Fallon gave each other a silent stare before they turned to their food.
After a few bites, they lost their appetite. In the end, Kent ate all the plates, citing that wasting food is not good.
Thankfully, he found the root of the beef between Vika and Fallon. Next, he would work on patching things up in his own twisted way.

chapters.title: Chapter 1482: Shopping Time
paragraphs: After dinner, they decided to buy some clothes. This was Vexthra’s idea, which, now that Kent had heard the root cause of the animosity between Fallon and Veth, he planned to use to help them bond.
Vika proved useful again by recommending the best boutique. As someone who values her appearance, she knew all the best clothing stores in town.
Luckily, it wasn’t that far from the restaurant, so they arrived in less than five minutes. On the outside, it looked grand, and inside, it was even grander.
It was also a pocket dimension, so its size on the outside was nothing compared to what it was on the inside.
"Welcome to the Celestial Wear Boutique. What are we buying today?" A young store attendant approached them with a polite smile as they entered.
Watching the smile on her face, Kent knew she was just being polite. Even so, he didn’t mind and turned to the ladies, but they turned to look at him as well.
Seeing this, he smiled and responded...
"We want to buy some clothes. If possible, we would like to take advantage of the VIP section."
The store attendant nodded and led the way. Although Kent was merely a mortal in her eyes, he walked in with three powerful immortals, so she had no reason to doubt him.
If he were alone, she would have doubted him.

Along the way, the store attendant started to introduce the nature of their store to them. "In the Celestial Wear Boutique, we have a variety of VIP sections. We have options for casual wear, official wear, and even battle wear.

We have thousands of VIP sections, meaning if you enter, the whole place will be for you to use. Also, to ensure privacy, when a customer enters a VIP section, no one else can enter until they leave. It is our way of ensuring the customer takes their time selecting what they want.
It is vast enough that changing to see what fits can be done easily. Trust me, you will have more than enough freedom to select the best clothes.
However, to ensure our time and resources are not wasted, you are required to make a 100,000 spirit stone deposit before you are allowed entry."
Kent nodded and pulled out a storage pouch containing the 100,000 spirit stones. "We want to go to the casual wear section."
She received the deposit and led the way. Three minutes later, they arrived at a door. "Here you go, mister."
She opened the door, making way for Kent and the three ladies behind him to enter.
"Alright, ladies, good luck. I will be picking a few things over there." Kent turned toward the ladies, who instantly wore frowns on their faces.
"Aren’t you coming with us?" Fallon asked.
"Nope. I am not that good with fashion, and since we aren’t really hoping for me to judge outfits, it would be best if I do not come."
"You are coming with us. What if you try to pull a fast one on us and run away before paying for our things?" Lene grabbed Kent’s arm, and before he could resist, she pulled him inside.
Fallon and Vika followed, leaving the store attendant standing there with a smile on her face.
"Nice try, mister, but when it comes to women, we don’t know what we want. Having you around will speed things up a bit."
After sealing the door, she left with a smile on her face.
Meanwhile, Kent and the ladies appeared on the other side of the door, where racks filled with all kinds of clothes lay before them.
"So many clothes," Lene’s eyes sparkled, her hold on Kent tightening. This was her first time inside a clothing store, both in this era and in her past life.

In her past life, she was a slave who died after falling off a cliff. Just like what happened to Uncle Drew a couple of years back, just before she was about to cross over to the land of the dead, the Wraith Queen found her and brought her back.

Later, she became one of her generals. Later, she became one of the sixty-nine Night Riders. In this life, too, she reincarnated as the daughter of a farmer. Before she awakened as a Night Rider, making ends meet was a headache. So, for such a person to appear in a grand place like this was like a dream come true.
Kent smiled. "Go ahead, pick anything you want. I will be seated here to judge if it looks good on you or not." He smirked. "After all, that is my job here, isn’t it?"
"You are so smart, master," Lene giggled and ran off.
Fallon and Vika, on the other hand, seemed to have realised something critical that caused them to narrow their eyes at Kent now that they had the time to think things over.
"You aren’t actually going to sit there, are you?" Vika asked, a suspicious look appearing on her face.
The place where they gestured toward was the changing area.

Kent grinned and turned to face them... "Isn’t this what you all wanted? I was perfectly fine being on my own, but you dragged me here. Now, I have a front-row seat to see what is hidden beneath your clothes."
He took a single step and was seated in the only chair available. There was wine on the table, so he poured himself one and started taking tiny sips.
The two ladies turned and looked at each other, momentarily forgetting their beef. Right now, they have Kent to deal with.
The fact that he would be seeing them naked when they changed into their new clothes wasn’t something they were prepared for.
Unfortunately for them, Kent was not going anywhere.
Seeing him just sit there sipping his wine, something Lene had told them about her master flashed through their minds.
’Master likes women, so if you don’t want to be eaten by him, don’t get close to him.’
When they asked her whether he had eaten her, she smiled and replied, ’Not yet, but soon.’
Lene had already planned to get inside her master’s pants, so she had no problem showing him the sinful body she was carrying in this life.
As if right on cue, Lene walked toward Kent with a few clothes in hand. Seeing the smile on her face, they instantly got a bad feeling.
"Master, I have picked a few clothes. I will change into them, and you can tell me which one you like."
Kent nodded and took a sip of his wine.
Lene turned and winked at the ladies before she started removing her clothes. Kent remained seated, a smile playing on his lips as he watched Lene get naked before him.
To make it even more stimulating, Lene deliberately turned her back to him so that when she bent down to remove her stockings, her cameltoe was fully on display for him to see.
"Nice view, Lene, keep it up."
She blushed but replied, "Thanks, master."
If Selene were around, she would give Lene a high five. She was a good student after all.
She was not at Alina’s level in the ass department, but she had one that would drive any man mad. Her boobs were also large enough that Kent wanted to suck on them.
Lene went ahead and wore the first clothes. They were a casual cotton pair of trousers and a tank top. This was something she would mostly wear inside the tower.
"What do you think, master?" she asked, a smile playing on her face.
Kent smiled and gestured for her to come closer. She obeyed and moved toward him. When she was close enough, he grabbed her ass and had it massaged.
"Good enough, but let’s check the others."
With a blush on her face, she nodded and got naked again, this time her cameltoe much closer to Kent. She knew what she was doing, and Kent, of course, had no plans to fail her.

But aside from that, she also wanted him to make others happy. The relationship between him and the three ladies had deepened after the event in the boutique, so he chose to keep that fire burning.
Lene had grown much closer to her master. While she knew it would happen eventually, now that she had actually done it with him, even if partially, it made all the difference.

There was just no way they would remain at each other’s throats for long...
They spent a couple of hours moving from one store to the next, buying everything he needed.

Kent planned on sharing with the universe a new kind of art. In the past, Aurelion relied solely on his own imagination to bring out the arts. However, his mother started taking him out to see and experience the world.

This helped him come up with more amazing things to paint. While he never truly had more knowledge of the universe until he was taken to the sect, later on, all the art he painted was bought by gods and even higher beings.
That made him rise to become one of the best painters in the universe. He later stopped and decided to focus on using painting to dominate the cultivation world.
But the knowledge was still there, and as someone who had lived many lives, Kent knew there was a lot more to imagine and paint.
Like in the past, Aurelion painted a dangling bridge where, before crossing it, one would have to know the law of gravity.
It was purely out of his imagination, but because he was a spirit painter, that painting was later manifested by a god and was named the Swinging Isle.
To this day, that painting, if not destroyed by the passage of time and deadly battles destroying the universe every era, could still be manifested for cultivators to use to cultivate.
So Kent planned to use knowledge from his past lives to paint some things that even the heavens would be impressed by.

After spending about six hours shopping, they returned to Fallon’s rundown shop. That was where all the magic would happen. Of course, if things started to get out of hand, he would take everything into the tower.

"Master, I will be going to book the hotel room now," Lene said to Kent after they returned. She wanted to raise Kent’s status by using her demigod cultivation base to book the best hotel she could find.
While Vexthra had sealed her cultivation, that seal worked when there was a fight. On a normal day, she could choose to activate it or leave it dormant manually.
Right now, she had left it dormant, so her cultivation was at the demigod stage.
"Alright. Take care and don’t offend any god or supreme being. The last thing we want is to draw attention the wrong way."
"I will be careful, master."
Kent nodded, and Lene started to leave. Fallon stopped her and decided to go with her, but for a different reason.

"I have collected quite a number of art pieces for a collection-owner in this city. Since we will need someone to draw attention to your art, I want to meet her and see if we can come to some agreement."
"Okay. Do you want Vika to come with you?"
"No. I will be fine. Plus, I need the time to clear my mind. I have been worried about my sister’s safety for a very long time. I never had the time to take a break, so I want to be alone this time."
"Good luck then."
The two left together but separated a few miles later, Lene heading east while Fallon headed southeast.
After they were gone, Vika sighed and sat down, a look of pain appearing on her face.
"Are you alright?" Kent asked, seeing the expression that had appeared on her face.

"I am fine. Just that I can’t bear to see Fallon hate me that deeply." A weak smile appeared on her face. "You know, we were best friends. When I travelled with her, I had so much fun. I never expected that one day, a tragic event would shatter the bond we shared."
"It happens. Sometimes, those we trust become so hurt that instead of listening to reason and perhaps seeing things from our perspective, they tap into their anger to draw a conclusion.

I can tell you really like her and that you were telling the truth. However, if you look at things from her perspective, she had lost her entire family, nearly losing the one person that mattered to her the most several times.

Even if she wanted to, there is just no way she can drop everything and return to how you were before everything happened. She needs time to process everything, and once she comes to terms with what you have said, she might start to trust you.
For now, be by her side and let the passage of time do its job."
Vika nodded, feeling a bit better.
Kent decided to use the moment to start working on the paints. He had to mix some of the colours to create new ones, so while he talked with Vika, he slowly worked on that.
As it turned out, Vika was an orphan whose entire family was killed by a god who wanted to have his way with her sister. Just because she refused him once, he killed them all.
She only survived because she was away from home on an errand. When her current master found her, she was moving from one city to the next, doing all kinds of manual labour for food and money.

She took his offer and started training as an assassin under him. Later, she would meet the god who killed her family, only to find out she was a lady and that everything was a giant misunderstanding.
After digging deeper into it, she would find out who the real perpetrator was and why he did what he did just so he could get his hands on her.

She now knows her master was the perpetrator. She just doesn’t know why he killed her entire family. Her loyalty to him was just her way of getting close so that one day, she could kill him and finally avenge her family.
Though deep down, she knew becoming a god so she could kill a god was next to impossible. Now, after meeting Kent, she believes she can rise to that rank one day.
This also means she didn’t come back to take Fallon and Aysel back to her master. She came to save them from her master.

She nodded and started to speak. "Before meeting Fallon, I was a cold-hearted killer who cared little about emotion and only sought to please my master. However, she changed me. The first day I set my eyes on her, something in me clicked.

Initially, Vika thought that now that she had tasted the dragon juice and even touched the beautiful monster, she was safe from all kinds of embarrassment.
However, Selene quickly proved to her that there are things that will even make the goddess of sex blush and feel embarrassed.
"Are you sure you are not secretly a succubus?" Vika asked, a smile tugging at the corner of her lips.
"I am not, my dear. Her name is Adina, and she is a virgin... shocking, right? You would think a succubus as beautiful and seductive as her would have already tasted the forbidden fruit."
"Very shocking."
Selene chuckled, knowing that if Adina were present, she would smack her head for making fun of her situation.
"But while her situation is a bit funny, can you do all we have discussed? Trust me, doing just one will secure you a spot in my Pro Class."

"There is even a Pro Class?" Vika was surprised this time. While her travels had revealed so many things to her, what she had learned from Selene now contained more than she ever thought was possible. So to think there was more left to know...
"Sex is a field of study that has been explored many times in the past. If you want to know more, then you must prove yourself. Lene is my second student, so you might just be the third."
"Who is the first?"
"Her name is Indie. Fun fact, she is actually the Queen of the entire Underworld."
"Just who are you, people?"
Selene grinned. "We don’t have a collective name yet, so for now, you can just call us the Dragon Harem."

sentences.text: "Fallon really hates me, right?"
Vika suddenly asked.
She was quiet for a while, watching him mix the paints.
Now, it seemed her focused thoughts were interrupted by the thought of Fallon hating her.
Although Kent had already told her to relax and let time do its work, she just could not stop thinking about the bond they once shared.
Their friendship was ruined, and while they bonded over Kent’s dick and yang qi, that connection they shared in the past wasn’t there anymore.
The trust Fallon had for her, which was the reason why she even told her about Aysel, wasn’t there.
This pained her deeply.
Kent turned and looked at her for a few moments before a smile appeared on his face.
"You really love her, huh?"
"I do," she replied without any hesitation.
"Tell me about your friendship."
She nodded and started to speak.
"Before meeting Fallon, I was a cold-hearted killer who cared little about emotion and only sought to please my master.
However, she changed me.
The first day I set my eyes on her, something in me clicked.
All of a sudden, I found myself falling deeply in love with her.
Of course, it wasn’t the kind of love you expect.
I just wanted to be close to her always, and for years, I got that.
Because of her, I started feeling like a normal person again.
She taught me how to smile again, and for years she made me belong."
A painful smile appeared on her face.
"She once told me she would marry a powerful cultivator who could take her roaming the entire universe, collecting art.
Back then, my response to her words was that I would either become her servant or seduce her man and become her sister.
She just laughed, but I knew she wouldn’t mind the latter.
In the end, however, she lost everything mainly because I wasn’t fast enough.
If I had killed that bastard fast enough, word wouldn’t have reached headquarters.
Because I was slow, she lost 17 members of her family, every last one of them people I smiled with, talked with, and dined with.
I am such a terrible person, Kent." Tears started flowing down her face.
Kent abandoned his work and moved to her side.
"Hey, hey, look at me." He used his hand to lift her chin, accidentally leaving red paint there.
"You are not a terrible person, Vika.
From what you just said, it was plain you love your friend and did what you could to protect her.
Even now, while you knew she was safe and sound, you didn’t reveal to her why you came back.
You still want to protect her.
That is a sign you love her more than yourself.
I know Fallon also sees that, but sometimes grief has a way of making us see what we want to see.
Hating you makes things easier for her, so don’t take it to heart.
She will come around eventually.
The only thing you can do now is wait for her to come to terms with everything."
Vika nodded, feeling a little better.
"Thank you, Kent.
I feel a bit better now, so you can go back to mixing your paints.
I will use the time to go through the technique you’ve transmitted to me."
"About that," a guilty smile appeared on Kent’s face, "I may have accidentally painted your face red when I cupped your cheeks, so you have to clean up first."
Vika brushed her cheek with her hand to confirm.
"Wow." She wanted to get mad at him, but she stopped herself and just smirked.
"Relax.
The time inside the tower runs faster than the time here, so you will only be gone for a few minutes even if you spend hours there."
"Fine.
Just make sure you don’t trap me there."
"The tower will send you out when you are done.
Just tell her you are done, and she will handle everything."
She nodded and was taken away by the tower at Kent’s behest.
She appeared before the Love Pool inside the Harem Tower.
When her eyes landed on the majestic pool and everything around her, a look of astonishment appeared on her face.
She was about to say ’wow’ when a presence appeared behind her.
She jumped forward and, as if by design, she stepped onto the edge of the pool.
This caused her to trip and fall face-first into the water.
She immediately forced her head out of the water to see who had scared her.
"Hi."
Selene waved before she also jumped into the water, arriving before Vika.
"My name is Selene.
What is your name?"
"V-Vika," Vika stammered, not because she was scared of Selene.
That would be ridiculous, considering Selene is merely a Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator while she is an Immortal Lord.
While she was suppressed, she still had her Immortal Lord experience, and even better, she could still use the shadows as she could while at the Immortal Lord stage.
So she had no reason to fear Selene.
However, looking at the smile on her face, something deep within her kept telling her she should be careful around her.
"Are you one of the fine ladies travelling with Kent?"
Vika nodded.
"Pleasure meeting you, Vika.
I believe you and I are going to be best friends."

chapters.title: Chapter 1488: Meeting a Client
paragraphs: An hour later, Vika returned with a small blush on her cheek. Since only an hour had passed on the outside, it meant she had spent a day inside the tower.
Kent was done mixing the paints and was brainstorming what to paint first.
When he saw her appear, a smile tugged at the corner of his lips. She tried to hide it from him, but she failed terribly.
"Let me guess, you met Selene."
"H-How did you know?"
Kent chuckled, "Selene tends to have a certain effect on people. Looking at how embarrassed you are now, there is no doubt she was the cause."
"She is so shameless in a sweet kind of way."
"That is my Selene. None of us truly knows what goes on in her head. Just that when it comes to being shameless, she is second to none."
Kent didn’t even know where her shamelessness came from. When they met, she was the shy type, making herself scarce so that she wouldn’t fall for him.
Kent was still green back then, so he felt like she wasn’t interested. However, after tasting the forbidden fruit, her personality flipped.

She not only made it so her sister Neomi would join her in the harem, but was also behind the sudden downfall of most of the women in the dragon harem. Because of her, most of them did things they never knew they were capable of.
Even Vexthra had to give it to the shameless Saintess; she is one of a kind.
"I will be sure Fallon stays far away from her. Who knows what she would do to my sweet collector?" Vika laughed, then focused on the blank canvas.
"Are you coming to paint?"
"Yes. I am just putting some things together first."
"Then I will not disturb you."

She sat back and started staring at him. Kent knew his first art would determine how long he would stay in Snow City. With three powerful ladies by his side, even crossing the sea using a ship was possible.
However, if he could use the teleportation channel or, even better, the teleportation gates, which he had just discovered existed, it would go a long way.
It’s been a long time since the universe has seen a Spirit Painter. Now that he is back and with a mission in mind, he will take the universe by storm again.
After sitting there for ten more minutes, he lifted the brush and started to paint. It would take some time, but with the experience he has under his belt, he has nothing to worry about.

Meanwhile, after Fallon left, she made her way toward the busiest part of the city, where the various activities were rather chaotic. Her destination was an antique store where artefacts from several eras were on display.

While she only collected paintings, there were those who collected all kinds of stuff. This particular client was one for whom she had collected quite a sum of paintings, some of which nearly cost her life had it not been for the people she worked for coming to her aid.
In the world of collectors, the competition was rather severe. A slight mistake and not only would the item be taken off their hands, but it could also be taken from their bodies, too.
When she got to the store, as expected, it was packed with admirers who came from far and beyond to look at the items on display.
While some people chose not to show their collections, most didn’t mind. Some even went out of their way to sell the item at many times the price they bought it for.
Fallon merely collected for others, so she had no business with what they did with whatever she got for them.
Seeing the long queue, she only stopped for a moment before she started walking toward the entrance.
"Hey, lady, can’t you see we’re all in a queue?" The people in the queue started to complain; however, Fallon didn’t even bother to look at them.
"What a bitch. If not because leaving this queue would send me back even more, I would have snapped her neck to put her in her place."
"Same here."
The more she walked forward, the more their curses increased until suddenly, they all stopped.
"Welcome, Lady Fallon," the two Immortal Lord guards at the gate bowed when Fallon approached them.
This sight made everyone who insulted her tense.
They had no idea she was someone important. But even if they didn’t know, just the fact that Fallon moved forward with her back held high was enough reason to tell everyone she wasn’t here like them.
Now, looking at her back, fear and panic started to set in. In their minds, she could easily tell on them, and they would be sacked and even banned from entering the store ever again.
Thankfully, after talking to the guards for a few seconds, one of them took her inside.
The other one arrogantly smirked. "The items many of you are about to see were collected by the fine lady who just entered. In the future, learn to show some respect."
Those who feared they would be banned exhaled, feeling like they had jumped the gun. If only they knew they still stood in the queue simply because Fallon chose not to make enemies this time.
In the past, she wouldn’t have hesitated to use her standing to expel the people who rained curses on her. Now, with a god and his minions after her, she knew keeping a low profile was paramount.
Aysel may be safe now, but that doesn’t mean she would call attention to Kent and her new companions.
She was led up the stairs by the guard, and after a few minutes of climbing, they came to a stop in front of a golden door.
The guard knocked, and a voice came from inside.
"Let her in."
"My lady, you can enter."
"Thank you, Sam." The guard opened the door, and Fallon walked in.

"Glad to see you are still alive, Fallon. The last time I tried contacting you, I was told you and your family no longer lived on the Elven Continent," an elven lady said, sitting behind a desk with a round pair of eyeglasses suspended on her nose.
She looked so down-to-earth that one would mistake her for a mortal; however, she was actually a demigod.
Fallon said nothing and only sat down on the chair she was given. The demigod lady sighed and decided to change the topic.
While she started by asking where she had been, as someone who valued the safety of her workers, she had already become aware of Fallon’s predicament.
The only reason she said nothing or did nothing was that against a god, even she was powerless. Also, she was not a martial cultivator, so offending a god was the last thing she wanted.
"Hope you are well."
"I am fine, Lady Annette," Fallon answered.

While she had expected Lady Annette to at least offer her help back when she was in need, she also knew Lady Annette had no obligation to aid her, not when their relationship was the type that ended at ’find an item, and I will pay for your service.’
"I am here with business, like always," Fallon said before taking out the painting of Kent’s mom. The moment Lady Annette’s eyes landed on it, her entire body shook.

chapters.title: Chapter 1489: Sweet Deal
paragraphs: "Where did you get this?" Lady Annette asked, her greedy eyes locked on the painting. The beauty of it all, and the fact that just looking at it fills her heart with all kinds of emotions, deepened her desire to own it.
No collector would look past such a beautiful painting.
Fallon smirked and put the painting away before this greedy bitch would snatch it off her hands.

"I have taken on a client who paints. This is his first work, which he completed in under two hours. I am here because he wants to dominate the world of painting, and to do that, people like you are needed.
He will provide the painting, you will display it, and spread his name. Of course, you can also purchase it, which will become yours, and you can do with it whatever you desire."
"I am not declining what you said; however, wouldn’t it be better to just auction it?"
"Auctioning it would indeed spread his name. But that would be for the ordinary folk. He has no qualification to place an auction in any of the S-Tier auction houses."
"But I do," Lady Annette smiled. "Because of my reputation, I can place an item there."

"Yes. With your connections, you can easily put one of his paintings on sale at any of the S-Tier auction houses. I know you and Lady Tilly are more than just friends. Using her auction house wouldn’t be too bad."
Lady Annette blushed but said nothing.
She sat there and began analysing what Fallon had just said. In her mind, there was no harm in using her services to sell a painting if it meant she herself would have her name spread far and beyond.

She had been in the game for long enough that she could tell when someone was trying to break into the scene. This meant that since his name was not yet known, she would have the privilege of making him famous.
Once he became famous, his name would be tied to hers, which in this regard would make her own avenue famous.
But there was a downside, which had to do with whether or not the person she would be dealing with would be able to remain consistent and provide when requested.
A god or many gods might fall in love with his painting, and they would want some. What then was the guarantee he would be able to provide? The last thing she wanted was angering gods.

"I would have to see three more paintings from this person. If I like them, I will ensure that one of his paintings is auctioned within the next week. The other two will be displayed here for all who want to see.

Though I will advise you to hurry. The Annual Wealth Auction is just two weeks away. If what you bring me is enough to make me happy, I might even throw in a VIP ticket for you and whoever you can bring."
A smile formed on Lady Annette’s face, causing Fallon to narrow her eyes. She knew the lady before her wanted to say something, but she wanted her to ask first.
"Just spill it, Lady Annette."
Lady Annette giggled and said:

"I even learned that one of the Spirit brushes will be auctioned this time around. Now, while I am not certain, I can tell this painter of yours may be a spirit painter. Now, I am sure they would love to have such a weapon."
Fallon narrowed her eyes further as she stood up. "I will make sure my client hears your request and gets back to you. Be sure to stay close to your communication."
Fallon stood up and started to leave. When she reached the doorstep, she turned and looked back at Lady Annette. "I wasn’t here, and you most certainly have never been in contact with me."
Before she could say anything, Fallon vanished into thin air, her presence completely erased. She used the tower to move since Kent had granted her permission to enter and leave as she pleased.
After she was gone, Lady Annette picked up a communication jade token and called someone. A few rings later, a lady spoke from the other end.
"Make it quick, Annette. I have an auction to prepare for."
"No need to be uptight, Tilly. I just wanted to tell you I may have found a potential Spirit Painter, so that brush mustn’t be auctioned."
"A Spirit Painter?"
"Yes. I am yet to confirm, but I am 80% sure, and when confirmed, I will come to you first. So maybe take out the brush from the line-up and also reserve one more slot for me."
"I will not take out the brush since it was given to me by a god. But I can reserve a slot for you."
"Tch, why did I even bother to ask?" A frown appeared on her face, but quickly went away. "Fine, just be ready to process everything hastily when I come to you."

She hung up and took a deep breath. She planned to use her superior senses to follow Fallon and see if she could find the person she works for much more quickly. But the sneaky lady just vanished into thin air.
"Don’t disappoint me, Fallon."
Two hours had passed since Kent had started painting. Fallon had already returned to his side. After leaving Lady Annette’s office, she entered the tower and appeared inside the Mountain Garden.
Once she appeared there, the tower brought her back to her store.
She joined Vika to watch as one detail after another was added to the painting, gradually bringing it to life. An hour and a half into it, Lene also arrived using the same method as Fallon.
She joined them, and a few minutes later, Kent stopped and turned around, making sure none of them saw what he was about to add to his painting.

They saw he was painting an eye; however, he hadn’t added the pupil yet. This made them wonder why that was the case. After all, from what they could sense from the painting, it wasn’t something simple.
Its profoundness was just too vast for them to make sense of. Maybe that was because it wasn’t complete yet. But even so, they couldn’t help but wonder why he turned away from them.
In the end, to not disturb him, they chose to wait for him to finish.
Thirty minutes later, the painting started to glow. Lene immediately waved her hand, creating a dome around the store to shield the light. The last thing they wanted was to create a scene.
Thankfully, the light only lasted for two minutes before dispersing.
Kent then stood up and walked away, his back turned to the finished work. Five minutes later, he turned back and looked at his work, bringing a smile to his face.
Of course, while he made it look like he was smiling, what he was looking back at was a bit scary. A few seconds later, he shielded his eyes and gestured for the ladies to turn the painting around.
Lene moved and held his hand. "Are you okay, Master?"
"I am fine. It is just the success of my painting that caused me to nearly injure my soul."
"Success?" Lene moved him to sit down first before she walked toward the painting. A few steps in, she stopped when she saw the pale looks appear on Fallon and Vika’s faces.
"Turn it away from them."
Lene obeyed and turned the painting away, causing the two ladies to gasp for breath. They both turned and looked at Kent, their expressions changing.
The dragon merely smiled.

Now, while I am not certain, I can tell this painter of yours may be a spirit painter.
Now, I am sure they would love to have such a weapon."
Fallon narrowed her eyes further as she stood up.
"I will make sure my client hears your request and gets back to you.
Be sure to stay close to your communication."
Fallon stood up and started to leave.
When she reached the doorstep, she turned and looked back at Lady Annette.
"I wasn’t here, and you most certainly have never been in contact with me."
Before she could say anything, Fallon vanished into thin air, her presence completely erased.
She used the tower to move since Kent had granted her permission to enter and leave as she pleased.
After she was gone, Lady Annette picked up a communication jade token and called someone.
A few rings later, a lady spoke from the other end.
"Make it quick, Annette.
I have an auction to prepare for."
"No need to be uptight, Tilly.
I just wanted to tell you I may have found a potential Spirit Painter, so that brush mustn’t be auctioned."
"A Spirit Painter?"
"Yes.
I am yet to confirm, but I am 80% sure, and when confirmed, I will come to you first.
So maybe take out the brush from the line-up and also reserve one more slot for me."
"I will not take out the brush since it was given to me by a god.
But I can reserve a slot for you."
"Tch, why did I even bother to ask?" A frown appeared on her face, but quickly went away.
"Fine, just be ready to process everything hastily when I come to you."
She hung up and took a deep breath.
She planned to use her superior senses to follow Fallon and see if she could find the person she works for much more quickly.
But the sneaky lady just vanished into thin air.
"Don’t disappoint me, Fallon."
Two hours had passed since Kent had started painting.
Fallon had already returned to his side.
After leaving Lady Annette’s office, she entered the tower and appeared inside the Mountain Garden.
Once she appeared there, the tower brought her back to her store.
She joined Vika to watch as one detail after another was added to the painting, gradually bringing it to life.
An hour and a half into it, Lene also arrived using the same method as Fallon.
She joined them, and a few minutes later, Kent stopped and turned around, making sure none of them saw what he was about to add to his painting.
They saw he was painting an eye; however, he hadn’t added the pupil yet.
This made them wonder why that was the case.
After all, from what they could sense from the painting, it wasn’t something simple.
Its profoundness was just too vast for them to make sense of.
Maybe that was because it wasn’t complete yet.
But even so, they couldn’t help but wonder why he turned away from them.
In the end, to not disturb him, they chose to wait for him to finish.
Thirty minutes later, the painting started to glow.
Lene immediately waved her hand, creating a dome around the store to shield the light.
The last thing they wanted was to create a scene.
Thankfully, the light only lasted for two minutes before dispersing.
Kent then stood up and walked away, his back turned to the finished work.
Five minutes later, he turned back and looked at his work, bringing a smile to his face.
Of course, while he made it look like he was smiling, what he was looking back at was a bit scary.
A few seconds later, he shielded his eyes and gestured for the ladies to turn the painting around.
Lene moved and held his hand.
"Are you okay, Master?"
"I am fine.
It is just the success of my painting that caused me to nearly injure my soul."
"Success?" Lene moved him to sit down first before she walked toward the painting.
A few steps in, she stopped when she saw the pale looks appear on Fallon and Vika’s faces.
"Turn it away from them."
Lene obeyed and turned the painting away, causing the two ladies to gasp for breath.
They both turned and looked at Kent, their expressions changing.
The dragon merely smiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 1490: Demon Heart Gaze
paragraphs: "What is wrong?" Lene asked, a bit worried.
Seeing Vika and Fallon turn pale at the sight of a painting made her worry. But the fact that Kent even seemed affected by it took her aback.
She looked at the painting, and all she saw was a green eye with a red pupil. At first glance, she knew it wasn’t an ordinary painting. However, the reaction that made the ladies pale wasn’t present.
She knew they had seen something, so she wanted to know what. But regardless of how she looked at it, she saw nothing that should freak her out.
"I have sealed it, Lene, so it wouldn’t work unless you channel your energy into it," Kent said, standing up with a tired look on his face.
"What is it, Master?"
"I call it the Demon Heart Gaze. It is a spirit painting that tells whether someone has a heart demon. All you have to do is look into the eye, and you will see your heart demon."
"Does Master also have a heart demon?"
"Yes. I’ve always had a heart demon, even during my life as the ruthless bandit. However, if we succeed on this mission, then I will be able to kill it before it defeats me."
Lene moved and hugged Kent.

In her eyes, a heart demon was the most dangerous thing a cultivator could ever experience. It could easily kill or, worse, cripple the cultivator. So learning that her master had a heart demon made her afraid.
"Relax, Lene. I am certain it wouldn’t be long before this heart demon is dealt with." Kent said in a comforting tone before he snapped his eyes and looked at Fallon and Vika.
"However, you two now have a decision to make. Just now, you saw your heart demons, and they are each other...right?"
They said nothing, but their expressions told Kent what he needed to know.
"Fallon, your heart demon is Vika, and Vika, your heart demon is Fallon."
They nodded, and Vika asked, "But how? It isn’t like I hate Fallon or want to kill her. She is my friend... My best friend."

"I know that. However, you blame yourself for what happened to her family, even though none of it was your fault. You care about her opinion of you so much that you decided to look down on yourself and blame yourself for something you shouldn’t be blamed for.
Because of that, you have developed a heart demon that, now that I know what happened between the two of you, I can boldly say keeps making you doubt and blame yourself."
Fallon’s eyes widened.
She turned and grabbed Vika’s hand, the look of guilt appearing in her eyes. "It is not your fault, Vika, so stop blaming yourself."
It was clear she wanted to help her friend now that she knew she had a heart demon.
"I am afraid it is not that simple, Fallon." Kent’s words snapped her attention back to him.

"What do you mean? You already said the reason why she formed a heart demon was that she keeps blaming herself for what happened to my family. So if she stops blaming herself, won’t that solve the problem?"
Kent smiled. "It wouldn’t. That is because heart demons are hard to kill. Hers was formed because she keeps blaming herself, while yours was formed because you hate her for no reason.

Deep down, you knew she wasn’t at fault. However, to make your life easy, you decided to blame it all on her. In your soul now is a version of Vika that wants you to keep hating and blaming her, while inside her is a version of you that wants her to keep blaming herself.
To destroy these heart demons, you must each confront your version of the heart demon inside each other’s souls. Vika would have to confront yours, and you would have to confront hers."
"How do we do that?" Vika asked, feeling Fallon’s grip tighten on her. She smiled inwardly because she could feel the friend she once had now seemed to have returned when she heard she was in danger.

"Heart demons are insidious. They would never reveal themselves so they can be dealt with easily. They hide and strike when you are vulnerable. They are indeed the most dangerous fiends a person could ever face.
However, now that we have identified the source of your heart demons, killing them can wait. I have to set up a formation, which at my current speed will take me two years.
I don’t have that much time now. But even if I did, considering time runs differently inside the tower, you don’t have to worry about your heart demons growing stronger.
In fact, if you two can do away with the animosity between you, it will weaken them. This will make it easy to confront and win when I set up the formation."
They nodded, feeling a little better.
"You have nothing to worry about, ladies. I wouldn’t let any harm come to you."

They nodded again. Fallon hugged her friend and apologised. Of course, it will take more than an apology to weaken their heart demons. However, since they have more time to spend together anyway, they can start to rekindle their friendship.
Fallon proceeded to tell Kent the outcome of the meeting she had mentioned with the collector.
"Three paintings, huh. I can do that in less than a day."
"Also, I don’t know whether it is a coincidence, but she said they will be auctioning a spirit brush at the annual auction."
"Really, did she say which spirit brush it was?"
"No. She only said that if you can produce three paintings, she will help with a VIP ticket to the auction and even promised to put one of your paintings up for auction under her name.
Of course, your painter’s name will be announced to all who would come to the auction."
"Sounds like a good thing to me. I guess I’d better add two more paintings to it then."
Fallon turned to Vika before they both turned to Kent. "We want to go back to the tower for a while."
Since the time difference is vast, they wanted to take advantage of it to catch up and see if they could handle the heart demons they’ve formed.
Kent gave them the go-ahead, and they left.
After they were gone, Lene jumped into Kent’s arms and planted her face on his chest. After hugging him for a few minutes, she pulled back and looked at the painting...
"You really knew what you were doing, huh, using a painting to reveal what had been right before them all this while. That is genius."
Kent smiled and grabbed Lene by the ass, lifting her into his arms. She wrapped her slender legs around him and smiled.
"They needed to see the danger they are in. Also, I wanted to see how Fallon would react when she learned Vika was in such danger because of her."
"I suppose she reacted as you expected."

"Indeed. She really cares a lot about their friendship. It was her heart demon that kept her stubborn all this time. But now that she knows what is on the line, I am sure the next time we see them, there will be a profound change in their friendship."
"And all this is done from a mere painting." Lene stared inches away into Kent’s eyes before adding, "What is the next thing you plan on painting?"
After sharing a kiss, Kent returned to painting.

chapters.title: Chapter 1491: The Eleventh Floor - Four Fallen Immortals (1)
paragraphs: After spending a few hours on Planet Brymrr, Vexthra and Miryssa returned to the 10th floor of the planet’s Killer Dungeon.
They said nothing of what they went out to do, aside from informing them that Lene will not be joining them anymore—at least for the duration of Kent’s mission on Planet Brymrr.
After that, they prepared to leave for the 11th floor. They still have 27 floors to go, and thus far, they have already started meeting True Immortals.
Vexthra knew it was only a matter of time before demigods and gods started popping up.

So she wants them to train much faster and, hopefully, when the danger starts appearing, even with their low cultivation base, they can handle it. Already, most of them had long surpassed the strength Heavenly Ascension Stage cultivators should have.
The limits they are breaking and the innate talents they keep awakening seem to keep pushing them to grow stronger than they should be.
If this streak continues for another five floors, then there will be no telling the kind of monsters they would become.
"Alright, since we are all ready, we should move to the next floor." She opened the portal, and they all walked in.
As usual, Vexthra was the last to enter before the portal closed. When she appeared on the 11th floor, she found herself standing with three others: Kaizo, Sylara, and Indie.
"Where are the others?" Kaizo asked, looking around. The others mirrored his action, except Vexthra, who held a calm expression, though deep within, she wondered why she had been suppressed again.

’A True Immortal again, huh?’ A smile appeared on her face even though she knew death in this form was possible. Although at heart she is still a god, now that she has been suppressed to the rank of a True Immortal, if she is dealt a deadly blow, she would die.
But instead of feeling fear, she felt more alive. The fact that she can contribute like her sisters could make her happy.
"Looks like we have been divided into teams for different missions." The moment she said that, the details of the mission appeared, and it was shared with everyone.
⟦Name: Planet Killer Dungeon⟧
⟦Floor Name: Four Fallen Immortals (11th)⟧
⟦Power Level: True Immortal -- Immortal Lord*⟧
⟦Description:
↠ Long before the climax of the Chaos Wars, a great battle was fought between the heroes of the Celestial Dream Sect and the four Chaos Envoys who later became the four fallen immortals
↠ Before the Chaos Beasts invaded this universe, they sent their envoys, beings born from the primal chaos, wielding absolute control over the true essence of Chaos Qi.
↠ Their mission was to create chaos in this universe, drawing all attention from the real invasion.
↠ The four Chaos envoys found themselves in the Celestial Dream Sect, where for 20 straight hours, a great battle was fought.
↠ In the end, every last being was slaughtered by the four Chaos Envoys. Their power was so great that even when faced with the overwhelming forces of the sect, they emerged victorious.
↠ However, despite winning, their rampage was destined to end at the sect grounds. In the end, the heroes won, but at the cost of everything they had.

↠ The four Chaos envoys were trapped by the Grand 616 Arcane Formation. This formation, powered by the chaos energy flowing through their veins, had held for billions of years, sealing the four Chaos envoys away.
↠ The world lived on since then, and for billions of years, it had a semblance of peace. The sacrifice of the heroes didn’t go to waste in the end.

↠ However, just like every good story, 200 years ago, the unthinkable happened. In pursuit of claiming absolute power, some zealots broke the formation that held the four Chaos Envoys, creating a chain reaction that promises to devour the entire world in a few years if not handled.
↠ Your mission comes in five phases.
1. Kill Draxion – The Undying Commander.
2. Kill Selvara – The Crimson Valkyrie
3. Kill Gorath – The Mountain Breaker
4. Kill Velmora – The Ghost Strategist
5. Kill all 200 Agents of the Soul Temple. For this mission to be considered a success, be sure to prevent any member from sending out any distress signal to the soul temple.

↠ Your team has been divided into five. Each must execute their mission with absolute precision. Failure to get this mission done will result in catastrophic consequences that this world is not prepared for.
Rewards
↠ 120 Billion Tower Points
↠ 1.2 Trillion Soul Essence
↠ Limit Breaker Key (Everybody)
↠ Innate Talent Awakening Pill
↠ Soul Ascension Fruit
↠ Chaos Heart Stone (x4)

Vexthra and her team of three took a deep breath after reading the description of their mission. "Looks like things will be much more perilous than the previous ones," Kaizo said, feeling like this mission would perhaps be the most dangerous one yet.
Of course, he is ever prepared for what is to come. In fact, he is more than happy to get things going.
Indie and Sylara knew the kind of person Kaizo is, so they said nothing to him and instead turned to Vexthra.
Indie asked, "What is the plan, big sister?"
"I tried reaching the others, but it seems there is something blocking the connection. This means we have to finish our mission and hope the others can also handle their own."
They nodded to her words. They also tried to contact their friends, but nothing happened. It was just like what happened on the 9th floor.
"But where do we go from here?" Kaizo asked again. This time, Sylara was the one who answered.
She pointed toward the west. "That way. I can see a large statue standing in front of what appears to be a tall mountain."
Because she had drawn a blood tattoo meant for enhanced perception, she was able to see thousands of miles. Her sight now even surpasses Kent, who could sense and see up to 80,000 km.
With a 500 times boost, she could now see even over 200,000 km wide.
Knowing she has the eye of an eagle, they never doubted her. Instead, they started following her in the direction she pointed.
Half an hour later, they arrived 20,000 km from the statue.
To everyone’s shock, what Sylara initially thought was a statue was actually a person wielding a large broadsword.

He stood 200 meters tall, muscles built to punch like a titan. His skin was made of stone, with most of it appearing metallic. They knew the monster standing before them, though only at the peak of the True Immortal stage, was no simple fiend.
Even Vexthra panicked, for she knew the titan of a man standing and looking directly at them was bad news.
"That is one large bastard," Kaizo, who prided himself on being a brute, knew he was nothing compared to this monster of a man.
"Kaizo, how large can you grow after using your transformation innate ability?" Vexthra asked, already formulating a plan in her mind.
"For now, I can grow to 50 meters. However, if I use my bloodline, I can reach 100 meters for 30 minutes before I run out of energy."
"That is good enough. You will be our vanguard. Sylara and Indie will support from the side."
Kaizo nodded and asked, "What will you be doing?"
Vexthra smiled and flicked her hair back—something she learned from Dia (Unity’s sister).
"While this time I can’t sense most of my Immortal Qi, if you three can buy me 25 minutes, I will refine this brute into a golem. I am sure you will love to have a training buddy."

However, if I use my bloodline, I can reach 100 meters for 30 minutes before I run out of energy."
"That is good enough.
You will be our vanguard.
Sylara and Indie will support from the side."
Kaizo nodded and asked, "What will you be doing?"
Vexthra smiled and flicked her hair back—something she learned from Dia (Unity’s sister).
"While this time I can’t sense most of my Immortal Qi, if you three can buy me 25 minutes, I will refine this brute into a golem.
I am sure you will love to have a training buddy."

chapters.title: Chapter 1492: The Eleventh Floor - Four Fallen Immortals (2)
paragraphs: Vexthra and her team waited for a few minutes before they started to advance again. Already, they can sense that their opponent isn’t an ordinary being.
The mission description mentioned Chaos Beasts, so they knew the ordinary immortals they had killed in the past were nothing compared to this monstrosity.
Even the fiend Kaizo and the others killed on the 10th floor pale in comparison to this brute.
However, with Vexthra having a plan, the three—Kaizo, Sylara, and Indie—knew they had to survive for at least 25 minutes to buy her all the time she needed.
As to how that can be achieved, they all know Kaizo will play a huge role. So the moment they were 300 meters away, Kaizo took action.
He activated an innate skill that instantly caused his body to start to grow. In no time, he rose 50 meters tall; however, he was still a bug before the mountain of a man standing 200 meters tall.
Despite there being four people advancing toward it, it remained standing, its large, broad sword stabbed into the ground, held at the hilt by both hands.
"Ancient Angelic Titan Bloodline Ignite,"
At once, a powerful aura burst out of his body as he shot into the air, vanishing into the clouds. Suddenly, a power ripple spread across the sky, causing a wave of heavy energy to fall down.
This time, the brute named Gorath reacted. He pulled his broad sword from the ground and lifted it up, ready to face whatever was heading toward him from the cloud.

"Big mistake ignoring us." Indie moved, and millions of shadows moved with her. She only took a single step, but then appeared before Gorath, her dagger stabbing forward. At once, the entire region around her turned completely black.
Then, up in the air, a giant dagger formed from the shadows, and two large hands that were also formed from the shadows grabbed it.
"Underworld Dagger,"
Both hands moved, and before Gorath could move one hand to defend against it, it already landed on its chest, causing cracks to appear on its stony armour.
The attack pushed it back, just in time for a second attack to land on the same spot the dagger had landed.

"Blood Scythe," Sylara also attacked, forming a large scythe from blood. She had collected so much blood from the previous massacres, so she had an abundance of blood to use for whatever attack she wanted.
As expected, her attack further pushed the giant back, causing it to roar in defiance. It lowered its sword and tried to slash through the two bugs who dared attack its majestic self.
However, just when its sword moved, a chilling voice came from the clouds, followed by a powerful fist that instantly locked Gorath in place.
"Here I come,"
Kaizo descended like a mountain, the space under his giant fist cracking and spiderwebbing all around. Sylara grabbed Indie, and they vanished into blood mist, appearing far from the battlefield.
"Ancient Giant Art—"
The clouds rumbled, manifesting the silhouette of a golden giant man with large wings on his back. Golden lightning brust in the cloud, adding to the already chilling sensation on the ground.
"First Form—"

Kaizo’s fist burst into lightning flames, something not even Vexthra was able to remain calm about. At once, the space around them started to break. Vexthra waved her hand, and two streams of her Immortal Qi moved, encircling Indie and Sylara, just in time for the fist to land on Gorath’s face.
"Dragon God’s Face Smasher"
BOOOOOOOM
Kaizo landed his fist, and at once, the entire space shuddered. Gorath was sent flying several kilometres away, part of his face blasted off.

"Nice one, Kaizo," Indie cheered for the brute who, despite there being immortals and demigods now among them in the legion, everyone knew was not to be underestimated. There is just something about Kaizo that makes him a pillar they all feel they could stand behind.
Watching him blast away a True Immortal who also happens to be a Chaos Beast, they knew he was not to be underestimated.
"Go on, ladies, keep it busy," Vexthra commanded, and they moved. Soon, they started bombarding the giant, making sure it had no rest whatsoever.
Vexthra sat down in a lotus posture and retrieved a cauldron-like item from her space ring. She formed a hand seal, and the item expanded, taking the shape of a golden bowl.
If a god were to be present now, they would have coughed up a few mouthfuls of blood if they saw what Vexthra was about to use the ’Genesis Purifying Cauldron’ to do—refine a golem.
It is one of the hundred Celestial artefacts crafted by the legendary ’Nine Immortal Flame Blacksmith’, a being who dominated the Flame Era with his legendary creations.
Maybe knowing the kind of blunder she was committing, she smirked, muttering something under her breath, "I am sorry, Lord Nine Flame, but I have no other choice."
Sitting somewhere, creating art, a certain dragon sneezes a few times.
Vexthra formed a few hand seals, and then a green flame burst under the cauldron. She continued to form more hand seals, making sure not even a single mistake was made.
Meanwhile, with Kaizo leading the beatdown, he and the two ladies continued to keep Gorath busy, making sure that by the time they grew tired, Vexthra would be ready to turn it into a golem.
[Vari’s Team]
Vari, just like Vexthra, arrived at a different place with four others: Lani, Neomi, Mara, and Enkay. They were a bit stunned that they were separated from their sisters.
However, after the mission description appeared, they knew what they had to do.
The only difference was that they had no idea who they were meant to hunt.
Initially, they expected to be given a direction. However, even after waiting a few minutes, nothing like that showed.
Vari, who was selected as the de facto leader, came up with a plan.
"Let’s fly high into the air and scan the surroundings. I am sure we can find a clue." They nodded to her words and flew into the air, using their senses to scan far and wide.
Enkay, being a True Immortal, was able to scan further than the rest. However, he saw nothing, or at least he saw it a bit too late.
"Lani... watch out,"
He moved with explosive speed, a sword appearing in his hand. However, despite alerting Lani, both of them were too slow to react.

A mist appeared and turned into a slender lady with a heavy chest who stabbed her spear at Lani, aiming for her neck. She sensed the attack and reacted, but she was a step too slow, so the spear pierced her back, appearing on her chest.
"NOOOOOOOOOO"
Vari moved with deadly speed, hoping to join Enkay in stopping the lady. However, she smiled and snapped her finger, causing a dark portal to form.
"Come find me. By then, I will be done eating her..." With a laughter that caused the space around them to shudder, she stepped into the portal—or at least she tried to.
Neomi clapped her hands together, and the lady who moved to step into the portal froze. Then, in an anticlockwise manner, she turned her right palm against the left.
"Grim Reversal."
Her forward movement reversed, and all her actions began to undo. In under two seconds, she was turned back to the point where the mist appeared.
That was when Neomi used a second skill... "Life Swap,"
A formation formed under Lani, and just when the spear could pierce her, she and Neomi changed positions. The spear pierced Neomi’s chest, but instead of screaming, a smile tugged at her lips.
"Well then, why don’t we dance?"
