chapters.title: Chapter 1493: The Eleventh Floor - Four Fallen Immortals (3)
paragraphs: Before becoming the legendary warrior called Rakshara, she was known as Shara, the Mother of Killers. She was one of the most prolific killers to ever walk the face of the universe.
It was said that she had killed so many people that even the fame once held by the legendary Contractor and the Joker was no match.

The Contractor was a being whose legend shook the Immortal Era, and the Joker was an insidious assassin who had killed her fair share of people. They caused the universe to shake in fear, but even they fell short when Shara appeared.
The legend said she had killed to the point that the Grim Reaper himself was left dumbfounded. For beings whose job was to rip fallen souls, he was shocked by Shara’s ruthlessness.
She was also the first being to have cultivated her killing intent to the point that death itself feared her.
It was also said that before she went into seclusion, which years later she emerged from as Rakshara, the Grim Reaper granted her a certain level of authority over death.
This made her nearly impossible to kill.
So, watching the smile on her face despite a long spear sticking out from her chest, her attacker felt her back crawl, fear appearing in her eyes.
She saw that her attack impaled Lani as she had intended. However, before she could retreat and eat her, everything reversed, and now her attack landed on a maniac who seemed to find joy in pain.
"You never saw that coming, huh?"
"H-How?" she stammered, momentarily feeling her life in danger.
Neomi smiled and answered, "Death and I have an agreement, a very long time ago. You see, until I want to, I cannot die... easily."
Her leg moved, and before the lady could dodge, it landed on her face, sending her flying back. Neomi yanked the spear out of her chest, and it flew toward its owner.
Mara was momentarily stunned by how Neomi handled the sneak attack. She recovered and then joined Enkay and Vari in attacking, ensuring their opponent was surrounded on all sides.
From the moment she appeared, Vari sensed their opponent had assassin properties. So she took control of the shadows, making sure she didn’t slip up on them.
"Are you okay?" Lani moved to Neomi’s side, a worried look appearing on her face.
"I am okay. But killing this bitch will make me feel better."
"Then let’s kick her ass." They moved, Lani, taking out her scythe while Neomi summoned her spear. Inside her weapon, the six-armed lady sat, all six hands clapped in a prayer pose.
She was the weapon spirit she received during her Weapon Spirit Enlightenment. Now, knowing the battle was not as simple as the previous ones, she decided to aid her master in any way she could.
Soon, Velmora, the Chaos Envoy who, several billion years ago, single-handedly slaughtered all the Inner Disciples of the Celestial Dream Sect, found herself surrounded, with nowhere to run.

Vari and Lani took control over the shadows, so whenever she tried to run, they blocked her there. Mara, who has an affinity for the light element, was put in charge of dishing out all the heavy damage, while Enkay was made to lead the close combat.
As for Neomi, she was making sure Enkay had all the openings he needed to get close and perhaps deal a severe blow, one that would tip the odds in their favour.
Although they had the upper hand, they knew the moment they made one mistake, it would be game over for them.
So, against all odds, the battle was progressing in perfect synchrony, something they had mastered after years of training inside the tower and previous floors.
[Unity’s Team]
Unity and her team were also tasked with killing one of the four Fallen Immortals. Their target was Selvara, a redhead vampire whose power comes from the power of blood.

While she is a Chaos Beast, she looks just like a human. The only beastly thing about her is her four pairs of horns and animal-like pupils. They are red, and looking into them feels like looking into the deepest, darkest abyss.
When they arrived in her domain, she instantly created a formation that trapped them inside using blood, which seemed to soak the very ground they stood on.
Unity, as the leader, took charge because she can fight in the air without hindrance. She is an archer after all. Kol, who also happens to be an archer, joined her.
He is a True Immortal, so he qualifies to join this campaign.

Zareth also summoned both the World Serpent and the Jade Dragon, using their overwhelming might to aid Unity and Kol in keeping their opponent at bay long enough for Velyra to take control over the entire blood pool that Selvara was using for her attacks.
As someone with a natural affinity for blood, she was tasked with stripping their opponent of her weapon. This is also Velyra’s first big battle after awakening her innate body.
When Kent first met her, he mistook her for a weakling. However, he was quickly proven wrong when the high priestess of the Bloodvein Tribe proved her abilities as a dangerous warrior.
Kent calls her his Redskin Beauty mainly because of her skin color. However, aside from the cute side of her, in battle, she doesn’t shy away from showing her warrior side.
So, with her absolute control over blood coming into play, she worked her way into slowly taking control over the blood around them.

A few minutes into the battle, both Unity and Zareth sustained quite a few gory wounds. Although they were far from the ground where the blood was, their target was a True Immortal, so surviving her attacks was even a miracle in itself.

The only one with little to no injuries was Kol, who is both faster and stronger than the two of them. But they weren’t injured for no reason. Zareth had dealt some heavy blows to their target, while Unity herself put a few arrows into her body.
Velyra remained standing for 10 full minutes before suddenly, her eyes emitted faint reddish smoke. Then suddenly, the blood on the ground started to tremble.
Selvara, who was about to attack Unity with a deadly blood spear, felt her control over the blood severed, causing the spear to turn into liquid blood.
"What?" Her body shook.
Turning around, she saw Velyra standing with large blood spears forming behind her.
"How did you do that?"
"No need to look shocked. I merely took control over all the blood inside this domain."
"But that is impossible. There is no way you should have the means to deprive me of using the blood inside this domain. I am the owner," Selvara was both shocked and angry.
This blood pool was formed from the slaughter she committed billions of years ago. The Celestial Dream Sect had hundreds of thousands of disciples, so she alone killed enough to form a blood pool.

Over the years, it had absorbed the energy of the souls on the battlefield, making it one of the most powerful blood sources one could ever find. When she broke free from the formation, she took control of it and planned to use it to dominate the world, as she had wanted to billions of years ago.
Taking it from her caused her anger to boil.
"Relax. I am not going to kill you." Velyra smirked, waving her hand for the spears to dissolve. Unity and the others, alongside Selvara, became stunned hearing what she said.
"Vel, maybe kill her first before you play with her," Unity said, but the Redskin Beauty smiled and clapped her hands together.
"Killing her will be a waste. Turning her into my blood puppet, however, will be fun." The moment she said that, she formed a hand seal, and a red formation enveloped them.
Chains burst from the ground and grabbed hold of Selvara’s arms and legs. Before she could move to break them, Velyra appeared before her and pressed her index finger against her forehead.
"Sleep."
Her eyes rolled back, and she fell unconscious.

chapters.title: Chapter 1494: The Eleventh Floor - Four Fallen Immortals (4)
paragraphs: "I never knew you could do that, Vel." Unity stopped beside Velyra, who was using her finger to draw a series of runes in the air.
Taking control of the blood pool was within their expectations. They knew she was connected to the blood more than even vampires. So taking hold of the large blood pool was perfectly normal.
However, putting a True Immortal to sleep with a mere tap on her forehead wasn’t something they saw coming.
Even Zaila, who happens to be a mind cultivator, wouldn’t have this much power to accomplish what Velyra had accomplished.
"How did you do it?" Unity asked, but Velyra merely smiled.

"Fine, if you are not going to tell me, then keep it to yourself." Unity clearly wanted to hear how Velyra managed to put the True Immortal to sleep; however, since she didn’t want to tell her, she could not force it out of her.
Velyra laughed, but she said nothing.
Seeing this, Unity smirked, removed the storage ring from Selvara’s finger, and stored it away in her Love Space.
They stood back and continued to watch as Velyra filled the air with runes.
[Veera’s team]

Meanwhile, Veera, Yi Lai, the Shade King Nykali, and Elaine sat on a boulder, glasses filled to the brim with red wine in their hands as they watched their subordinates wage war on Draxion – The Undying Commander.

When they arrived on the 11th floor, they appeared within the domain of one of the four Chaos Envoys. He is the strongest of them simply because he has several undead, most of which are immortals, under him.
Naturally, if a team like Vexthra’s, Unity’s, or Vari’s were to be assigned there, they would have faced the greatest challenge yet.
Facing hundreds of immortal-level undead isn’t something to scoff at. However, the team assigned to face him was made up entirely of abnormal people.
Veera has over a thousand undead, five of which are True Immortals, three Core Immortals, and the remaining ranging between Spirit Immortal and Life Stage.
Shade King Nykali also commands over 10,000 wraiths. Just like Veera, he had also gained the ability to create powerful spirit wraiths by merging the weaker ones.

He had only succeeded in creating two who are only Root Immortals. However, the tens of thousands of wraiths under his command are all within the rank of the Life and Death Stage. Unleashing all of them was more than enough to handle a large chunk of Draxion’s undead army.
As for Yi Lai, she has seven undead, one of which had only recently reached the Death Stage. The rest are True immortals, with even one of them being an Immortal King.
The dangerous part, too, was that all seven of them are dragons.
Elaine, on the other hand, had summoned three Death Agents, each a True Immortal. Naturally, she is among the strongest in the legion, all things considered.
So with this lineup unleashed on Draxion, they themselves had nothing to worry about. They just had to relax and watch as their subordinates fought for them.
Standing behind them is Fero, the Immortal King Dragon Yi Lai had waited weeks for to complete his dragon ascension trial.
"Fero, do you want to join them?" Elaine turned and asked the handsome white-haired dragon who had his arms crossed over his chest.
"No offense, my lady, but I have standards, and these small fries don’t meet them. So until a real opponent appears, my sword will remain sheathed."
"Spoken like a true dragon," Yi Lai said with a grin, causing her friends to laugh. Dragons are naturally arrogant, so the fact that he even showed Elaine the respect she needed was a miracle.
However, what he said is indeed true. As someone who is already an Immortal King, he is above the standard of this mission. It’s even shocking that he got to keep his cultivation base intact.
However, even if he had been suppressed, as a dragon, he would have felt insulted and might even have chosen not to fight.
Thankfully, with those sent into the battle already overpowered, Draxion and his undead force are having a bad day.
But the four battlefields weren’t the only ones ablaze. Somewhere else, the rest of the legion, led by Miryssa, were locked in with the agents from the Soul Temple.

There are about 200 of them, the majority of whom are immortals, with some even at the Immortal Lord stage. However, with the likes of Miryssa, Uncle Drew, Vargus, and Avotha among them, the enemy wasn’t having a good day.
Although some of them had been suppressed to the peak of the True Immortal Stage, they aren’t in any way bothered at all.

Miryssa may be suppressed, but she is someone who has reached the Universal God Stage during the Primordial Era. Someone like that had nothing to fear when locked in combat against beings who are struggling against even Uncle Drew, who is merely at the Death Stage.
Vargus was suppressed to the True Immortal Stage, but he was everywhere with his hammer, causing mayhem.
As for Avotha, he was suppressed to the Immortal Lord Stage, and he alone held back four Immortal Lords.
He was basically everywhere on the battlefield, making sure the four Immortal Lords regret coming to this planet in the first place.
The mission was to kill all 200 of them and ensure not even a single one of them escaped. Naturally, Elina made sure none of them dared run, since before the battle, she had sealed the entire space.
Not even a distress signal could pass through. So the only hope they had was creating a chance for one of them to escape. Unfortunately for them, karma was against them.
A couple of minutes into their battle, some people joined them.

It turned out the survivors of the planet were keeping track of the Soul Temple agents, so when they saw they were under attack, they joined to finish off the parasites that had invaded their world, killed their high-ranking elders, and had been working behind the scenes to free the four Fallen Immortals.
With them joining the battle and bringing a few Immortal Lords with them, the battle suddenly shifted, and before long, every last agent was killed.
Their bodies were collected by Miryssa, who knew Veera and the other freaks would have a use for them.
It would have taken them quite some time to finish everyone. However, with the help they received from the natives, it took them less than 30 minutes to slaughter everyone.

Just when they were done handling everything, they felt their connection with Unity’s team had been established. This gave them the perfect escape, so after using their classic line, they vanished into thin air.
"Kent Madson, huh. We should thank him when we meet him one day," the leader of the natives, a rabbit kin, said, tapping his cane on the ground.
"Leader, should we send out word to our allies? Maybe if we can form some connection with these people, they can help us rescue the princess."
"Let’s hold back for now. The oracle clearly said our destiny is about to change. As to how it will happen, I have a feeling these wonderful people are involved somehow."

sentences.text: "I never knew you could do that, Vel." Unity stopped beside Velyra, who was using her finger to draw a series of runes in the air.
Taking control of the blood pool was within their expectations.
They knew she was connected to the blood more than even vampires.
So taking hold of the large blood pool was perfectly normal.
However, putting a True Immortal to sleep with a mere tap on her forehead wasn’t something they saw coming.
Even Zaila, who happens to be a mind cultivator, wouldn’t have this much power to accomplish what Velyra had accomplished.
"How did you do it?" Unity asked, but Velyra merely smiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 1495: Side Mission, Huge Reward
paragraphs: In the end, it turned out that the most taxing battle of all happened between Vexthra’s team Vs Gorath.
Rather ironic, one might say, considering the team with the bona fide Pseudo-Supreme actually ended up suffering the most.
But given the setup of the battle, it was perfectly understandable why they suffered so much. Kaizo lost one hand, while Indie had a deep cut on her shoulder.
Sylara was rather squeaky clean despite sustaining the most damage. The reason for that was due to the overpowered effect of the second blood tattoo she had drawn a few weeks ago.

The first tattoo was the [Blood Perception Tattoo]. It allows her to enhance her perception and reaction speed by 500 times. This boon helped them easily locate their target. It was something she had been looking forward to for a while.
As for the second tattoo, it was the [Blood Immortal Tattoo].

The name sounds a bit exaggerated; however, its use is exactly as its name suggests. Basically, as long as she has the tattoo, unless an attack has the power to kill her instantly, all other forms of damage will be returned to the one who inflicted them.
This meant that during the battle, all damages dealt to her were returned to the attacker, leaving her with no injuries whatsoever.
All injuries were returned to Gorath, allowing her to indirectly deal far more damage to the brute than she thought she could have.
But even so, because Vexthra chose to refine the brute into a golem, they had to endure 25 minutes of torture. In the end, however, Vexthra came through.

Just when her teammates were running on their last reserves, she activated the formation, trapping Gorath. The rest was her using the Genesis Purifying Cauldron to refine the brute into a pitch-black golem with a pair of green eyes.
Surprisingly, while Gorath was a Peak True Immortal, the golem came out as an Immortal King. Even more shocking was the aura surrounding it.
If an Immortal King stood before it, they would turn pale from sheer shock.
Kaizo, who was furious because he lost a hand, became ecstatic when Vexthra was done refining the golem.
Once she was done, she turned to Kaizo. "Sorry about the arm. Elaine will fix it for you. For now, however, I want a drop of your blood essence."
Kaizo did not even bother to ask why she needed his blood essence. He simply handed over a drop and waited for Vexthra to do her thing.
After a few minutes of applying the blood essence, the golem let out a powerful aura that caused Kaizo and the others to pale for a second.
Kaizo felt a connection form between him and the golem.
"You can name him now."
Kaizo grinned and thought for a moment before a smile formed on his face. "I will call him Titan."
The moment he named him, the 3-meter-tall golem shrank to the same height as Kaizo. He then went down on one knee and bowed toward him.
He said nothing, but Kaizo knew he was pledging his allegiance to him. This made him laugh, and after a few seconds, he told Titan to stand.

"Titan is now yours to command as you please. He is linked to your blood essence, so as you grow, so will he. There are many other uses for him. If you want to know more, you can have a chat with him. I am sure you will be blown away by how useful he is."
"Thank you, my lady. I will be sure to value my new pal with all my heart."
Vexthra laughed, "I know you will; that is why I refined him for you."
She waved her hand, and Kaizo’s severed hand flew into her space ring. A few seconds later, she sensed the connection between them and the others form, so she reached out.

It turned out that the others, except Veera’s team, had finished their battles. Unity’s team ended their battle first, thanks to Velyra taking control over the blood pool and putting their target to sleep.
Just like Vexthra, she also refined her opponent into a Blood Puppet. The moment she took control over her entire being, the battle ended.

After that, Velyra flew toward the source of the blood pool, fully submerged her body in it, and began absorbing it. According to her, she awakened an innate ability that would allow her to break past the limits of the high world.
So she entered seclusion, leaving Unity and the others with her Blood Puppet.
As for Vari’s team, they had a brief but intense battle before Enkay drove his sword through their opponent’s head, ending her instantly.
She wanted to play a game of hide and seek with them, but with Neomi turning the tide by reversing her kill, everything flipped on her, allowing them to overwhelm her from the start.
In the end, she died, bringing their part of the mission to an end.

The only ones still at it were Veera’s team. Thankfully, after standing there for nearly an hour, Fero had had enough, so he joined the battle and, in under five minutes, he slaughtered everyone, bringing the battle to a close.
Surprisingly, after he killed Draxion, the Dragon Ascension Gate opened, and his resurrected body was sent inside. If he were to pass, then Yi Lai would have another subordinate on her hands.
Vexthra called everyone over to her side. However, because Velyra was in seclusion, she asked everyone to side with Unity. This way, they could stay there when she came out of seclusion.
As for the Dragon Ascension Trial, Yi Lai left it for two of her undead dragons to guard it. She had no reason to stay, since whatever goes on inside the trial is out of her reach.
After everyone gathered, Vexthra broke the news to them.
"Congratulations, everyone. We have successfully cleared the 11th floor. However, this time, we have a side mission."
"A side mission?"
"Yes. I myself was a bit shocked when I saw it; however, after reading through it, I believe we have to accept it." Vexthra shared the details with everyone.
It would be better if they saw the mission they would be embarking on. Of course, not all of them would be deployed, but since they are a team, Vexthra wanted them to see the details.
The mission is a good one, so he wants them to address that first.
[You have received a Side Mission]

[Description: Twenty years ago, the oldest princess of the Green Skin Rabbitkin was kidnapped by the Soul Temple. Three years ago, it was discovered that she was sold into slavery to a warlord called Biania on Planet Skar.
She commands the Silent Graves Legion, a mercenary team of dangerous immortals. Their reputation precedes them, and Warlord Biania holds one-fourth of the power in Planet Skar.
Your mission is to locate this princess, rescue her, and, if possible, eliminate Warlord Biania. Under no circumstances should she be allowed to escape with the princess.
Should you choose to accept this mission, go to the High Priestess of the Green Skin Rabbit kin and collect the contract.]
[Rewards:]
↠ Blood Life Fruit
↠ Dragon Ascension Fruit
↠ Stone Heart Fruit

chapters.title: Chapter 1496: Dream Illusion Flower & Seven Pattern Butterfly
paragraphs: After reading through the mission, Vexthra and her team concluded that only a few of them should go. They still have the 12th floor and subsequent ones to clear, so they can’t waste weeks on a single floor.
Travelling to a different planet will surely take weeks, if not months.
So after some talks, they decided to send a five-member team on this mission. Since the mission said nothing about the strength of their opponent, they decided not to risk it.

Miryssa had already informed everyone that they had encountered natives from the world they are in. From what she revealed, the people of this world have about five Immortal Lords among them and a few others who are already at the Immortal Monarch and Emperor stage.
Such a lineup is enough to go to this planet and rescue their princess. The fact that they haven’t already told them their opponent is no simple warlord.
So Avotha and Vargus were tasked to lead the team. Going with them is Axiom, who is an Immortal Monarch, and Kailan, who is an Immortal King.
Lastly, they added Fero, who happens to be a dragon and also an Immortal King, just like Kailan. These five can be considered a very lethal force that many would run from.

Vargus is a Demigod, someone who is only a step away from becoming a god. Aside from him, Avotha is a force even more lethal than Vargus. He is a Demigod who has gone against several harrowing opponents and walked out alive.
As someone who trained his entire life in hell, he can be considered a monster.
In fact, two of Vargus would struggle against him. So he would lead, and Vargus would support. Axiom will ensure they don’t die since his handle over the void is next to none.

Kailan and Fero are there to handle the small fries. While that is a bit funny considering Fero alone can take on multiple Immortal Kings, the mission is to rescue the Princess and, if possible, kill the warlord.
"Remember, we have three legendary rewards on the line, so be sure to get the job done and, well, have fun while at it," Vexthra said before pointing in the direction they should go.
Now that the mission is over, she is back to her goddess strength and can sense the entire world.

It was also because she could sense the entire planet that she put together such a team. There are powerful immortals living on the planet, so she knew the only reason why they haven’t yet rescued their princess may be because she is hard to reach. The warlord may be a threat they can’t handle easily.
After they are gone, Vexthra turns to the rest of her sisters.
"The moment Velyra is done, we will head directly to the 12th floor. For now, use the time to see if you can find anything that will aid Unity."
They nodded and scattered, leaving Vexthra and Miryssa behind.
Miryssa waited for a few minutes before she asked, "We could have sent only Avotha on this mission, and he would have done an impeccable job. Why did you add the others, too?"
Vexthra smiled, knowing Miryssa was right.
Avotha is strong enough to kill someone at the God Ascension stage. Sending him on a mission with four others, with one at the Demigod stage, feels like overkill.
"You are right. Avotha alone is enough. However, he alone would take longer than I wanted. The reason, of course, is the rewards."
Miryssa furrowed her brow, hearing Vexthra’s words.

"The Dragon Ascension Fruit is what I am most concerned about. The reason for that is, of course, to help Kent. The Dragon Ascension Fruit, paired with the Chaos Heart Stones, will not only help him in forming his first Chaos Heart, but it will also raise his bloodline by at least 10%.

I know you are already aware that once he returns, he will be embarking on another dangerous mission, one that he will be tried and tested, draining him of all the strength he has. I want him to have all the power he can carry before leaving.
If he can create a Chaos Heart and raise his bloodline by even 5%, I will be able to sleep at night knowing he will be safe when inside the Star Gateway.
This is why I want them to hurry. If they complete the mission fast enough, he will have ample time to use the Dragon Ascension Fruit."
Miryssa nodded, understanding why Vexthra made such a decision. "I guess the only delay here will be their travel from this planet to the other planet."
Vexthra nodded. She knew the moment they got to Planet Skar that Warlord could be considered dead.
After spending a few minutes talking about other things, they also joined the search after Vexthra created a formation around Velyra.
Meanwhile, back on Planet Brymrr, Kent had finished his second painting and was on the verge of finishing the third.
Vika and Fallon had yet to return from the tower, so it was just Kent and Lene. She had booked a hotel for them and was only waiting for her master to be done so they could move there for the night.
Since Vika and Fallon are not around, she wants to spend some quality time with him.
Thankfully, a few hours later, Kent completed the third painting, causing a ripple to spread through the city. Many felt it but failed to track its origin.
After performing his post-painting ritual, he turned to the three paintings he would use to make a name for himself in the coming days.
The first is, of course, the Demon Heart Gaze, which he knew would cause a bidding war when auctioned. Using painting to see one’s heart demon is something everybody will love to have.
In fact, all his paintings would cause a bidding war.

The second painting, for example, is a painting of a beautiful flower. At first glance, it appears ordinary, but if one channels their focus into it, their consciousness will be sucked into the painting, allowing them to enter an illusory realm where the longer one stays inside, the stronger their mind becomes.
Basically, it strengthens the mind against illusions.
The third is the Seven Pattern Butterfly. This painting was something he witnessed during his life as Jest. It was when he was travelling through the Sword Valley.
On one fateful evening, he met a spirit beast called the Seven Pattern Jade Butterfly. It was a beast he spent three days running from.

At first, he thought he would be able to escape from it, but after three days, the sly beasts were still after him. It took some time, but he eventually noticed the patterns on the butterfly were not there for decoration.
They each have unique flight patterns and abilities that, when mastered, can allow anyone who specializes in aerial combat to become nearly invincible.
Jest spent one month studying all seven patterns before he managed to escape. Afterwards, he spent five months mastering them before he finally gained the upper hand and killed the vile beast.
Later, he discovered it was one of the Overlords of the Sword Valley. Killing it was an achievement he never expected to achieve that easily.

He brought it back to life through painting. Those who wish to master the seven patterns will have to send their consciousness into the painting, where they will meet the Seven Pattern Jade Butterfly and learn from it.
This time, however, instead of running for their dear lives like many did billions of years back, they would have the liberty to control what happens while inside the painting.
Kent knew these three paintings would cause chaos soon, so he wanted to rest and recover his strength first before calling Fallon over to take the paintings to Lady Annette.
"I am hungry again. Let’s grab a bite before heading to the hotel."

sentences.text: After reading through the mission, Vexthra and her team concluded that only a few of them should go.
They still have the 12th floor and subsequent ones to clear, so they can’t waste weeks on a single floor.
Travelling to a different planet will surely take weeks, if not months.
So after some talks, they decided to send a five-member team on this mission.
Since the mission said nothing about the strength of their opponent, they decided not to risk it.
Miryssa had already informed everyone that they had encountered natives from the world they are in.
From what she revealed, the people of this world have about five Immortal Lords among them and a few others who are already at the Immortal Monarch and Emperor stage.
Such a lineup is enough to go to this planet and rescue their princess.
The fact that they haven’t already told them their opponent is no simple warlord.
So Avotha and Vargus were tasked to lead the team.
Going with them is Axiom, who is an Immortal Monarch, and Kailan, who is an Immortal King.
Lastly, they added Fero, who happens to be a dragon and also an Immortal King, just like Kailan.
These five can be considered a very lethal force that many would run from.
Vargus is a Demigod, someone who is only a step away from becoming a god.
Aside from him, Avotha is a force even more lethal than Vargus.
He is a Demigod who has gone against several harrowing opponents and walked out alive.
As someone who trained his entire life in hell, he can be considered a monster.
In fact, two of Vargus would struggle against him.
So he would lead, and Vargus would support.
Axiom will ensure they don’t die since his handle over the void is next to none.
Kailan and Fero are there to handle the small fries.
While that is a bit funny considering Fero alone can take on multiple Immortal Kings, the mission is to rescue the Princess and, if possible, kill the warlord.
"Remember, we have three legendary rewards on the line, so be sure to get the job done and, well, have fun while at it," Vexthra said before pointing in the direction they should go.
Now that the mission is over, she is back to her goddess strength and can sense the entire world.
It was also because she could sense the entire planet that she put together such a team.
There are powerful immortals living on the planet, so she knew the only reason why they haven’t yet rescued their princess may be because she is hard to reach.
The warlord may be a threat they can’t handle easily.
After they are gone, Vexthra turns to the rest of her sisters.
"The moment Velyra is done, we will head directly to the 12th floor.
For now, use the time to see if you can find anything that will aid Unity."
They nodded and scattered, leaving Vexthra and Miryssa behind.
Miryssa waited for a few minutes before she asked, "We could have sent only Avotha on this mission, and he would have done an impeccable job.
Why did you add the others, too?"
Vexthra smiled, knowing Miryssa was right.
Avotha is strong enough to kill someone at the God Ascension stage.
Sending him on a mission with four others, with one at the Demigod stage, feels like overkill.
"You are right.
Avotha alone is enough.
However, he alone would take longer than I wanted.
The reason, of course, is the rewards."
Miryssa furrowed her brow, hearing Vexthra’s words.
"The Dragon Ascension Fruit is what I am most concerned about.
The reason for that is, of course, to help Kent.
The Dragon Ascension Fruit, paired with the Chaos Heart Stones, will not only help him in forming his first Chaos Heart, but it will also raise his bloodline by at least 10%.
I know you are already aware that once he returns, he will be embarking on another dangerous mission, one that he will be tried and tested, draining him of all the strength he has.
I want him to have all the power he can carry before leaving.
If he can create a Chaos Heart and raise his bloodline by even 5%, I will be able to sleep at night knowing he will be safe when inside the Star Gateway.
This is why I want them to hurry.
If they complete the mission fast enough, he will have ample time to use the Dragon Ascension Fruit."
Miryssa nodded, understanding why Vexthra made such a decision.
"I guess the only delay here will be their travel from this planet to the other planet."
Vexthra nodded.
She knew the moment they got to Planet Skar that Warlord could be considered dead.
After spending a few minutes talking about other things, they also joined the search after Vexthra created a formation around Velyra.
Meanwhile, back on Planet Brymrr, Kent had finished his second painting and was on the verge of finishing the third.
Vika and Fallon had yet to return from the tower, so it was just Kent and Lene.
She had booked a hotel for them and was only waiting for her master to be done so they could move there for the night.
Since Vika and Fallon are not around, she wants to spend some quality time with him.
Thankfully, a few hours later, Kent completed the third painting, causing a ripple to spread through the city.
Many felt it but failed to track its origin.
After performing his post-painting ritual, he turned to the three paintings he would use to make a name for himself in the coming days.
The first is, of course, the Demon Heart Gaze, which he knew would cause a bidding war when auctioned.
Using painting to see one’s heart demon is something everybody will love to have.
In fact, all his paintings would cause a bidding war.
The second painting, for example, is a painting of a beautiful flower.

At first glance, it appears ordinary, but if one channels their focus into it, their consciousness will be sucked into the painting, allowing them to enter an illusory realm where the longer one stays inside, the stronger their mind becomes.
Basically, it strengthens the mind against illusions.

chapters.title: Chapter 1497: Grab a Bite — Fight
paragraphs: "Master, are you sure you are not too tired to be walking right now?" Lene asked, hugging Kent’s arm as they walked toward the restaurant.
Spirit Painting is different from normal painting.
It requires one to tap into the astral planes to infuse the painting with the very essence of the soul. Since Spirit Paintings can be manifested, it requires a connection to the astral plane.
Normally, Kent wouldn’t have to worry, provided he had a Spirit Brush. These brushes are created with a connection to the Astral Plane already established within them.
So when using such a brush during the painting process, the painter wouldn’t have to tap too much into their soul essence.
Kent doesn’t have that, so he was forced to use his soul essence for all three paintings. Also, since the paintings he had painted aren’t exactly simple, it drained him more than he expected.

"I am fine, Lene. I just need a few hours to recover." He had already sent his soul body into Kenna’s spirit pool inside the Soul Universe, so as they walked toward the restaurant, his soul was being replenished with both the pure essence of the Soul Universe and the Spirit Pool.
Lene nodded, and while they were being watched by thousands due to how cute they both looked, they didn’t seem to care.
After about 10 minutes, they walked into a restaurant and booked a table. Kent sat down and closed his eyes, letting his soul strength recover much faster.
Thankfully, with how vast his soul universe is, he managed to recover about 60% of his soul strength before the food was served. He picked up his chopsticks and started eating.

Lene followed suit and, like her master, started eating to her heart’s content. Since all food prepared in this world is made from spirit ingredients, eating them strengthens the body, mind, and soul.
"This food is delicious," Lene said, taking a bite of the spirit meat. Savouring the taste, she let the energy wash through her body.
Kent smiled.
After a few minutes, he asked Lene a question:
"How far are you from becoming a god?"
Lene set her chopsticks down and wiped her lips before answering.

"I have already formed my law of self. The only thing left is to find a God Ascension Platform and inscribe it into the Dao Mountain. Then, after I take the tribulation, I can finally step into the Early God stage."

She smiled and added, "Considering I have already tempered my body to the peak of the Immortal stage and even cultivated my soul to the god stage, I am sure I have already taken a step onto the path of god ascension. I only need the ascension tablet at this point."

"That is wonderful, Lene. I am sure sooner rather than later, we will find a God Ascension Tablet for you to use." Kent also set his chopsticks down before adding in a serious tone, "Though I can’t help but wonder if you are open to a new way of ascension."
Lene raised her brow. "Are you talking about the Ancient Path?"
Kent nodded, not surprised Lene already knew of the Ancient Path. After all, all his wives are walking that path, and she has been with them ever since she returned from hell.
It was only normal that she knew about it.

"Big sister Vexthra had already explained how it works to me, and to be frank, I want to take that path. However, Master has to know I have been a god before, and so becoming a god again wouldn’t be too hard for me.

If I pause my ascension and choose to walk the Ancient Path, it wouldn’t be for another thousand years before I can ascend. And as Master said, we have to be ready for what is coming. So the earlier I become a god, the better."
Kent laughed and reached for Lene’s hand. "You are right to think that way, Lene. Becoming a god is indeed the most important thing for you now.
But I think you are forgetting one thing: the fact that the dangers we will face this time are going to be dangerous is all the more reason you should walk the dual path.
Walking the path of the Dao and the Ancient Path will not only allow you to embody the essence of the Dao, but your domain will be absolute."
Kent cast his mind back to when he met Zaila’s past self. Back then, he was put in an illusion that kept him in what looked like a vivid life till the god stage.
The illusion ended with him returning home after the battle he embarked on was over, only to find the dead bodies of his loved ones.

"You know, I was once put in an illusion where I reached godhood. Inside that illusion, I fought beings from the ancient past. Most of them wielded absolute domains, the kind even I struggled to suppress.
These absolute domains are the manifestation of the Dao itself. If I had an absolute domain back then, perhaps my battles would have ended much faster.
That is why I decided to let my wives walk both paths. If they were to face someone like that one day, I want them to be able to match them in every aspect.
So maybe consider that. You will still be a demigod on the Dao path, and as your primordial soul grows, so will your power.
I want you to reach at least the 500th layer of the Dao mountain during your ascension. That would put you among the most powerful gods in the universe."
Lene nodded.
"I guess I was worried for nothing."
She was indeed worried she wouldn’t be there to aid her master against the gods when the need arose. However, hearing his words now, she knew she had worried for nothing.
They resumed their dinner like a couple. However, a few minutes later, Kent sensed a gaze directed at them. Lene also sensed it, but she did not think much of it.
Since the person was merely looking, they said nothing. Their focus remained rooted in their food.
However, although they showed no reaction, the person looking at them frowned. After all, he is an Immortal Emperor, surrounded by three beautiful Immortal Kings.
If anything, he expected them to notice him and react since he made it rather obvious. However, Kent and Lene ignored him completely, almost as if he wasn’t there.
This infuriated him, so he picked up a chopstick and, tapping into his Immortal Emperor strength, flicked it, sending it flying toward Kent’s head.
In his mind, Kent is just a Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator, and Lene is a True Immortal. Suppressing them is as simple as flicking a chopstick.

However, to his shock, the moment the chopstick was half a meter from Kent, Kent turned sideways and flicked a single corn kernel, meeting the chopstick in a silent clash. The two items struggled for a few seconds before both exploded.
Kent finally turned and looked at the brat who chose to start a fight with him despite doing his best to keep a low profile.
The others inside the restaurant turned and looked at the altercation, some quickly pulling out their recording devices.
The dragon smirked and spoke coldly:

"Judging by how polished your armor is and the fact that you have a sword, yet look nothing like a swordsman, tells me you are a greenhouse flower that has been sheathed for who knows how long. It would be in your best interest to save yourself the humiliation by going down on your knees and apologizing to my majestic self."

chapters.title: Chapter 1498: Teaching Him A Lesson
paragraphs: The moment Kent’s words came out, the entire restaurant became quiet. Every last person eating dropped their chopsticks, their jaws hanging open wide.
"Hahahahahahaha..."
Suddenly, the Immortal Emperor, clad in polished armor, laughed, his expression turning slightly amused and a bit angry.

He stood up and walked away from his table, leaving the three Immortal King beauties behind. They didn’t seem a bit scared since, in their eyes, their young master would crush the bug who dared disrespect him.
Everyone came to the same conclusion. They recognised who Kent dared to mess with, and so they knew how this would end.
"You want me to go down on my knees and apologize?" he spoke, taking a step forward.
Kent set down his chopsticks again and wiped his mouth with a napkin before turning toward the annoying bastard.
"I believe my words weren’t ambiguous."

The Immortal Emperor stopped, unsheathed his sword, and pointed it at Kent. At once, a wave of killing intent started emitting from his body, causing those closer to him to take a series of steps back.
The waitresses around moved back, some running to the back room to call the manager.
"Do you know who I am?"
"I don’t know, and I most certainly don’t care. All I ask is for you to go down on your knees and apologize."
"Just who is this kid? Does he even know who he is messing with?"
"I don’t think he has any idea. Just look at him; this is my first time seeing him in this place."
"I am sure he is not from around here. But even if that was why he didn’t know who he was messing with, the fact that he is looking down on an Immortal Emperor shows he has a death wish."
"I am sure. Though I wonder why the lady he is dining with seems rather calm despite her companion courting death."
Attention turned to Lene, who was still eating her food as if her Master wasn’t facing off against an Immortal Emperor.

"Before I kill you for the insult, know that when you are gone, your lady friend will become my servant for the rest of her useless life. You should have known better than to mess with the son of a Demigod."
The sword pointed at Kent vibrated, and a wave of divine sword aura gushed out, forming into a three-meter-long sword.
"Now die."
He stabbed his sword forward, forcing the manifested sword to move toward Kent, causing the very air around it to tremble.
Everyone inside the restaurant knew Kent was done for. Some let out a sigh while others shook their heads. However, when the sword arrived before Kent, all of them widened their eyes in shock.

Just when the sword reached his chest, Kent raised his hand and caught it between his fingers. It felt so effortless that before anyone could make sense of what had happened, the sword came to a stop.
"Not impressed."
Kent muttered.
Then he moved his other hand and used his index finger to gently tap the blade of the sword. It let out a sharp ringing sound, and it vibrated before shattering into fragments.
Many gasped, and the Immortal Emperor took a few steps back, sweat breaking on his brow.
Kent merely smiled and pointed his finger forward.
"I am only a Sword King, but watch carefully and learn how it is done."
Sword aura moved along Kent’s arm toward his finger. Once it reached there, it formed into a thin sword which started to grow bigger the moment sword intent was applied.

At once, everyone inside the restaurant sensed a powerful sensation emanating from the sword. That sensation only grew as the sword increased in size until it was three meters long, just like the one he was attacked with.
By then, even people outside the restaurant sensed an overwhelming amount of sword energy coming from the restaurant.
"Who is that? I have never felt Heavenly Sword Energy that pure before," a few wondered, some even rushing into the restaurant to witness who was unleashing such power.
The Immortal Emperor, however, felt like dropping to his knees at once.
While he had already achieved divine sword energy, the feeling coming from Kent’s Heavenly Sword Energy was so overpowering that he felt so small before him.

"You may be a Sword Divine, but my understanding of the sword is far superior to yours." A smirk formed on his lips as he added, "When I was fighting Divine swordsmen, your great-grandfather wasn’t even a sperm in his great-great-grandfather’s balls.

What makes you think you can measure up to me. Now have a taste, and be sure to remember this sensation." The moment the words left his mouth, Kent flicked his finger, and the sword he had manifested shot forward at a terrifying speed.
The Immortal Emperor crossed his sword over his chest, hoping to block the attack. However, when the sword struck it, he was sent flying, blasting holes through the walls of the restaurant.
Every jaw drop, beads of sweat breaking on their foreheads.

"You could have gone down on your knees and apologised as I demanded," Kent sighed and sat back down. He reached into his space ring and pulled out a pouch containing spirit stones, then set it down on the table.
"That should cover my bill and handle the repairs."
Lene set her chopsticks down and reached for Kent’s hand. Then, under everyone’s stunned gaze, they vanished into thin air.
By the time the Immortal Emperor recovered and entered the restaurant again, Kent was gone, leaving him with a few cracked ribs and torn armour.
His furious scream filled the restaurant and spilt outward.

Kent and Lene appeared 80,000 km away and began heading to the hotel. He could have ignored the Immortal Emperor; however, Kent wanted to create a scene—small enough but impactful—so that word would start to spread about him.
This was his way of drawing Inaya’s attention.
Unbeknownst to him, he had drawn more than Inaya’s attention.

All the way in the Elven Continent, inside an underground space that could easily contain a million people, a young bald elven child who wasn’t a day older than 13 opened his eyes, turned his head sideways, and looked toward the Ice Continent.
This child, while he may appear human and harmless, is actually a sword intent left behind by Lord Genesis during the Divine era.
It was said that after he reached the peak and comprehended sword will, he gained enlightenment that allowed him to glimpse into the next realm beyond the Sword Celestial stage.
This breakthrough gave him a new kind of sword energy that enhanced both his sword intent and aura. A portion of that sword intent was what had recently transformed into a bald child.

After his transformation, he had not moved even an inch. He just sat there all day, his body unmoving. However, today, he moved, and those who were paying close attention even claimed they heard him mutter something.
"Big brother."
Inaya muttered, staring at an Elven Demigod who came to report what had happened to her. "Are you sure that was what he said?"
"Yes, my lady. I have confirmed it from more than a hundred people."
"Thank you. You can leave now." He bowed and left. After he was gone, Inaya turned and looked at her friend, Pill Supreme Ainna.
"Don’t say it."
Inaya smiled and took hold of her friend’s hand. "Cast a divination for me." She reached into her space ring and pulled out a patch of hair. "You can use this."
Ainna sighed, knowing she had no choice but to do as her friend wanted. "You are a lost cause, Inaya."

It felt so effortless that before anyone could make sense of what had happened, the sword came to a stop.
"Not impressed."
Kent muttered.
Then he moved his other hand and used his index finger to gently tap the blade of the sword.
It let out a sharp ringing sound, and it vibrated before shattering into fragments.
Many gasped, and the Immortal Emperor took a few steps back, sweat breaking on his brow.
Kent merely smiled and pointed his finger forward.
"I am only a Sword King, but watch carefully and learn how it is done."
Sword aura moved along Kent’s arm toward his finger.
Once it reached there, it formed into a thin sword which started to grow bigger the moment sword intent was applied.
At once, everyone inside the restaurant sensed a powerful sensation emanating from the sword.
That sensation only grew as the sword increased in size until it was three meters long, just like the one he was attacked with.
By then, even people outside the restaurant sensed an overwhelming amount of sword energy coming from the restaurant.
"Who is that?
I have never felt Heavenly Sword Energy that pure before," a few wondered, some even rushing into the restaurant to witness who was unleashing such power.
The Immortal Emperor, however, felt like dropping to his knees at once.
While he had already achieved divine sword energy, the feeling coming from Kent’s Heavenly Sword Energy was so overpowering that he felt so small before him.

"You may be a Sword Divine, but my understanding of the sword is far superior to yours." A smirk formed on his lips as he added, "When I was fighting Divine swordsmen, your great-grandfather wasn’t even a sperm in his great-great-grandfather’s balls.
What makes you think you can measure up to me.
Now have a taste, and be sure to remember this sensation." The moment the words left his mouth, Kent flicked his finger, and the sword he had manifested shot forward at a terrifying speed.
The Immortal Emperor crossed his sword over his chest, hoping to block the attack.
However, when the sword struck it, he was sent flying, blasting holes through the walls of the restaurant.
Every jaw drop, beads of sweat breaking on their foreheads.
"You could have gone down on your knees and apologised as I demanded," Kent sighed and sat back down.
He reached into his space ring and pulled out a pouch containing spirit stones, then set it down on the table.
"That should cover my bill and handle the repairs."
Lene set her chopsticks down and reached for Kent’s hand.
Then, under everyone’s stunned gaze, they vanished into thin air.
By the time the Immortal Emperor recovered and entered the restaurant again, Kent was gone, leaving him with a few cracked ribs and torn armour.
His furious scream filled the restaurant and spilt outward.
Kent and Lene appeared 80,000 km away and began heading to the hotel.
He could have ignored the Immortal Emperor; however, Kent wanted to create a scene—small enough but impactful—so that word would start to spread about him.
This was his way of drawing Inaya’s attention.
Unbeknownst to him, he had drawn more than Inaya’s attention.

All the way in the Elven Continent, inside an underground space that could easily contain a million people, a young bald elven child who wasn’t a day older than 13 opened his eyes, turned his head sideways, and looked toward the Ice Continent.
This child, while he may appear human and harmless, is actually a sword intent left behind by Lord Genesis during the Divine era.
It was said that after he reached the peak and comprehended sword will, he gained enlightenment that allowed him to glimpse into the next realm beyond the Sword Celestial stage.
This breakthrough gave him a new kind of sword energy that enhanced both his sword intent and aura.
A portion of that sword intent was what had recently transformed into a bald child.
After his transformation, he had not moved even an inch.
He just sat there all day, his body unmoving.
However, today, he moved, and those who were paying close attention even claimed they heard him mutter something.
"Big brother."
Inaya muttered, staring at an Elven Demigod who came to report what had happened to her.
"Are you sure that was what he said?"
"Yes, my lady.
I have confirmed it from more than a hundred people."
"Thank you.
You can leave now." He bowed and left.
After he was gone, Inaya turned and looked at her friend, Pill Supreme Ainna.
"Don’t say it."
Inaya smiled and took hold of her friend’s hand.
"Cast a divination for me." She reached into her space ring and pulled out a patch of hair.
"You can use this."
Ainna sighed, knowing she had no choice but to do as her friend wanted.
"You are a lost cause, Inaya."

chapters.title: Chapter 1499: The Divination
paragraphs: Aside from being an accomplished alchemist, Ainna is also proficient in the art of divination. In fact, her dream of becoming an alchemist started during the era of Pill Celestial Kevi Sage, the smartest man to ever live.
Inaya knew that all too well, and so she asked for her help.
"What at all do you see in him, Inaya?" Ainna asked, clearly annoyed that, at every turn, her friend seemed to drag her into Jest-related issues.
Inaya smiled and replied, "You wouldn’t understand even if I told you."
"Try me."

Ainna had known Inaya for years. She knew the kind of person she was at heart, and so she knew that when it came to matters related to Jest, she tended to be a bit stupid. Despite the brat hurting her terribly the last time, she still hung on to him.
This baffled her, and so despite years passing, whenever she heard Inaya speak about Jest—something she did almost every day—she always got annoyed.
"When you meet him, I am sure you will understand." A blush appeared on her cheek. "Jest is the kind of person you would hate at first sight, but would come to love over time."
"What an idiot," Ainna muttered, and then she sighed.

After sitting there for a few minutes, she retrieved an artifact from her space ring and set it down. Then she grabbed the hair that Inaya retrieved from her space ring with an annoyed look on her face.
Clearly, it belongs to Jest.
"Stupid."
Inaya smiled, knowing her friend had every right to insult her.
"It will take three days, so don’t disturb me," Ainna said before closing her eyes. Inaya nodded to her words and started waiting.

In her mind, if indeed Jest is back and he is on Planet Brymrr now, she would go to him and give him a piece of her mind. She had a lot to tell him, and as she sat there, looking at her friend do her thing, she could only hope she succeeded.
[Ainna’s POV]
While Inaya was waiting for her to finish the divination, Ainna was fighting an internal battle. In her mind and heart, she hated Jest for what he did to her friend.
When she found Inaya, she was broken and on the verge of death. This sight broke her so much that after spending hundreds of thousands of years fixing her, she vowed to make the brat pay.
By then, Jest had reached a level where she couldn’t touch him. Even so, she cursed him a few times, hoping he would suffer before dying.

Thankfully, after Jest died during the Divine War, she managed to find peace in her heart. Now, the same brat had resurfaced, and while she wished with every part of her being that all of this shouldn’t be the case, a part of her knew the brat was indeed back.
Now, she was tasked with finding him, something she knew she could easily do. The only reason she asked for three days was to see if she could deceive her friend.
However, using her divine sense to look at Inaya fidgeting with her fingers like a kid, she knew doing so to her would be bad.
’Curse you, Jest. If you are indeed back, then I will look for you and make sure I send you falling into the deepest, darkest hole.’

She remained seated for two and a half days, just cursing the brat. Eventually, she decided to cast the divination spell. Immediately the spell was cast, her consciousness was pulled away, appearing in front of a beautiful tower.
The tower stood in a pink flower field, one filled with the scent of love. The field was vast and so beautiful that the moment Ainna appeared there, she felt her restless heart calm down.

The tower was tall and segmented like a pagoda. There were 13 segments, each with a unique design. The first segment had a dragon tattoo before it. The second had a sword, while the third had crossed daggers.
At every segment, a different color was emitted from the windows. This made Ainna wonder what this place was. However, because of how beautiful the place was, she didn’t speak for a few minutes.
Eventually, she spoke:
"Where am I?" she muttered, looking around her.
"Welcome to the divine space of my master. My name is Tower." A beautiful loli with golden hair and a pair of glassy eyes appeared from thin air and spoke, giving Ainna a fright.
"Who are you?" Ainna asked, causing the loli to sigh.
"I clearly just said my name is Tower. Are you deaf?"
Ainna narrowed her eyes. "Tower. What kind of stupid name is that?"

Tower also narrowed her eyes. Clearly, both ladies didn’t like each other’s tone. Thankfully, Ainna saw Tower as a child, so she chose to be the bigger person. Unbeknownst to her, Tower is several billion years older than her.
"Why am I here?"
"What were you up to before you ended up here?" Tower asked, crossing her tiny arms across her chest.
"I was performing a divination on a certain jackass."
"Does this jackass happen to be called Jest?"
Ainna narrowed her eyes again. "How did you know that?"

Tower turned and looked toward the second segment of the tower. "The one you are looking for is in the second segment. But before I let you go, tell me one thing: what do you want with him? I can tell you clearly hate him, so why are you divining his fate?"
"It is a favour for a friend who can’t just let go. That said, I want to break every bone in his body, so there is that. Can I go now?"

Tower smiled and pointed at the second segment, causing stairs to form. "Let me warn you, though. For choosing to divine someone that important, you will have to pay a price. I cannot say what the price will be, but I am certain it will make you wish you had never performed divination on him."
Tower waved her hand, and Ainna was pulled up the stairs. Before she could turn and say anything, the door to the second segment opened, and she was pulled inside.
Instantly, her consciousness traveled through space and time in the blink of an eye before she appeared in a place she hadn’t been for billions of years.
Her consciousness was drawn to a certain hotel, where, in one room, a certain handsome man with purple hair, with strands of gold and red, lay on the bed, his dick buried in the throat of a demigod.
When she appeared, Kent turned to face her, causing her heartbeat to rise. She thought she was discovered, which would have been awkward.
Thankfully, after a few seconds, Lene pulled her head back and asked, "Everything alright, Master?"
"Yes, Lene. I thought I had sensed a presence, but it was a false alarm." Kent replied, ran his hand through her hair, and asked, "Are you satisfied yet?"
"No, Master. Not yet."
Kent laughed and said, "You know, when it is just the two of us, you can call me Kent."
Lene smiled and held onto him. "No. Kent Madson is for everyone else. I prefer Master. It makes me feel special."
"Fine. Just don’t make it your kink and start dressing like a maid." They both laughed.
Meanwhile, after several minutes, Ainna woke up in her body back in the Elven continent, her cheeks red.
"I-I found him."

chapters.title: Chapter 1500: Tracking Him Down
paragraphs: "Ainna, why are you blushing?"
Inaya asked, a bit stunned, looking at her friend, who hid her red cheeks away from her. She had known her for billions of years, and all this time, she had not seen her blush, not even once.
Ainna is the type of lady who has no affection for anyone aside from her craft.
During the Era of the legendary Pill Celestial Kevin Sage, she was just starting out as an alchemist. Back then, her inspiration was Kevin Sage, a man known as the wisest man in the universe.
She was so obsessed with him that she followed in his footsteps, embracing the craft with an open mindset and the confidence to try something new.
One time, she actually met Kevin Sage. But while many blushed and asked for his autograph, she faced him with several questions, her focus fixed on what she had come for.
Inaya herself saw the will her friend carried and knew that nothing romantic would ever stand in the way of her achieving her goal.
Her blushing today was the last thing she expected.

"What did you see?" Seeing that she was not answering her first question, she asked a different one. She had already said she had found Jest, so she wanted to know what she saw that made her blush that profusely.

Ainna said nothing for a few minutes, replaying the sight she saw over and over again. She willed herself to stop thinking about it, but no matter how hard she tried, the sight of Lene sucking Kent’s dick kept replaying in her mind.
After 15 minutes, she managed to push it to the back of her mind.
She then turned and looked at her friend.

"I found him, and as you said, he is indeed in this world. In fact, you may have long guessed it. That scumbag is indeed Kent Madson. He has reincarnated, I suspect, since he is now a Heavenly Ascension stage cultivator and a dragon."
Inaya said nothing for a few minutes, then a smile appeared on her face.

"Where is he currently?" she asked. Ainna, who felt like she had jumped the gun, considering Inaya was now focused on Kent more than the fact that a few minutes ago she was blushing, was quick to answer,
"He is currently living in a hotel in Snow City." She formed a hand seal, and a mark appeared. "I suspect he would be in disguise, so I left my mark on him. This will help you locate him."

"Huh, aren’t you coming with me?" Inaya asked, seeing that her friend, who a few days ago had bragged about how she would torture Jest when she got her hands on him, had given away the one thing she could use to find him.
That is not like her. Naturally, this action made her mind go back to her first question. This was not like Ainna, and Inaya could see that.

"I-I am afraid that if I get close to him, I might just end up killing him. So you can go alone. I will sit this one out." She flashed a fake smile and added, "Plus, I have to prepare for my Pill conference. Concocting a Supreme Pill is not as simple as swinging a sword,"
Inaya locked her gaze on her for a few more seconds before she grabbed her hand. "Nope. You are coming with me. Using alchemy as an excuse was your mistake, Ainna.

I have lived a very long life, so I know that aside from Pill Celestial Kevin Sage, those monsters at the Pill Council, and the 13 Disciples, there is no one below the Pill Celestial stage who can measure up to you.
You have long prepared for this Pill Conference, so don’t bullshit me. You are coming, and there is nothing you can do to avoid that."

Ainna smiled. "Thanks for the compliment, but don’t say those words in public, or else you might lose your head to a cauldron smash. While your lazy bum was asleep, many legendary alchemists appeared.
That said, I really don’t want to come. I might end up actually killing him."
Inaya stood up and retrieved a pill from her space ring. Ainna smiled when she saw the pill. It was the appearance-altering pill she invented when she reached the Pill God stage.
"You said it yourself. Jest is now Kent Madson. The last time I checked, his name appeared on the Pill Dao Tablet, something you have been struggling to achieve for over a billion years already.
Since that is the case, why don’t you get close and see what kind of person he is now? I know I want to see what that scumbag turns out to be in this life.
I have waited a very long time for this reunion." She tossed the pill into her mouth, and at once, her appearance changed, turning from a beautiful elf into a red-haired Flame Human.
Her Peak God stage aura also slowly changed, taking on the form of an Immortal Lord. At once, she went from a drop-dead red-haired elf to a drop-dead red-haired Flame Human.
Aside from the hair, she looked nothing like the Inaya Jest knew.
"Your turn," Inaya said, extending one more appearance-altering pill to her friend. Ainna sighed and knew that no matter what, she would have to listen to her friend and take the pill.
Inaya would drag her if she had to, so going on her own accord, even if she was pressured, sounded like a good plan.
"Don’t get heartbroken if I go overboard and he ends up dead,"
"You can try, but you won’t succeed."
Ainna scoffed and swallowed the pill. At once, she turned into a beautiful, purple-haired Ice Human. Considering her hair color was purple, her ice aura also came out purple.
This appearance-altering pill does more than alter one’s appearance. It transforms them into different people, granting them the abilities they desired before swallowing the pill.
It was one of her many creations that made her famous in the world of alchemy.

"Let’s go then." She activated a formation around her mansion. Inaya smiled and grabbed her hand. They walked out, and after they were free of the formation, she pointed her finger forward, causing Supreme Sword Aura to form into a tiny sword on her finger.
After it fully formed, she pinched the space in front of them, and it cracked. Soon, the crack spread, and before long, it became undone.
A reddish portal opened, releasing a powerful spatial energy.
"Unbelievable, you actually mastered space law to this extent."
Inaya smiled. "That is what happens when you are stuck at the God stage and run out of hobbies."

Ainna just chuckled and allowed herself to be pulled into the portal. Instead of using the void to travel, which, considering the distance between them and Snow City, would take them at least a week, Inaya chose to use space law.
Thirty-four hours later, they arrived in Snow City, appearing 3000 km away from the city walls. They flew the rest of the way, and a few hours later, they found themselves in the city.
Ainna took Inaya to the hotel she saw in her divination. Since she could still feel that Kent was there, it was only logical that they stay close to him.
A day after they arrived, Kent finally came out, followed by three ladies.
